☆ Olivier nominee for Best New Play and Best New Director ☆

Smart. Scrappy. Savage. 1536, the “electrifying” (The Standard) historical drama with a modern edge, transfers to the Ambassadors Theatre in London’s West End following a sold-out run at the Almeida Theatre – don’t miss your chance to see this “effortlessly funny, bold and ballsy” (The Guardian) must-see new play.

Written by Ava Pickett, winner of the 2024 Susan Smith Blackburn Prize, directed by Lyndsey Turner (Chimerica) with Liv Hill (Three Girls), Siena Kelly (Black Mirror) and Tanya Reynolds (Sex Education) reprising their original roles, this “razor-sharp, darkly comic and blisteringly relevant” (The Independent) new play explores the dynamics of female friendship in a world stacked against women. Joining them are Oliver Johnstone as Richard (Retrograde; All My Sons) and George Kemp as William (High Noon; Who’s Afraid Of Virginia Woolf?).

Playing for a strictly limited run at the Ambassadors Theatre with previews from 2 May 2026. Don’t miss your chance to experience this “wonderfully vibrant, cracking debut” (The Guardian).

Book your 1536 theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

Read More for show synopsis, cast & creative, age guidance and more…

What is 1536 about?

Kings don’t kill their wives, right?

Tudor England.

A field in Essex.

Three women hurry to their childhood meeting place, thirsty for gossip from London.

Word spreads of a clash between King Henry VIII and his Queen, Anne Boleyn. And closer to home, another rumour begins to catch fire.

As these women begin to see echoes of the royal drama in their own rural lives and a rise in violence spreads throughout the land, the actions of a queen imprisoned in a tower threaten to cost them everything.

Ticket Information

Tickets available for performances from 2 May – 1 Aug 2026

Show Information

Age Guidance: Key Stage 4 and above.

Content Warnings: This production includes strong language, depictions of violence, sexual assault, discussion of miscarriage, rape, domestic violence, traumatic childbirth. the use of blood, flashing lights and haze.

Running Time

Cast & Creatives

Ava Pickett (Writer), Lyndsey Turner (Director)

Liv Hill (Jane), Sienna Kelly (Anna), Tanya Reynolds (Mariella), Oliver Johnstone (Richard), George Kemp (William).

shows.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream

sources.title_as_listed: A Midsummer Night’s Dream - Globe Theatre

shows.description:
A Midsummer Night’s Dream returns to the Globe Theatre, in the heart of London’s Bankside. Step into a world where lovers chase desires through a moonlit forest and playful spirits stir magical mischief under open skies. The play’s rich tapestry of love stories, supernatural mischief and meta‑theatrical humour makes Dream one of Shakespeare’s most widely performed works, and this new staging embraces the theatre’s iconic open‑air design and communal spirit, inviting audiences into a shared experience of mischief and wonder. Secure your tickets today!

Amid moonlit woods just beyond the city, love’s logic unravels, identities shift, and magic reigns. With a sprinkling of fairy dust, a wild web of stories is woven together: the impending wedding of Theseus and Hippolyta, the romantic entanglements of four young Athenians, a band of amateur players rehearsing a rustic play, and the capricious antics of a fairy host led by Oberon and his sprite, Puck.

In this forest, desire is both unpredictable and irresistible. The edge between dream and waking life blurs, and laughter springs from both chaos and connection. So let yourself be spellbound, and who knows who you’ll be by morning…

A Midsummer Night’s Dream is one of William Shakespeare’s most celebrated and enduring comedies, believed to have been written between 1595 and 1596. Scholars suggest it may have been composed for a noble wedding celebration, possibly that of Elizabeth Carey, a member of Queen Elizabeth I’s court. Its intricate structure, poetic language, and fantastical themes mark it as one of Shakespeare’s most imaginative works.

A Midsummer Night’s Dream was first published in quarto in 1600, with a more reliable version included in the 1623 First Folio. It became a popular choice for performances during Shakespeare’s lifetime and has remained a staple of theatrical repertoire ever since. The play’s popularity surged in the 19th century with spectacular Victorian productions that emphasised its fairy-tale elements.

Over the centuries, it has inspired numerous adaptations in opera, ballet, film, and contemporary theatre. From Benjamin Britten’s 1960 opera to the modern screen adaptations by directors like Michael Hoffman in 1999 and Julie Taymor in 2014, A Midsummer Night’s Dream continues to captivate audiences with its dreamlike blend of romance, comedy, and magic.

Casting for this production includes:

A Midsummer Night’s Dream is written by William Shakespeare. Emily Lim ( The Odyssey, Brighter Still ) directs, with set design by Aldo Vázquez ( Romeo and Juliet ), and costume design by Fly Davis ( Othello ). Music and composition are by Jim Fortune, whose credits include Pericles and A Christmas Carol .

Step into the forest and experience a sunlit summer dream where love’s enchantments dance beneath open skies, and laughter mingles with poetry. Illusion, desire and transformation meet in Shakespeare’s best-known comedy returning to the Globe this summer season in an exciting new production that emphasises the community spirit of the play. So don’t be a fool, mortal - secure your tickets for A Midsummer Night’s Dream at Shakespeare’s Globe today.

shows.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream

sources.title_as_listed: A Midsummer Night’s Dream (Regent’s Park Open Air)

shows.description:
Prepare to be enchanted as A Midsummer Night’s Dream comes to the Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, in the heart of glorious Regent’s Park, this summer. Shakespeare’s most beloved comedy, about the tangled love triangle between four mortals, complicated by the interference of mischievous fairies, comes alive in a gorgeous outdoor staging. Blending hilarity, folk‑infused music, and the natural beauty of London’s iconic parkland, A Midsummer Night’s Dream is a play that truly casts a spell - secure your tickets today.

A Midsummer Night’s Dream is a riotous tale of love, transformation, and magic that unfolds in an enchanted forest where anything can, and will, happen. Four young Athenians flee into the woods to escape social constraints, only to find themselves at the mercy of mischievous fairies and errant love potions. At the same time, the fairy king and queen are dealing with romantic troubles of their own, while a band of rustic actors rehearse a hilariously earnest play in a delightful metatheatrical twist. This new Regent’s Park production infuses Shakespeare’s classic comedy with folk‑inspired melodies; the open‑air setting amplifies the play’s themes of nature, illusion, and the joyfully unpredictable experience of falling in and out of love.

Since its first recorded performance in the late 16th century, A Midsummer Night’s Dream has been one of Shakespeare’s most frequently staged and visually expressive plays. Scholars believe it was written around 1595–1596, likely to be performed at a court wedding. Early stagings would have used minimal scenery, relying on the language and movement to evoke the magical forest setting.

A Midsummer Night’s Dream has long been associated with open‑air performance, its forested spell perfectly matched to the natural world. This production leans into that tradition, with live music, laughter, moonlight, and merry enchantment under the open sky.

Casting for this production includes:

The 2026 production of A Midsummer Night’s Dream at Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre is directed by Atri Banerjee ( The Glass Menagerie, Julius Caesar ). Original music is composed by Maimuna Memon ( Portia Coughlan, The Grapes of Wrath ).

Naomi Dawson ( Romeo and Juliet, Look Back in Anger ) is the set designer, with costume design by Tómas Palmer ( Run Sister Run, Gruesome Playground Injuries ). Lighting design is by Joshua Pharo ( Kenrex, Noughts and Croses ), with sound design by Max Pappenheim ( Twelfth Night, A Raisin in the Sun ) and movement direction by Anjali Mehra ( Jesus Christ Superstar, Marriage Material ).

If you’ve ever dreamed of Shakespeare where the rustle of leaves becomes part of the soundscape and moonlight co‑stars with the players, this summer’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream promises precisely that. Let Shakespeare’s raucous comedy wash through you beneath the stars - book your tickets for A Midsummer Night’s Dream at the Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre today

shows.title: Abigail's Party
shows.description:
Cheesy-pineapple, anyone? Nadia Fall’s production of Abigail’s Party , starring Tamsin Outhwaite, returns to London following a sell-out run in 2024. This darkly hilarious play, about a party in 1970s Essex that turns from stilted to chaotic, finishes its UK tour at the Harold Pinter Theatre, in the heart of the West End, for a strictly limited run. Don’t miss this vibrant and “gaspingly, immortally funny” (TimeOut) new production of the Mike Leigh classic - secure your tickets today.

In 1970s Essex, married couple Beverley and Laurence host a party for their new neighbours, nurse Angela and ex-footy player Tony, alongside their longstanding friend, the anxious and mousey Susan, who is escaping from her own home, where her boisterous fifteen-year-old daughter Abigail is hosting a party of her own. What begins with nibbles, music, and an awkward merging of old and new neighbours soon devolves into booze-fuelled bickering, extra-marital flirtations, and ultimately takes a darkly unexpected turn…

Abigail’s Party was originally devised and directed by Mike Leigh, with the original cast, which included Alison Steadman as Beverley and John Salthouse as Tony, extensively developing their characters' backgrounds and contributing to the production. The play premiered at the Hampstead Theatre in 1977 and was recorded and Broadcast as a BBC Play for Today later the same year. With its enduring themes of class, aspirationalism and romantic dissatisfaction, Abigail's Party remains exceedingly popular and has been revived many times over the decades. This production was first staged at the Theatre Royal Stratford East in 2024, and embarks on a UK tour before coming to the Harold Pinter Theatre for a strictly limited run.

Tamzin Outhwaite reprises her role as Beverley from the 2024 production. Perhaps best known for her role as Mel Owen in EastEnders, Outhwaite’s other credits include Red Cap, New Tricks and Inside No 9 as well as stage roles in The Haunting of Alice Bowles and Alan Ayckbourn's How the Other Half Loves .

Abigail’s Party was created by Mike Leigh. Leigh is a screenwriter, producer, and director, best known for his improvisational, hyperrealist films. Leigh is a BAFTA winner and Academy Award nominee. His credits include films Secrets and Lies, Happy-Go-Lucky, Vera Drake and Another Year , and stage plays Greek Tragedy, Smelling A Rat , and It's a Great Big Shame .

Nadia Fall directs. Fall is a playwright, director and the artistic director and joint-chief executive of the Young Vic Theatre. Her credits include Equus , the Olivier-winning opera Noye's Fludde with Lenny Henry, Chewing Gum Dreams with Michaela Coel and Inua Ellams’ adaptation of Three Sisters .

This smash hit revival of Mike Leigh’s sharp suburban satire returns to London following a sell-out run in 2024. Starring Tamzin Outhwaite and directed by Young Vic Artistic Director Nadia Fall, Abigail's Party is “a perfect cocktail of sharp wit, social tension, and barbed comedy” (West End Best Friend). Don’t miss it - book tickets for Abigail’s Party at the Harold Pinter Theatre today.

shows.title: Adriana Mater
shows.description:
Blistering opera Adriana Mater comes to London this winter in a brand new, specially commissioned translation for the English National Opera. This powerful, rarely staged opera about a young woman raising a son in the brutality of war is by acclaimed Finnish composer Kaija Saariaho and comes to the London Coliseum, in the heart of Leicester Square, for a strictly limited season.

During a brutal civil war in an unnamed country, a young woman, Adriana, falls pregnant after being violently assaulted by a soldier, Tsargo. Against the advice of her sister, Refka, Adriana chooses to keep the child, whom she names Yonas, concealing the truth of his origins from her son. Raised to believe in love and hope, the optimistic young man later learns the real story of how he was conceived, and is compelled to seek revenge. Can Adriana convince Yonas that true strength lies in mercy, or will he be consumed by the inherited cycle of male violence?

Picking up where the renowned opera Tosca leaves off, Adriana Mater contributes to a bold narrative season at the ENO, centring stories of resistance, resilience, freedom and hope. The opera can be watched as a stand-alone story or paired as a double bill with Tosca .

Adriana Mater premiered at the Opéra Bastille in Paris in 2006, directed by Peter Sellars. The opera later debuted in Finland in 2008, and also received premieres in the UK in a concert performance and in the US later that same year.

Adriana Mater is written by award-winning, long-term collaborators, late Finnish composer Kaija Saariaho and French writer Amin Maalouf. Music is by Saariaho ( Innocence, L'Amour de loin ), with a libretto by Maalouf ( La Passion de Simone, Emilie ). The English translation is by Saariaho’s son, Grammy winner Aleksi Barriere ( True Fire, Innocence ).

ENO Music Director Designate Andre de Ridder ( Only the Sound Remains, Drei Frauen ) conducts, with direction by Annilese Miskimmon ( Madama Butterfly, I Puritani ), with the production marking the pair's first creative collaboration.

Don’t miss this rarely staged gem of an opera by one of the most influential voices in contemporary classical music, starring ENO favourites and acclaimed singers making their Coliseum debut. Book for Adriana Mater at the London Coliseum today.

shows.title: Allegra
shows.description:
Hailed as a “quirky comedy bursting with joy” (Theatre South East), Dame Maureen Lipman returns to the West End stage this summer in a limited run of Peter Quilter’s fresh, new heartwarming comedy, Allegra . Playing at the Harold Pinter Theatre, located near Trafalgar Square, join Allegra , whose joyful impulse to sing everywhere she goes brings both delight and chaos to the people around her. Secure your tickets for the show’s West End debut today!

The comedy introduces us to Allegra , a woman who has a real zest for life and carries an irresistible urge to sing. Wherever she goes, whether she’s at home, in the streets or even at the local shops and cafes, this joy spills unapologetically into the real world and impacts those around her. Whilst her devoted brother Ronan and her carer Anna do their best to keep life steady for Allegra , they also try to protect her without dimming the light that makes her who she is.

Allegra is penned by the Olivier and Tony Award-nominated playwright, Peter Quilter, whose credits include End of the Rainbow and Glorious! . The show made its debut at Wycombe Swan Theatre as part of a limited UK tour. Now Allegra heads to the West End’s Harold Pinter Theatre.

With a career spanning over five decades, Dame Maureen Lipman is one of the country’s most beloved actresses. She has an expansive career in theatre, film and TV with credits including Oklahoma , Carry On Colombus! , See How They Run and Plebs .

Bailey Patrick ( The Country Girls, Our Country’s Good ) plays the role of Officer Rogers. John Middleton ( ITV’s Emmerdale, Strangers on a Train ) plays the role of Ronan, with Elizabeth Bower ( Midsomer Murders, The Importance of Being Earnest ) completing the cast as Anna.

Allegra is directed and choreographed by Stephen Mear. A three-time Olivier Award winner, his credits include Mary Poppins the Musical , Funny Girl and La Cage Aux Folles .

The creative team also includes set and costume designer Justin Williams, lighting designer Samuel Biondolillo, sound designer Russell Ditchfield, video designer Ben Bull for Big Tele, production management by Setting Line, general management and tour booking by Thomas Hopkins Productions, and casting director Rob Kelly.

Allegra at Harold Pinter Theatre promises a tender and life-affirming story about family, love and holding on to joy for as long as possible. Secure your tickets for this limited summer season in the West End and discover a comedy which will “turn our current face of gloom into an upturned grin of happiness” (Maureen Lipman)!

shows.title: An Ideal Husband
shows.description:
This vibrant new production of Oscar Wilde’s enduring and hilarious play, An Ideal Husband , comes to the Lyric Hammersmith in West London. This comedic melodrama about reputation and blackmail is as relevant as ever, and this brand new production by Lyric Associate Nicholai La Barrie showcases Wilde’s witty word-play and exploration of the dark underbelly of politics and public personas in a bold new staging. Secure your tickets today!

“Questions are never indiscreet. Answers sometimes are.”

Politician Sir Robert Chiltern is on the rise. A man of impeccable taste, he appears to have it all - a loving wife, magnificent clothes, a wonderful house and most importantly, a spotless reputation. That is, until the meddling Lady Cheverley enters the scene. An old school rival of Robert’s wife, and the widow of one of Robert’s old colleagues, Lady Cheverley has a long-held grudge, a flair for the dramatic and a whole load of secrets ready to spill. With the threat of scandal on the horizon, just how far will Robert go to keep his reputation unblemished?

An Ideal Husband first premiered in 1895 at the Theatre Royal Haymarket. The show was critically acclaimed and continues to be popular today. It has since received many revivals and adaptations, with notable productions including the 2018 Vaudeville Theatre staging starring Father-son duo Edward and Freddie Fox, and the 1999 film adaptation starring Julianne Moore, Cate Blanchett and Rupert Everett.

Casting for An Ideal Husband includes:

The Lyric’s Associate Director Nicholai La Barrie directs. La Barrie is a British writer, actor and director. Previously, La Barrie was a MOBO fellow and a resident director on Tina - The Tina Turner Musical . His credits include Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) in the West End, Romeo and Juliet at the Royal Exchange, Manchester, and God of Carnage at the Lyric Hammersmith.

An Ideal Husband is written by Oscar Wilde (1854 -1900). Wilde was an Irish author, poet, and playwright, often regarded as a key figure in the aestheticism movement. Wilde is widely considered to be one of the most well-known and greatest writers of the Victorian Era, best known for his witty word-play and satirical epigrams. Wilde’s most famous works include his plays The Importance of Being Earnest, Salome, Lady Windermere's Fan and A Woman of No Importance , and his Gothic horror novel The Picture of Dorian Gray .

Corruption, blackmail and societal expectations collide in this exhilarating new staging of one of Wilde’s wittiest and most beloved plays. Don’t miss this fresh new take on the classic comedy of manners from one of London’s hottest up-and-coming directors. Secure your tickets for An Ideal Husband at the Lyric Hammersmith today!

shows.title: Arcadia
shows.description:
Immerse yourself in the extraordinary, where brilliant ideas and burning hearts fuse, in Arcadia , coming to the West End this summer. This revival of Tom Stoppard’s seminal play takes place at the Duke of York's theatre, just a short walk from the Trafalgar Theatre. Directed by acclaimed British director Carrie Cracknell, Arcadia “pits the classical against the romantic, science against poetry, the past against the present” (Guardian). You won't want to miss this breathtaking new staging for a limited time; secure your tickets today.

Set in a country house in Derbyshire, Arcadia follows two intertwined storylines across time. In the early 19th century, a teenage prodigy named Thomasina Coverly discovers mathematical truths about chaos and thermodynamics, while the adults around her - tutors, guests, and the household - attempt to discipline her passion with reason. Meanwhile, in the 1990s, scholars descend on the same estate, chasing the ghosts of that earlier era, seeking proof, revelation - and perhaps each other.

Pulsing with themes of order and disorder, the irreversible flow of time, the intersection of intellect and emotion, poetry and physics, Arcadia is brilliant, funny and deeply moving. Making its West End premiere after its initial staging at The Old Vic, the in‑the‑round staging of this revival heightens the play’s sense of immersion and immediacy.

Arcadia premiered at the National Theatre Lyttelton stage in London on 13 April 1993, directed by Trevor Nunn. The play received widespread critical acclaim upon its premiere and went on to win the Laurence Olivier Award for Best New Play. Arcadia later received its first Broadway transfer at the Lincoln Centre Theatre in New York in 1995, and has been revived several times, including a major 2009 production at the Duke of York’s Theatre in London and a 2011 Broadway revival. This new revival at the Duke of York’s Theatre is a result of a triumphant debut at The Old Vic at the start of 2026.

Arcadia is widely regarded as one of the most significant plays of the 20th Century, and in 2006, the Royal Institution recognised the play as one of the greatest science-related literary works ever written. This honour reflects the play’s extraordinary ability to weave complex scientific concepts - such as thermodynamics, chaos theory and fractals - into a compelling, emotionally resonant narrative.

“A truly marvellous play, full of wit, wisdom and a rare warmth” (WhatsOnStage), “A stellar, lust-filled revival” (The Independent): critics were transformed by Arcadia at The Old Vic. Now that the West End transfer has been announced, more people will be able to witness a pulsating relationship between past and present unfold on the big stage this summer.

Casting for this production is to be announced.

Carrie Cracknell directs the production. Cracknell became the youngest artistic director of a professional UK theatre when she co-led the Gate Theatre from 2007 to 2012. Her acclaimed work includes A Doll’s House at the Young Vic and West End, Medea and Julie both at the National Theatre, and the Netflix film Persuasion .

Arcadia is written by Tom Stoppard. Tom Stoppard is a Czech-born British playwright and screenwriter, widely regarded as one of the most influential dramatists of his generation. His major stage credits include Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead , The Real Thing , The Invention of Love , Rock ’n’ Roll and Leopoldstadt . Stoppard has received numerous prestigious awards, including four Tony Awards for Best Play and an Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay for Shakespeare in Love . He was knighted in 1997 for his services to drama.

This landmark revival of acclaimed playwright Tom Stoppard’s most critically acclaimed work comes to London for a strictly limited run, directed by one of the UK's hottest young directors. Arcadia is where minds meet, loves blaze, and time unwinds and a “dazzling meditation on our endless search for understanding” (What’s on Stage). This production promises to be unmissable – book your ticket for Arcadia at the Duke of York’s Theatre today.

shows.title: Avenue Q
shows.description:
Come home to Avenue Q as the Tony-winning, boundary-pushing musical returns to London’s West End this Spring. This raunchy, raucous musical is “Sesame Street for grown-ups” (Entertainment Weekly) and tells the story of bunch of dissatisfied friends, both puppet and human, who live together in the titular borough of NYC. Avenue Q is an equal opportunity offender - with love, sexuality, and privilege all in the firing line. The musical comes to the Shaftesbury Theatre, in the heart of Covent Garden, for the first time in over two decades - you won’t want to miss it, read our Avenue Q review and secure your tickets today!

Set in a shabby outer borough of New York City, Avenue Q is a raucously funny and surprisingly heartfelt coming-of-age musical where humans and puppets live side by side. The story follows Princeton, a bright-eyed (puppet) college graduate who moves into Avenue Q with big dreams and a tiny bank account. As he tries to figure out his purpose in life, he meets a host of colourful neighbours, including Kate Monster, an earnest teaching assistant; Rod, a closeted banker and Nicky, his slacker roommate; landlord and former child-star Gary Oldman (yes, the Gary Oldman) and Trekkie Monster, who’s definitely not your average children’s puppet!

As the characters navigate adulthood, love, friendship, and disappointment, Avenue Q balances outrageous humour with relatable moments. From job-hunting to heartbreak, it captures the awkward hilarity of trying to grow up when you’re not quite sure how. With songs like “It Sucks to Be Me”, “There’s a Fine Fine Line”, “Schadenfreude”, “If You Were Gay”, and “Everyone’s a Little Bit Racist,” the show isn’t afraid to tackle taboo topics with tongue firmly in cheek.

Avenue Q premiered off-Broadway in 2003, winning a Lucille Lortel and Outer Critics Circle award, before transferring to the John Golden Theatre on Broadway later that same year. The musical went on to win three Tony awards in 2004, including the award for Best Musical, which the edgy, underdog production controversially won over the smash-hit Wicked. The musical ran until 2009 on Broadway, when it transferred back off-Broadway and ran for a further ten years. The show has since toured internationally and across the United States. In 2006, Avenue Q premiered in the West End and ran for five years at various different venues. While an anniversary concert was held in 2024 to celebrate the show’s 18th anniversary, this brand new revival marks the first full run of the show in London in almost two decades.

Casting includes:

Avenue Q has music and lyrics by Robert Lopez and Jeff Marx, with a book by Jeff Whitty.

Lopez and Marx are long-term collaborators who have worked together on the music and lyrics for the musical Book of Mormon , the musical episode of Scrubs , the songs for Disney films Frozen 1 and Frozen 2 as well as music for Bear in the Big Blue House and The Book of Pooh .

Lopez is an American songwriter and playwright. He is one of only 27 people in the world to hold an EGOT, meaning he has won an Emmy, Tony, Oscar and Grammy. Lopez is the youngest person to have won an EGOT, as well as the only person to have won all four awards more than once. As well as his collaborations with Marx, his credits include work on Disney’s Coco , South Park and Marvel series’ WandaVision and Agatha All Along .

Jeff Marx is an American composer and lyricist. Aside from his collaborations with Lopez, his credits include Rick & Steve: The Happiest Gay Couple in All the World, Home Street Home and How To Win A High School Election .

Whitty is an American playwright, actor, and screenwriter. He is a Tony, Independent Spirit and Writers Guild of America Award winner, and an Academy Award and BAFTA nominee. His credits include the Libretto for Bring it On the Musical , The Further Adventures of Hedda Gabler , and Oscar-nominated film Can You Ever Forgive Me?.

All your fantasies can come true with Avenue Q ! This outrageous, hilarious, “savvy, sassy and eminently likeable” (The New Yorker) musical returns to the West End for the first time in almost two decades. Book your tickets for Avenue Q today and check out this memorable musical for yourself at the Shaftesbury Theatre!

shows.title: Be Like Blippi
shows.description:
A cherished children’s character worldwide, Blippi is back with a brand-new interactive show in 2026! Playing at the West End’s newest venue, The Arts at Marble Arch, located close to Hyde Park, experience the ultimate educational adventure this summer! Grab your orange glasses and embrace your inner explorer with Be More Blippi , jam-packed with high-energy music and plenty of surprises for children aged 2+. Secure your tickets today!

Blippi and Meekah invite families to bring their children to explore the world around them more curiously with this brand-new show. Step inside an interactive adventure which features some surprises alongside fan-favourite songs like “Monster Truck” and “Dino Dance”, and “The Excavator Song”.

Blippi is an American educational YouTube channel that rocketed to global popularity since its first episode aired in 2014. His 2023 show, Blippi the Musical , was based on the original YouTube series written by Steve John, and it was nominated for an Olivier Award. Blippi On Tour has delighted millions of children worldwide, playing in countries like North America, Mexico, Africa and the UK!

His last show in London, Blippi: The Wonderful World Tour , ran for a limited time at the Harold Pinter Theatre in 2024.

Clayton Grimm is best known for portraying the character of Blippi since 2019. He has credits in theatre and voice acting. Clayton previously played The Flash in the DC Justice League tour. This run in the West End will offer audiences a rare opportunity to see Clayton perform live, as well as appearing as Blippi at this year’s Camp Bestival.

This summer, make a date with this energetic children’s production that is “sure to uplift both kids and adults alike” during its limited engagement in the heart of London. If you’re looking for a fantastic addition to your summer holiday plans this year, don’t miss out on the opportunity to play and learn with Blippi himself! Book your tickets for Be Like Blippi at Arts at Marble Arch today!

shows.title: Beetlejuice
shows.description:
Have the time of your afterlife with the ‘supernaturally fun, fun, fun’ (Radio Times) musical sensation BEETLEJUICE. Hailed as ‘hilarious’ (Independent) and an ‘absolute scream’ (The Standard), don’t miss the ‘drop-dead gorgeous’ (Guardian) Broadway spectacular at London’s Prince Edward Theatre – for a limited season only.

Olivier nominee David Fynn (School of Rock) unleashes mayhem in a ‘sensational…unparalleled performance’ (Daily Express) as the iconic Beetlejuice in this ‘mercilessly entertaining celebration’ (Daily Mail) of Tim Burton’s beloved movie. Starring alongside him in an acclaimed cast is Hannah Nordberg (HBO’s Euphoria), giving a ‘dazzling West End debut’ (The Standard) as Lydia.

Meet Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teenager sharing her home with a pair of newly-deads and the demonic ghost with the most, Beetlejuice. He’s dead trouble, but if you really want to feel alive, just say his name three times…

Hailed as a ‘hallucinogenic spectacle’ (The Telegraph) bursting with ‘sets to die for’ (Daily Express) and ‘songs that are a blast’ (Sunday Express), BEETLEJUICE is the outrageous, life-affirming hit with a big (cold) heart. See it and you’ll want to make the most of every Day-O!

But act dead quick – BEETLEJUICE only appears in the West End for a limited run only. Possess your tickets now. Book your BEETLEJUICE theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

What is Beetlejuice about?

shows.title: Bill Bailey: Vaudevillean
shows.description:
Comedy legend Bill Bailey returns to the West End with his brand-new live show Bill Bailey: Vaudevillean at the Theatre Royal Haymarket, just off vibrant Picadilly. This limited stand-up musical comedy residency brings Bailey’s unique blend of musical virtuosity, surreal humour and storytelling to one of London’s historic theatres. Inspired by the rich tradition of vaudeville entertainment, the show celebrates the performers who once dominated pre-radio and pre-television stages with comedy, music and speciality acts - with a typically modern Bill Bailey twist. The run follows his previous sold-out engagement at the venue with Thoughtifier and arrives after a major UK arena tour of the same show.

Before streaming, before television and even before radio, vaudeville was the prime-time entertainment of its day, with performers combining comedy, music and eccentric speciality acts in lively variety shows that captivated audiences across theatres and music halls.

In Vaudevillean , Bill Bailey revisits that vibrant tradition, blending stand-up, original music and offbeat observations about modern life. Bailey, a multi-instrumentalist known for his ability to move effortlessly between instruments and musical styles, mixes witty storytelling with playful musical interludes and unexpected cultural references in this wonderfully wacky celebration of the art form.

Bill Bailey began performing stand-up in the 1990s, quickly gaining recognition for his imaginative mixture of music and comedy. His early solo show Bill Bailey’s Cosmic Jam helped establish his distinctive style and led to a television special broadcast on Channel 4.

Over the decades, he has become a regular presence on British television, while his live tours consistently sell out across the UK and internationally. Bailey’s shows often combine philosophical musings, cultural satire and impressive musicianship, making him one of the most distinctive performers in contemporary comedy. With Vaudevillean, Bailey continues that tradition while paying homage to the theatrical variety performers who shaped modern entertainment. The show will tour the UK before landing in London’s West End for a limited run.

Vaudevillean is written and performed by Bill Bailey ( Black Books, Never Mind the Buzzcocks ). One of the UK’s most distinctive comedians, Bailey is celebrated for blending stand-up with musical performance. His television appearances include Black Books, QI and Have I Got News for You , and he won BBCs Strictly Come Dancing in 2020.

Blending stand-up comedy, off-the-wall musical performances and affectionate nods to classic variety entertainment, this hilarious show is a lively celebration of performance in all its forms as Bill Bailey’s distinctive style brings the spirit of old-school vaudeville into the modern West End. This witty and unpredictable show from one of Britain’s most beloved and original comedians comes to London for a strictly limited run - secure your tickets for Bill Bailey: Vaudevillean at the Theaytre Royal Haymarket today!

shows.title: Billy Elliot
shows.description:
BILLY ELLIOT THE MUSICAL is heading on a UK tour, and will be playing at London’s Adelphi Theatre in 2027

Seen by almost 12 million people across five continents and honoured with more than 80 awards worldwide, BILLY ELLIOT THE MUSICAL is one of the most successful and beloved British musicals of all time. Ten years after it last played to audiences in its original home of London and the UK, this landmark production returns at last.

This is the musical that took the nation by surprise and went on to conquer the world. Praised as ‘Breathtaking. A dazzling 40-carat gem of a show’ (Daily Mail), ‘Dazzling. A triumph’ (Independent on Sunday) and ‘Pure magic’ (Sunday Express), BILLY ELLIOT THE MUSICAL returns as exhilarating, hilarious and unforgettable as ever, a defining British production finally coming home.

Book your BILLY ELLIOT THE MUSICAL theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

What is Billy Elliot the Musical about?

Set in a northern town during the miners’ strike of 1984/5, the show follows Billy’s journey from the boxing ring to the ballet class, where he discovers a passion for dance that will change his life forever. As Billy dares to dream, his courage unites his family, inspires his community, and proves the transformative power of art. Brought to life by the award-winning creative team behind the film, with iconic music by Elton John, Billy Elliot is an extraordinary theatrical experience that has captivated audiences around the world.

shows.title: Brainiac Live
shows.description:
The Brainiacs are set to blow your mind this summer with the return of their most popular and explosive live family science show! Based on the popular UK television show that aired on Sky One in 2003, Brainiac Live makes science thrilling for audiences of all ages at the Garrick Theatre, located just a stone’s throw away from the bustling area of Leicester Square and Chinatown.

Expected to be more mischievous than ever, Brainiac Live takes all those science experiments that are deemed too dangerous to try at home and brings them to life on the West End stage. From exploding microwaves, vortex smoke rings and exploding hydrogen balloons, to supercharged spinning chairs, Brainiac Live is a “60-minute entertainment spectacle that thrills with every crash, bang and wallop” (LondonTheatre1).

Brainiac Live has been a firm favourite for families since its first staging in 2008, and it has gone on to become an international success. The show’s West End debut took place at the Palace Theatre, current home of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child , in 2013. It went on to have more summer runs in London, as well as a two-week season at the Sydney Opera House and other subsequent productions in places like Hong Kong and Barcelona. Brainiac Live has also headlined major science festivals, and a recent dual-language English/Arabic production was staged in Saudi Arabia.

Last year, its success was rewarded when the show won the 2025 Olivier Award for Best Family show.

The 2026 West End company will be announced soon.

Brainiac Live is produced by Dan Colman. Other creatives on the team include Andy Joyce as creative director and Damian Stanton as designer.

Experience all the weird and wonderful world of science from the safety of your seat as Brainiac Live arrives in London with a bang at the Garrick Theatre for a limited run. This “show is quite literally, explosive, in both its energy and experiments” (Spy in the Stalls), making it the ideal addition to your plans this summer – don't miss it!

shows.title: Breaking The Waves

sources.title_as_listed: Breaking the Waves - English National Opera

shows.description:
Faith, heartbreak and loss combined with unflinching intensity are at the centre of Missy Mazzoli’s Breaking the Waves . A striking new production heads to the London Coliseum in 2027, a short walk from the National Gallery. This is your chance to experience one of the most contemporary operas of our time. Secure your tickets for this striking opera today!

Breaking the Waves is set in the Scottish Highlands in the early 1970s and centres on Bess McNeill and her husband, Jan. When her husband becomes paralysed in an offshore accident, the vows she made to Jan are put to the test. She is encouraged to have intimate relationships with other men and describe the experiences to him, convincing her that this will aid him.

The opera, which features a libretto by Royce Vavrek, is based on the 1996 film of the same name by Lars von Trier. It was adapted by Missy Mazzorli, one of the first two women who received a commission from the Metropolitan Opera House.

Staged in three acts, Breaking The Waves made its premiere in 2017 at the Skirball Center for the Performing Arts by Opera Philadelphia. It then went on to receive its European premiere in 2019 as part of a co-production with the Edinburgh International Festival and staged in association with Bristol Old Vic. The last time it was staged was at Detroit Opera in 2024.

The production won the inaugural Best New Opera Award from the Music Critics Association of North America and was also shortlisted for the Best World Premiere Prize at the International Opera Awards.

The principal cast includes:

Tinuke Craig will direct the production, conducted by Joana Carneiro.

Experience every beat of drama and emotion that Breaking the Waves has to offer for audiences. Book your tickets for a visceral, unflinching contemporary opera at the London Coliseum.

shows.title: Burlesque The Musical
shows.description:
Don your feather boa and grab the glitter as Burlesque The Musical slinks back into London! Based on the campy cult favourite movie about a small-town girl with a big voice, this musical thoroughly seduced audiences in 2025 and returns to the brand new, purpose-built Arts at Marble Arch Theatre, just a short walk from Hyde Park, for an encore this September. Burlesque is a “dazzling triumph” (Matinee Radio) and has a strictly limited run at the Savoy Theatre, so snap up your tickets today!

Aspiring singer Ali is “too much” for her quiet midwestern town, where she spends her days waitressing in her late mother's cafe. When Ali discovers she was adopted as a child, she leaves her humdrum home for the bright lights of New York City, hoping to find her long-lost birth mother. Drawn into the dazzling underworld of music, dance and seduction at a historic burlesque club, Ali not only finds her mother, Tess, who owns the club; she ends up finding herself, too. Amongst the misfits and dreamers of the club, Ali finally feels like she belongs, and sparks fly when she meets kindhearted barman Jackson. But when Tess’s vindictive ex Vince threatens to close down the club, Ali must fight for her new home. Will she be able to raise her voice to save Burlesque?

Gritty, glitzy and glamorous, Burlesque The Musical is a sizzling story of self-discovery, based on the hit 2010 film, which starred Cher and Christina Aguilera. This fresh new adaptation features all your favourite songs from the movie, with tunes by Christina Aguilera, Sia and Diane Warren, alongside new songs by Todrick Hall and Jess Folley. Burlesque is “big, in-your-face, blockbusting entertainment" (Reviews Hub) - book for this raunchy, riotous romp today!

The musical premiered at the Manchester Opera House in 2024 before transferring to the Theatre Royal, Glasgow. The show transferred to London’s Savoy Theatre in summer 2025, playing to sold-out audiences and earning a WhatsOnStage Award. The show now returns to the custom-built Arts Theatre at Marble Arch, and is the first production to open the semi-permanent venue.

Casting is to be announced for the 2026 production of Burlesque The Musical.

The film’s creator Steve Antin adapts his own work for the stage, writing the book for Burlesque , with additional material by Kate Wetherhead ( The Devil Wears Prada, Legally Blonde ). Antin’s previous credits include Gloria, Proud Mary, and Chasing Papi .

Music and Lyrics are by Christina Aguilera (who is also an executive producer for the show), Sia and Diane Warren, with additional songs by Jess Folley ( Les Miserables, X Factor – The Band) and Todrick Hall ( Midnight, Kinky Boots ).

So “Wagon Wheel Watusi” on down to Marble Arch and put some sparkle into your life with tickets to Burlesque The Musical at the Arts Theatre at Marble Arch. “ Burlesque is a musical that really does have it all” (Broadway World) - so what are you waiting for? Book this sexy, sassy and sequin-filled show today!

shows.description:
Winning a record-breaking seven Olivier awards, CABARET at the Kit Kat Club is one of the most successful musicals of all time. The story of a city, a club, and a generation dancing on the edge of history.

Berlin, 1930. A city alive with music, desire and possibility. The party is in full swing – but a shadow is growing at its edges.

Inside the intimate and electrifying Kit Kat Club, Sally Bowles sings to forget. Cliff Bradshaw writes to remember. And the Emcee reminds us that life is beautiful… until it isn’t.

Featuring some of the most celebrated songs in musical theatre history – including Willkommen, Mein Herr, Maybe This Time, Money and the title number Cabaret – London’s Playhouse Theatre is transformed into Berlin’s legendary Kit Kat Club for an unforgettable experience that the Daily Telegraph still calls “the best show in London”.

Olivier Award nominee Jamie Muscato (The Great Gatsby, Les Misérables) and Tony and Grammy Award nominated Joy Woods (The Notebook, Gyspy) take over the roles of Emcee and Sally Bowles from 25 May 2026. From 7 – 19 September 2026 the role of Sally Bowles will be played by Marina Tavolieri.

CABARET has music by John Kander, lyrics by Fred Ebb and a book by Joe Masteroff – based on the play by John Van Druten and stories by Christopher Isherwood.

Ready to immerse yourself in the electrifying Kit Kat Club and see the stars in London’s West End? Book your CABARET theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

Rehearsal photography by Marc Brenner From 22nd September 2026, Tuesday evening performances of Cabaret will be moving to 7pm.

Read More for show synopsis, cast & creative, age guidance and more…

What is Cabaret the Musical about?

It’s 1930s Berlin. It’s 2020s London. It’s Then, it’s Now. Who knows how long it will reside here. For now, we’re enjoying the party. The party at the end of the world.

Set in 1930s Berlin under the Weimar Republic, Cabaret the Musical tells the story of a racy, underground nightclub, the Kit Kat Club. It’s told through the lives of enigmatic Cabaret performers, The Emcee and cabaret singer Sally Bowles.

Before the show, guests are invited to enjoy the club with drinks, dining and pre-show entertainment all on offer. When booking, guests will receive a ‘club entry time’ and, for the richest experience and to immerse themselves fully in the club, we encourage people to arrive early.

Ticket Information

shows.title: Cats
shows.description:
Do you know how to go to the Heaviside Layer? Cats the Musical returns to London for a strictly limited run this summer, before embarking on a UK tour. This brand new staging of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Tony and Olivier-winning musical about the rhymes and rituals of a group of mischievous cats comes to Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, just a short walk from Baker Street. Don’t miss this purrfect new revival of Cats - secure your ticket today.

Once a year, the slinking stray cats and rebellious dreamers of London gather under the full moon for the Jellicile ball - a special time where one particular puss will be chosen to be reborn. As the cats gather, they sing, dance, celebrate, and tell their "tails". There’s the elderly patriarch Old Deuteronomy, the acrobatic, trouble-making twins Mungojerrie and Rumpleteazer, the devilish Macavity the mystery cat, sweet and quiet white kitten Victoria, and the outcast Grizabella, each with their own story to tell. But who will be chosen to ascend to the Heaviside Layer?

Cats is based on T.S. Eliot’s children’s poetry book Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats. The musical premiered in May 1981, and was a critical success, holding the record for longest-running West End Musical until 2006, when it was surpassed by Les Misérables . The musical has won several Olivier and Tony awards, and has enjoyed many revivals, tours and adaptations internationally, including a film adaptation in 2019 which starred Idris Elba, Judi Dench, Ian McKellen and Jennifer Hudson. This brand new staging features all your favourite songs from the show, including “Memory”, “Jellicle Songs for Jellicle Cats”, “Magical Mr Mistoffelees” and "Skimbleshanks: The Railway Cat".

Who will go to the Jellicle ball? Casting includes:

Cats is directed and choreographed by Drew McOnie. McOnie is an Olivier-nominated choreographer and director. He is the current artistic director of the Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, an Old Vic associate artist, and the artistic director of the McOnie dance company. His credits for Regent’s Park include Brigadoon, On the Town , Jesus Christ Superstar , and Carousel . Other credits include King Kong for the Broadway Theatre, Bugsy Malone for the Lyric Hammersmith and UK tour, and The Lorax for the Old Vic Theatre.

Lyrics are based on T.S. Eliot’s Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats. Music is by Andrew Lloyd Webber.

Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber is a British Composter. He is one of only twenty-one people in the world to hold an EGOT, which means he has won (multiple) Emmy, Tony, Oscar and Grammy awards. Lloyd Webber’s other accolades include Olivier, Ivor Novello and Brit Awards, and he also holds a Knighthood for his contributions to the arts. Lloyd Webber is a fellow of the British Academy of Songwriters, Composers, and Authors and an inductee into the Songwriters Hall of Fame. His best-known works include Sunset Boulevard, Starlight Express, Evita and Phantom of the Opera .

You’ll want to live the memories again and again this summer with this pawsome new production of Cats the Musical . Be dazzled by stunning choreography by Regent's Park Artistic Director Drew McOnie, along with all your favourite songs. The iconic Andrew Lloyd Webber musical comes to London for a strictly limited run this summer 2026, so don't miss out - secure your tickets for Cats at the Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre now!

shows.description:
This is the greatest show! Step inside the Empress Museum in Earl's Court, where the Big Top and immersive foyer performances transport you into the spectacle from the moment you arrive. Based on the blockbuster 2017 film, Come Alive! The Greatest Showman Circus Spectacular invites you into a vibrant world of music, storytelling, and jaw‑dropping circus artistry. You won’t want to miss this breathtaking experience, suitable for the whole family. Secure your tickets for this immersive circus show full of “incredible energy” (Daily Express) and “impressive acrobatics” (TimeOut) today!

A vibrant reinvention of the world of The Greatest Showman , but not a direct stage adaptation, Come Alive! tells a contemporary, original story inspired by the beloved film’s themes and soundtrack as plucky newcomer Max must learn to step into the spotlight and out of the shadows, with a little help from the circus’s owner, The Showman.

This “eye-popping theatrical spectacle” (WestEnd Theatre) features new characters, fresh narration, and all of Benj Pasek and Justin Paul’s hit songs from the film—including “This Is Me”, “Rewrite the Stars”, “A Million Dreams”, “Tightrope” and “The Greatest Show”. As well as enjoying the spectacular vocals, acrobatic feats and moving storytelling, audiences are welcomed into an immersive pre‑show experience, where performers mingle among the crowd and they can explore mini‑tents, meet performers, and enjoy food and drinks from the themed bars and vendors.

The Greatest Showman was a 2017 musical film by Jenny Bicks and Bill Condon, directed by Michael Gracey, starring Hugh Jackman, Zendaya and Zac Efron. Loosely based on the life of entertainer and circus ringleader PT Barnum, the film won the Golden Globe for Best Original Song for "This Is Me", and the award for Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media at the 2018 Grammys. “This Is Me” was also nominated for Best Original Song at the 2018 Academy Awards.

Main cast:

The show also features singer, dancers, and over 30 internationally acclaimed and award-winning circus performers from Cirque du Soleil and global ensembles, who bring spectacular acrobatics, aerial acts, teeterboard routines, Cyr wheel performances and human pyramids to life.

Come Alive! The Greatest Showman Circus Spectacular is the brainchild of visionary director Simon Hammerstein - grandson of famed lyricist Oscar Hammerstein II - who conceived the production as a reimagined celebration of The Greatest Showman’s spirit of inclusion and spectacle. Hammerstein’s other projects include hip-hop artist Usher’s sold-out Las Vegas Residency My Way , and immersive dinner theatre show Queen of the Night at New York's The Paramount Hotel. Hammerstein is a Drama Desk Award winner and co-founder of The Box nightclub in Soho. The show’s music is produced by Matthew Brind, an Olivier Award nominee whose previous work includes Paddington 2 and Live Aid jukebox musical Just For One Day . Choreography is by Jerry Reeve, known for his work with pop icon Taylor Swift and the Platinum Jubilee celebration, and Lukas McFarlane, whose credits include Strictly Come Dancing and The X Factor.

Lighting design is by Emmy Award nominee Adam Bassett, whose spectacular work lit up the London 2012 Olympics, with set design by Ruby Law, noted for her work on Warrior Queens . Costumes are by Susan Kulkarni, whose previous credits include The Peripheral and work for Secret Cinema. The production’s immersive art direction is led by Mika Handley, bringing experience from Secret Cinema and the Aladdin/Galaxy Experience.

Step under the Big Top and let the spirit of The Greatest Showman ignite your night with soaring acrobatics, live vocals, and a show full of wonder. Whether you're bringing family, treating visitors, or celebrating a special occasion, Come Alive! delivers spectacle, song and joyful discovery in every moment. Unmissable, unforgettable - and booking fast! Experience one-of-a-kind showmanship and book tickets for Come Alive! The Greatest Showman Circus Spectacular at the Empress Museum. Get in the ring - and prepare to be dazzled!

shows.title: Cyrano De Bergerac
shows.description:
Adrian Lester reprises his role as long-nosed wordsmith Cyrano, as the RSC’s acclaimed production of Cyrano de Bergerac transfers to the Noel Coward Theatre, in the heart of Covent Garden. Ashamed of his large nose, soldier and poet Cyrano is drawn into a scheme to help his hapless love rival charm the woman he too is secretly in love with in this “warm and likeable”(Guardian) revival of Edmond Rostand’s romantic play. This production was critically acclaimed when it debuted in Stratford in 2025, and comes to London for a strictly limited run - secure your tickets today.

'No master to serve, no leash to bear. I walk as I please, and I speak as I dare.'

Soldier, poet and philosopher, delightfully witty and deeply romantic, Cyrano de Bergerac is a truly brilliant man. There’s just one small, or large, problem - his remarkable nose.

Wilfully proud, but wracked with doubts over his appearance, Cyrano must watch from afar as the woman he loves - the bold, beautiful, poetry-loving Roxanne - falls for another man. But this suitor, Christian, whilst handsome, does not have a way with words - and he knows this is the only way to truly win Roxanne’s heart. Enter Cyrano, who must help Christian woo the woman he loves from the shadows.

Cyrano de Bergerac was written in 1897 by Edmond Rostand, loosely based on the life of the real 17th-century novelist and playwright, Cyrano de Bergerac. Though the real Cyrano did have a somewhat large nose, this element is generally very exaggerated for performance. The play, which is written entirely in verse, first premiered at the Théâtre de la Porte Saint-Martin, France, and has since had many notable adaptations - including Jamie Lloyd’s stripped back 2019 production starring James McAvoy, a 1970 production translated by Anthony Burgess, and several film adaptations including Netflix movie The Half of It , and Golden Globe-winning musical adaption Cyrano , which starred Peter Dinklage. The play is credited with introducing the word "panache" (meaning a confident and flamboyant style) into the English language.

This Royal Shakespeare Company production premiered at the Swan Theatre, Stratford-upon-Avon, in 2025 to critical acclaim, adapting the original verse in a mixture of rhyming couplets and modern English, and now transfers to London for a limited season.

Casting includes:

Adrian Lester reprises his role as Cyrano from the shows RSC run, which marked his debut with the company. Lester is an Olivier, Evening Standard Theatre Award and a Critics' Circle Theatre Award winner, and Tony nominee. He is best known for his roles in The Sandman, Riviera, Company, The Lehman Trilogy, Henry V , and for playing the titular role in Othello , opposite Rory Kinnear as Iago, at the National Theatre.

Cyrano de Bergerac was originally written by French dramatist and poet Edmond Rostand. The show is directed by Simon Evans ( Staged, The Dazzle, A Day in the Death of Joe Egg ), who also co-adapted the script with playwright and poet Debris Stevenson ( My Brother’s a Genius, Poet in Da Corner ).

Adrian Lester’s “standout” (Guardian) performance as the nosy, love-lorn poet “crackles with an electricity” (Broadway Baby) in this lyrical, romantic tale of love, lies, longing and disguise. Cyrano de Bergerac is full of “emotional authenticity and neat, quipping wit” (Guardian). You’ll fall for this brand new revival, so don’t miss this strictly limited RSC transfer - book tickets for Cyrano de Bergerac at the Noel Coward Theatre today.

shows.title: Dark of the Moon
shows.description:
A haunting tale of love and prejudice comes to life in Dark of the Moon , playing at the Charing Cross Theatre, just off the Strand. Based on a 1940s play about a witch-boy and a human who fall in love, this new musical reimagines a classic Appalachian folktale through a distinctive score, blending country, bluegrass and rock’n’roll. This production comes to London for a strictly limited run - read our Dark of the Moon review and secure your tickets today!

In a quiet Appalachian town, superstition and tradition shape daily life. High in the nearby Smoky Mountains, however, another world exists - a mysterious realm inhabited by witches and warlocks whose powers influence the land below. When John, a curious witch-boy, falls in love with Barbara, a human girl from the town, their relationship challenges the boundaries between these two worlds. Determined to live among humans, John makes a dangerous bargain that allows him to become mortal, but only if Barbara remains faithful. As suspicion spreads through the town and tensions rise between the earthly and supernatural communities, the couple’s love is tested by prejudice, fear and the consequences of the pact made under the dark of the moon. Blending folklore with emotional storytelling, this new musical explores whether love can survive when two opposing worlds collide.

Dark of the Moon is based on the play of the same name by Howard Richardson and William Berney, which was in turn inspired by the traditional folk ballad “Barbara Allen”, a centuries-old song that appears in British and American folk traditions. Richardson and Berney’s drama transformed the ballad into a supernatural tale set in the Appalachian Mountains, blending folklore, romance, and social commentary. Premiering on Broadway in 1945 and in London in 1948, the play became known for combining fantasy and realism and exploring themes of prejudice within a small community. Despite the story’s rich folklore and atmospheric setting, the play is rarely revived - although it does feature as a 'play within a play' in Stranger Things: The First Shadow .

While the original play does include songs, this musical version expands the story through a score influenced by Appalachian musical traditions, bringing the tension between the human and supernatural worlds to life through music as well as drama. The musical had its developmental debut at the Rubicon Theatre in California in 2023, and now makes its UK premiere at The Charing Cross Theatre for a strictly limited run.

Casting for this production is to be confirmed.

Dark of the Moon features a book by Emmy nominee Jonathan Prince ( American Dreams, Melrose Place ), with music and lyrics by Grammy winning song writers Lindy Robbins ( Birds of Prey, Descendants ), Dave Bassett (Elle King’s “Ex’s & Oh’s”, Vance Joy’s “Riptide”) and Steve Robson (James Blunt’s “You’re Beautiful”, One Direction’s “Story of My Life”). The musical is based on the play by Howard D. Richardson and William Berney.

The production is directed by Georgie Rankcom ( Ride, Anyone Can Whistle ), with choreography by Jane McMurtrie ( Lizzie, Spring Awakening ). Brad Haak ( Come From Away, School of Rock ) serves as Musical Supervisor, with Matt Herbert ( Matilda the Musical, Heathers ) as Music Director and orchestrations by Dillon Kondor ( Six, Be More Chill ).

Production design is by Libby Todd ( Ride, The Secret Diary of Adrian Mole Aged 13¾ ), with lighting design by Jonathan Chan ( Ride, The Time Traveller’s Wife ) and sound design by Andrew Johnson ( Heathers, Jerry Springer: The Opera ).

Dark of the Moon blends romance, folklore and music with supernatural drama and a sultry, Appalachian-inspired soundtrack. You won't want to miss this atmospheric new musical from an award-winning creative team. Let yourself be spellbound - secure your tickets for Dark of the Moon at the Charing Cross Theatre today.

shows.title: Death Note: The Musical
shows.description:
Death Note: The Musical makes its UK premiere at the Barbican Theatre, just a short walk from Moorgate, this summer. Based on the bestselling Japanese manga, this stage adaptation transforms the cult phenomenon psychological thriller into a high-intensity musical. When high school student Light discovers an otherworldly notebook that will kill anyone whose name is written in its pages, he sets about ridding the world of evildoers - until quirky detective L enters the scene, seeking to discover who exactly is behind the murders. What ensues is a tense game of cat and mouse, in this “deliciously dark masterpiece” (Stage2Page), coming to London for a strictly limited run.

When brilliant but disillusioned student Light Yagami discovers a mysterious notebook that grants him the power to kill anyone whose name he writes in it, his world changes instantly. The notebook belongs to Ryuk, a bored Shinigami, or death god, who drops it into the human world for his own amusement.

Determined to rid society of criminals, Light adopts the alias “Kira” and begins delivering his own twisted idea of justice, until his actions attract the attention of an enigmatic and eccentric detective known only as L. As the two engage in a tense battle of intellect and morality, the line between hero and villain swiftly blurs.

Blending supernatural elements with a gripping psychological duel, Death Note: The Musical explores power, corruption and the consequences of absolute justice, set to a stirring, contemporary score.

Death Note began as a manga series serialised between 2003 and 2006, quickly becoming a worldwide success. It has since inspired an equally acclaimed anime adaptation, live-action films, novels and video games, cementing its place as a modern pop culture phenomenon.

The musical adaptation premiered in Tokyo in 2015 and has since been staged in South Korea and in concert versions internationally, including two limited-run, sell-out concert stagings at the London Palladium and Lyric Theatre in 2023. The full production now makes its UK premiere at the Barbican Theatre, continuing the story’s global journey from page to stage.

Whose name will be written in the Death Note? Casting for this production is to be announced.

Death Note: The Musical features a book by Ivan Menchell ( Bonnie & Clyde, The Cemetery Club ), with music by Frank Wildhorn ( Jekyll & Hyde, The Scarlet Pimpernel ) and lyrics by Jack Murphy ( Wonderland, The Civil War ). The original manga was written by Tsugumi Ohba and illustrated by Takeshi Obata.

Further creative team members are to be confirmed.

Death Note is a “unique and exquisite musical” (West End Best Friend); you won't want to miss this cult phenomenon, fully realised in London for the very first time. Filled with moral complexity and an electric score, Death Note: The Musical is “to die for” (All That Dazzles). The battle of wits between Light and L will have you on the edge of your seat, and is sure to be in high demand, as the previous concert stagings sold out. Secure your tickets to Death Note: The Musical at the Barbican Theatre today.

shows.title: Dinosaur World Live
shows.description:
Embark on a Roarsome adventure this summer as Dinosaur World Live returns to London due to popular demand. Coming to the Wembley Park Theatre, in the heart of Wembley, this Olivier-winning, family-friendly show features jaw-dropping puppets and audience interaction in a vivid prehistoric world. Little ones can even meet the dinos afterwards - if they’re brave enough! Head off on a Jurassic adventure - book today!

In a prehistoric world, the terrifying Tyrannosaurus Rex lurks in wait for its prey - but T-Rex's arent the only creatures you will meet as Triceratops, Giraffatitans, Microraptors and Segnosaurus all roam the stage in this epic and educational show. Join a gang of intrepid explorers as they head on a thrilling journey back to Jurassic times, featuring astonishingly life-like puppets and audience interaction.

Dinosaur World Live is an international smash hit, and has toured the United States, Australia, China, and Ireland to great success. The show won an Olivier award in 2024, following five UK tours and multiple London seasons at Regent’s Park Open-Air Theatre, Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre and Underbelly's Wonderground Festival.

This show is dino-mite! Travel back in time on a thrilling trail through the Jurassic forests, and meet all your favourite dinosaurs in this award-winning interactive show. With eye-popping special effects and amazingly realistic puppets, this is an astonishing adventure for all the family, best suited to those 3+. Secure your tickets for Dinosaur World Live at the Wembley Park Theatre today!

shows.title: Dog Man: The Musical
shows.description:
Get ready for tail-wagging fun as Dog Man: The Musical bounds into the Queen Elizabeth Hall, Southbank Centre, on scenic Bankside, for a limited run. This high-energy kids' musical is based on the bestselling book series by Dav Pilkey, creator of Captain Underpants and Cat Kid Comic Club , and tells the story of a half-dog, half-human superhero. With quirky characters, catchy songs, and chaotic comedy, this “fun, goofy musical romp” (Broadway World) is perfect for families this summer holidays and makes its UK debut following an acclaimed off-Broadway run in 2024.

Best friends and comic-book masterminds George and Harold are back - and this time, they’ve gone full razzle dazzle. The ten-year-old pranksters decide it’s time to bring their most beloved character to life: Dog Man, the fearless, furniture-chewing crime-fighter who’s part canine, part cop, and all hero. And this isn't just any old Dog Man story - it’s a musical. But things quickly get ruff for this crime-biting hero. Dog Man’s arch-nemesis, Petey the Cat, has cloned himself for double trouble, the villainous cyborg fish Flippy is building an army of Beasty Buildings, and George and Harold might not finish their show before lunchtime! Bursting with silly humour, giant puppets, cartoon action and comic book-style staging, Dog Man: The Musical captures the anarchic charm of cartoonist and author Dav Pilkey’s books while encouraging kids to embrace imagination and teamwork.

Dog Man: The Musical is based on the hugely successful children’s graphic novels by Dav Pilkey, whose irreverent humour and doodle-style drawings have won him millions of fans around the world. First published in 2016, the Dog Man books have sold over 50 million copies and are known for combining slapstick silliness with messages of kindness, creativity and second chances. The musical premiered Off-Broadway in 2019, presented by TheatreWorksUSA, and was praised by The New York Times as “a hilarious delight” that successfully brought the chaos and heart of the books to life. It has since toured the US and enjoyed widespread acclaim from families and educators alike. Fun fact: Dav Pilkey came up with the idea for Dog Man when he was just a kid himself, as the character was invented during a school assignment that resulted in him being sent to the hallway for disrupting class! That same spirit of rebellious creativity now fuels this hilarious musical.

Casting for this production is to be announced.

The musical is directed and choreographed by Jen Wineman ( The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee, Shakespeare in Love ) with book and lyrics by Emmy nominee and Tony winner Kevin Del Aguila ( Peg + Cat, Altar Boyz ), and music by Brad Alexander ( Clifford the Big Red Dog, Click, Clack, Moo ). The show is produced by TheatreWorksUSA, a company known for creating fantastic theatre experiences for younger audiences. Further creative team members are to be announced.

Join the tail-wagging, villain-thwarting fun as Dog Man: The Musical brings the pages of your kids’ favourite book to life! With larger-than-life puppetry, jokes for all ages, big-hearted songs, and heroic hijinks, it’s a paws-itively perfect pick for school holidays. Book your tickets for Dog Man: The Musical at the Queen Elizabeth Hall today, and get ready for laughs, licks, and lots of live-action comic book musical magic!

shows.title: Grace Pervades
shows.description:
Ralph Fiennes stars in the London transfer of Grace Pervades , a new play from Olivier and Tony Award-winning playwright David Hare, about the lives of acclaimed Victorian actors Henry Irving and Ellen Terry. Fresh from a critically acclaimed transfer at the Theatre Royal Bath, this “exceptional” (Guardian) work comes to the Theatre Royal Haymarket, just a stone's throw from Piccadilly Circus. Set an alert to book today!

Grace Pervades follows the lives of groundbreaking Victorian actors Henry Irving and Ellen Terry, interweaving their personal and professional lives in an “elegant love letter to theatre” (Guardian). Irving is an established performer and manager whose wife and children come second to his career and his aim to make theatre respectable; Terry is an acclaimed actress and, scandalously, an unwed mother, who longs to step into the leading roles. As their relationship deepens from mentee and mentor to something more, Irving and Terry must navigate the changing face of the art form they have fought to shape, and contend with what their theatrical legacy might be.

Based on the remarkable true stories of Henry Irving, who was the first actor to be knighted, and Ellen Terry, whose decades-long career was highly influential, Grace Pervades sheds a new light on these theatrical icons. Titled after a scathing review of a performance of Terry’s, in which a reviewer stated “Grace pervades the hussy”, and made disparaging remarks about her children, who were born out of wedlock, Grace Pervades premiered at the Theatre Royal Bath in summer 2025 to critical acclaim. The production comes to the Theatre Royal Haymarket for a strictly limited run - make sure to book early for this “fascinating, absorbing and very funny” (Financial Times) play.

Ralph Fiennes and Miranda Raison reprise their roles as Henry Irving and Ellen Terry from the Theatre Royal Bath run.

Ralph Fiennes is a British actor, best known for his roles in Conclave, The English Patient, Schindler’s List, The Menu and as Lord Voldemort in Harry Potter . Fiennes is also an acclaimed stage actor who has performed with the RSC and at the National Theatre, and has won Tony Awards for his roles in Bryan Friel’s Faith Healer and Hamlet , directed by Jonathan Kent. As well as his Tony Awards, Fiennes is a BAFTA, Emmy, Golden Globe and Academy Award winner. Miranda Raison is a British actor, best known for her role as Jo Portman in BBC One spy drama Spooks . Her credits also include roles in Doctor Who , HBO’s Warrior, and Silk for BBC One. Her stage roles include originating the role of Anne Boleyn in Howard Brenton's Anne Boleyn at Shakespeare’s Globe, Jez Butterworth’s The River at The Royal Court and starring as Hermione in The Winter’s Tale at the Garrick Theatre, directed by Kenneth Branagh.

They will be joined in the West End by:

Grace Pervades is written by David Hare. Hare is an acclaimed British playwright and screenwriter. He is a three-time Tony winner, a BAFTA and Olivier Award winner, and Golden Globe and Academy Award nominee. Hare’s credits include Academy Award-nominated screenplays for The Hours , starring Meryl Streep and The Reader with Fiennes and Kate Winslet, and plays Racing Demon at the National Theatre, Amy's View at the National Theatre and on Broadway, starring Judy Dench, and Straight Line Crazy at the Bridge Theatre, also starring Fiennes. In 1998, Hare was knighted in the Queen's Birthday Honours List for his services to theatre.

Jeremy Herrin directs. Herrin is a British director, a co-founding director of Second Half Productions and a former Artistic Director of acclaimed theatre company Headlong. He is an Evening Standard Theatre Award and South Bank Sky Arts Award winner and three-time Olivier Award winner. Herrin’s credits include the critically acclaimed stage adaptations of Hilary Mantel’s novels Wolf Hall and Bringing Up the Bodies for the RSC and West End, People Places and Things at the National Theatre and Long Day's Journey into Night at the Wyndham's Theatre, starring Brian Cox.

Don’t miss your opportunity to see Ralph Fiennes and Miranda Raison’s “mesmerising” (Times) performances in this powerful new play from award-winning playwright David Hare. Grace Pervades is “luminous, magnetic” (What’s On Stage) and comes to London for a strictly limited run in April 2026. Set an alert today and make sure to secure your tickets for Grace Pervades at the Theatre Royal Haymarket as soon as they go on sale!

shows.title: Hadestown
shows.description:
Step into the mesmerising world of HADESTOWN at the Lyric Theatre, where myth, music, and love collide in a breathtaking Tony Award-winning spectacle – don’t miss your chance to experience this unforgettable journey!

HADESTOWN, the acclaimed Broadway musical phenomenon by singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and director Rachel Chavkin is now playing at the Lyric Theatre. Until 8 March, the cast features Daniel Breaker as Hermes; Desmonda Cathabel as Eurydice; Chris Jarman as Hades; Joy Wielkens as Persephone; and Dylan Wood as Orpheus.

From 10 March 2026, joining the company are Rachel Adedeji (Jesus Christ Superstar; Thriller Live!) as Persephone, Bethany Antonia (House of the Dragon) as Eurydice, Marley Fenton (Hamilton; The Wizard of Oz) as Orpheus, Alastair Parker (Matilda; The Crucible) as Hades, and Olivier Award-winner Clive Rowe (Guys and Dolls; Sister Act) as Hermes.

‘An epic celebration of music, togetherness and hope’ (Forbes) HADESTOWN is the winner of 8 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the Grammy Award® for Best Musical Theatre Album.

A deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience, HADESTOWN invites you to imagine how the world could be.

Book your HADESTOWN theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

What is Hadestown about?

WELCOME TO HADESTOWN, WHERE A SONG CAN CHANGE YOUR FATE.

HADESTOWN takes you on an unforgettable journey to the underworld and back, intertwining two mythic love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone.

shows.title: Hamilton
shows.description:
London’s Victoria Palace Theatre is home to Lin-Manuel Miranda’s critically acclaimed musical, HAMILTON – the story of America then, as told by America now.

Inspired by Ron Chernow’s biography of Alexander Hamilton, HAMILTON has book, music and lyrics by Lin-Manuel Miranda. Directed by Thomas Kail, HAMILTON has choreography by Andy Blankenbuehler and musical supervision and orchestrations by Alex Lacamoire.

Alex Sawyer portrays Alexander Hamilton alongside Nathania Ong (Eliza Hamilton), Emily-Mae (Angelica Schuyler) and Simbi Akande (Peggy Schuyler) as the Schuyler sisters.

Jay Perry plays Hamilton’s rival Aaron Burr, with Thomas Vernal in the role of George Washington and Daniel Boys playing King George. Completing the main cast are Jordan Benjamin as John Laurens/Phillip Hamilton, Lemuel Knights as the Marquis de Lafayette/Thomas Jefferson, and Jordan Castle as Hercules Mulligan/James Madison.

One of the most highly acclaimed Broadway musicals, HAMILTON is the winner of 11 Tony Awards including Best Musical. HAMILTON has also received 7 Olivier Awards, the Pulitzer Prize for Drama and the Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album.

Book your HAMILTON musical theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

Read More for show synopsis, cast & creative, age guidance and more…

What is Hamilton the musical about?

Hamilton is the story of America’s Founding Father Alexander Hamilton, an immigrant from the West Indies. Hamilton became George Washington’s right-hand man during the Revolutionary War and helped to shape the foundations of America. The score by creator Lin-Manuel Miranda blends hip-hop, jazz, blues, rap, R&B and Broadway.

shows.description:
Love Harry Potter? Can’t get enough of the books or movies which shaped the minds of a generation? Then you’ll certainly want to catch HARRY POTTER AND THE CURSED CHILD – TWO PARTS at the Palace Theatre in the West End. Book tickets for performances before 20th September for your last chance to see this magical play in its original 2 parts!

Based on original material by J.K. Rowling, Jack Thorne and John Tiffany, HARRY POTTER AND THE CURSED CHILD – TWO PARTS is the award-winning eighth story in the Harry Potter series – and the first Harry Potter story to be brought to life as a play on stage.

This critically acclaimed production received its world premiere in the West End in summer 2016. HARRY POTTER AND THE CURSED CHILD – TWO PARTS remains the most awarded West End play in the history of the Laurence Olivier Awards. The production scooped a record‐breaking nine awards including Best New Play and Best Director in 2017.

Experience magic in every moment. Book your HARRY POTTER AND THE CURSED CHILD theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

PLEASE NOTE: Prices displayed are per person, per perfomance. You will be charged for 2 performances per person (Part One and Part Two). Both performances on Sunday, 6 September 2026 will be Captioned.

What is Harry Potter and the Cursed Child about?

Return to the Wizarding World. Discover where life takes Harry and his youngest son Albus, as father and son learn the uncomfortable truth: sometimes, darkness comes from unexpected places.
