shows.title: Heathers The Musical
shows.description:
The students of Westerburg High are back in London and more murderous than ever as Heathers comes to The Arts at Marble Arch Theatre, just a short walk from Hyde Park, for a strictly limited season. This deliciously dark musical has been a fan favourite for over a decade, and now theatregoers can say “greetings and salutations” to even more black comedy, murderous plots, and queen bee cliques as Heathers the Musical returns to one of the capital’s most exciting new venues.

Welcome to Westerburg High, where popularity can be a matter of life and death. Social reject Veronica Sawyer is just trying to get by, but when she is unexpectedly taken in by the beautiful but cruel Heathers, her dreams of being popular seem to be coming true. Her newfound status is rocked by rebel newcomer JD, however, and soon Veronica learns that it might hurt to be a nobody, but being somebody could lead to murder…

Wickedly funny and whip-smart, Heathers The Musical is adapted from the 1988 cult film, which famously starred Winona Ryder and Christian Slater. Fans of the film can enjoy its biggest, bloodiest and most hilarious moments reimagined via songs including “Candy Store”, “Seventeen” and “Dead Girl Walking”. Since its UK stage debut in 2018, it has become a sensation amongst young theatregoers and won the fan-voted WhatsOnStage Award for Best New Musical.

Casting is to be announced.

Heathers is adapted for the stage with a book, music and lyrics by Emmy nominee Kevin Murphy ( Desperate Housewives, Reefer Madness! the Musical ), and Lucile Lortel winner Laurence O’Keefe ( Legally Blonde the Musical, Bat Boy: The Musical ). Andy Fickman ( She’s the Man, Reefer Madness! the Musical ) directs, with choreography by Gary Lloyd ( Cruel Intentions the Musical, Sweet Charity ).

Honey, what you waiting for? Don’t be a loser: join the clique that everyone’s talking about with Heathers ! The killer musical will get your heart racing and your feet tapping as chaos descends in the school halls - book tickets for Heathers at the Arts Theatre Marble Arch today!

shows.title: High School Musical
shows.description:
Twenty years after the release of the iconic Disney Channel Movie, High School Musical, arrives back in London! Join Troy, Gabriella and the students of East High as they navigate the highs and lows of being teenagers with their first love, friendships and self-discovery! Playing at the Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre, a short walk from Wembley Stadium, grab a slice of some 2000s nostalgia this autumn.

High School Musical tells the story of a popular basketball star and an academically gifted student whose lives unexpectedly intertwine after meeting on a ski trip. Back at East High School, the unlikely pair reunite and decide to use their love for singing to audition for the annual school musical. However, Troy is supposed to be focused on his basketball, whilst Gabriella has commitments to her studies. Add in the drama club leads, Sharpay Evans and her brother Ryan, who try to sabotage the duo to sustain the spotlight for themselves, will Troy and Gabriella be able to break free from who everyone around them expects them to be?

The musical features all the hit songs from the original movie, including “Breaking Free”, “We’re All in This Together”, and “Stick to the Status Quo”!

First released in 2006 on the Disney Channel, High School Musical became the most commercially successful television film of its time. It generated 7.7 million viewers during its broadcast premiere, with two further sequels being released in 2007 and 2008, respectively.

The first adaptation for the stage made its debut in Minneapolis in 2007, with a US tour subsequently taking place for 15 months. High School Musical made its way into the UK, both as a London and touring production, in 2008.

This brand-new non-replica musical will be staged at the Troubadour Wembley Park after its initial premiere at The Lowry in Salford in summer 2026.

The lead cast for Disney’s High School Musical includes:

Tobias Turley will play the role of Troy. A rising star, his credits include Hot Mess , White Rose The Musical, and Heathers the Musical . He won the ITV talent competition, Mamma Mia! I Have a Dream in 2023. He will be joined by Leonor Correia as Gabriella. Her professional debut was in Six the Musical.

Playing the roles of Sharpay and Ryan Evans will be Caitlin Tipping and Luke Bayer. Caitlin’s theatre credits include Disney’s Frozen the Musical and The Last Five Years . Luke Bayer’s credits include RENT and the original West End cast of Everybody’s Talking About Jamie . Caitlin and Luke recently starred in Titanique together.

Harry Judd will star as Coach Bolton in the London run of High School Musical. A member of the British band McFly, Harry won Strictly Come Dancing in 2011 and also starred in the UK tour of Shrek the Musical in 2023.

KayCee Stroh stars as Ms Darbus. The American actress, singer and dancer is most known for starring as Martha Cox in the High School Musical franchise.

High School Musical will be co-directed by Joseph Houston and William Whelton, the founders of the Hope Mill Theatre in Manchester.

The musical features choreography by Aaron Renfree, set design by Andrew Exeter, sound design by Matt Peploe, video design by George Reeve, lighting design by Rory Beaton, costume design by Sophie Pardon, musical supervision by Katy Richardson, and musical direction by Audra Cramer.

This fresh, feel-good hit is serving up a delicious slice of nostalgia at the Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre in 2026. Whether you are ready to revisit the generation-defining musical or want to discover it for the first time, Get’cha Head in the Game and book your tickets for this limited London run of Disney’s High School Musical!

shows.title: High Society
shows.description:
Get ready to misbehave as Cole Porter’s Golden Age musical High Society returns to London for the first time in over a decade. This brand new production stars The Good Life’s Felicity Kendal and Call The Midwife's Helen George, and comes to the Barbican, just a short walk from Moorgate, for a strictly limited run this spring. Don’t miss this hilarious, witty and sharply satirical musical all about the romantic misadventures of a stuck-up socialite.

Set in a wealthy enclave near New York City, High Society follows the romantic entanglements of Tracy Lord, a poised and independent socialite preparing for her second wedding. When her charming ex-husband, Dexter Haven, returns unexpectedly, with a pair of undercover reporters in tow, old flames reignite, and complications ensue. As the wedding approaches, Tracy must untangle her feelings and choose between her polished fiancé, her persistent ex, and a journalist who sees past her upper-crust exterior. Packed with Cole Porter classics like ”Ridin’ High”, “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?”, and “Let’s Misbehave,” the musical blends screwball comedy, class satire, and heartfelt romance into a sparkling tale of love, second chances, and social spectacle.

High Society is based on Philip Barry’s comedy play The Philadelphia Story, as well as the 1956 film adaptation, High Society . The musical blends Porter's original songs with a new book by Arthur Kopit and additional lyrics by Susan Birkenhead. The show first premiered at the American Conservatory Theater in San Francisco in 1997 before transferring to Broadway. The Broadway cast featured a 12-year-old Anna Kendrick in the role of Dinah Lord, a performance that earned Kendrick a Theatre World Award and a Tony nomination. The production ran for 144 performances and earned two Tony nominations before closing in 1998.

Across the pond, a different version of High Society, using Cole Porter’s songs but a separate book by Richard Eyre, premiered in the West End at the Victoria Palace Theatre in 1987, running for over 400 performances. The UK premiere of the Arthur Kopit version came later, with a summer 2003 production at Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, followed by a UK tour, and a West End transfer, running from 2005 to 2006.

One of the most acclaimed revivals came in 2015 at The Old Vic in London. Directed by Maria Friedman, this production presented High Society in the round, creating an intimate and immersive atmosphere. This brand new 2026 production marks the show's return to London for the first time in over a decade.

Strictly Come Dancing stars Felicity Kendal ( Arcadia, Rosemary & Thyme, The Good Life ) and Helen George ( Call The Midwife, The Three Musketeers ) lead the cast, with further casting including:

Music and lyrics are by Cole Porter. Porter (1891-1964) was one of the most celebrated American composers and lyricists of the 20th century, renowned for his sophisticated, witty, and urbane songs. He composed dozens of Broadway scores during the 1920s through the 1950s, and his best-known works include Anything Goes, Kiss Me, Kate, and Can-Can . Kiss Me, Kate earned Porter the first-ever Tony Award for Best Musical in 1949, along with awards for Best Composer and Lyricist. Arthur Kopit (1937 - 2021) was a Tony- and Pulitzer-nominated American playwright and librettist. He rose to prominence in the early 1960s with his absurdist satire Oh Dad, Poor Dad, Mamma’s Hung You in the Closet and I’m Feelin’ So Sad , which premiered Off-Broadway and quickly became a critical success. His other notable works include plays Indians, Wings, End of the World with Symposium to Follow, and the book for Broadway musical Nine , adapted from Fellini’s film 8½. Directed by Rachel Kavanaugh, who has previously directed at the Royal Shakespeare Company, Chichester Festival Theatre, and Regent's Park Open Air Theatre, choreogrpahy by Anthony Van Laast, and Musical supervision and direction from Stephen Ridley.

You’ll be “Ridin’ High” this spring as this brand new production of High Society twirls onto the stage at the Barbican for a strictly limited run. Strictly star Helen George and TV Legend Felicity Kendal lead the cast as this fizzing, hilarious and vibrant music returns to London for the first time in over a decade. You won't want to miss it - book tickets for High Society at the Barbican today!

shows.title: Horrible Histories: Barmy Britain
shows.title_norm: horrible histories barmy britain the best bits

sources.title_as_listed: Horrible Histories: Barmy Britain – The Best Bits
Horrible Histories: Barmy Britain - The Best Bits

shows.description:
Forget boring lessons about tedious Tudors and stuffy Saxons: Horrible Histories is back in the West End this summer with Barmy Britain ! This family show from the award-winning team behind Awful Egyptians and Ruthless Romans promises gruesomely good historical facts and hair-raising figures from the olden days. School’s out, but learning for fun is definitely in at the Apollo Theatre, near Tottenham Court Road.

Horrible Histories: Barmy Britain invites the whole family to experience history with all the nasty bits left in! From battling legendary warrior queen Boudicca and escaping dastardly graverobbers Burke and Hare, to a quick stop to party with Queen Victoria (you will be amused!), this is a riotous chance to get up close and personal with history’s most exciting moments and most eccentric people.

Following up on previous Barmy Britain productions, this is the ultimate pick ‘n’ mix of figures and events from the past. You might have heard of some, but you won’t know the full story, and this is a fantastic way to get kids interested in learning.

The best-selling Horrible Histories books were created by Terry Deary and inspired a hit television series full of catchy songs including “King of Bling” and “The Monarch’s Song”. They’ve since expanded to the big screen, with Horrible Histories: Rotten Romans invading cinemas.

On stage, shows including Groovy Greeks , Terrible Tudors and Ruthless Romans have played up and down the UK, created by multi-award-nominated children’s theatre creators Birmingham Stage Company. Artistic Director Neal Foster founded the company over three decades ago, and their hit productions include Awful Auntie , Gangsta Granny and Barmy Britain parts one to five!

Get ready to dodge the plague, catch the Gunpowder Plotters, stand and deliver to Dick Turpin… and have a wild ride through hundreds of years of brilliantly bonkers British history! Tickets for Horrible Histories: Barmy Britain - The Best Bits at Apollo Theatre are the ultimate treat for kids and big kids, aged 5 to 105.

shows.title: Hot Mess
shows.description:
Jack Godfrey and Ellie Coote’s “blazing musical about Earth and humanity’s toxic love affair” (The Guardian) returns to the stage following its triumphant debut in Birmingham, Edinburgh and London in 2025. Take your chance on a hopeful new musical and experience a fresh perspective on the climate crisis at The Other Palace, located just a short walk away from Buckingham Palace.

Told through the infectious narrative of a rom-com, Hot Mess explores the relationship between Earth and Humanity. Earth has been waiting for over a billion years for someone to come along that she can relate to, and when she meets Human, she thinks her luck has finally changed. But things start to become toxic between the pair when Human begins to take her for granted by not clearing up his mess, and begins to develop an interest in other planetary bodies. Hot Mess is a musical that ultimately shows the climate crisis as a relationship on the brink of collapse.

Previously entitled This is a Love Story , the production was both performed on the stage at the Dundee Rep and live-streamed in 2021. After developing the productions and creating new songs, the show was given a new title of Hot Mess and was commissioned by Vicky Graham Productions in its debut at the Birmingham Hippodrome.

Hot Mess went on to perform at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 2025, starring Danielle Steers as Earth and Tobias Turley as Humanity. It was hugely popular and ultimately made its first transfer to London, where it played at the Southwark Playhouse Elephant. It is the first production to transfer to the city from Birmingham’s in-house New Musical Theatre Department, launched in 2023.

Ellie Coote co-wrote and directed Hot Mess . Her credits include 42 Balloons , which has performed in the UK as well as toured to Chicago. Music and lyrics are by Jack Godfrey. He was the winner of the Best Composer, Lyricist, or Book Writer at The Stage Debut Awards in 2024 for 42 Balloons .

Hot Mess will make you excitedly reconsider your relationship with Earth, backed by the punchiest new music available for musical theatre fans! Book your tickets to experience this exceptionally brilliant new musical launch into the hearts of new audiences this year.

shows.title: I'm Every Woman
shows.title_norm: im every woman the chaka khan musical

sources.title_as_listed: I’m Every Woman – The Chaka Khan Musical
I'm Every Woman - The Chaka Khan Musical
I'm Every Woman: The Chaka Khan Musical

shows.description:
Get ready to groove as I'm Every Woman: The Chaka Khan Musical comes to Wembley Park Theatre, right next to Wembley Stadium, this summer. This dazzling new jukebox musical celebrates the life and legacy of the ten-time Grammy Award-winning icon, Chaka Khan, in a strictly limited run. Don't miss your chance to witness the story of a music legend come to life on stage - book your tickets today.

I'm Every Woman delves into the extraordinary life of Chaka Khan, tracing her journey from her early days in Chicago to international stardom. The musical explores her time with the funk band Rufus, her solo career, and her collaborations with music legends like Prince, Stevie Wonder, and Joni Mitchell. The show also delves into her activism, personal struggles, and triumphs, offering an intimate look at the woman behind the music.

Audiences will be treated to a soundtrack of Chaka's greatest hits, including "I Feel For You," "Ain't Nobody," "Sweet Thing," and, of course, "I'm Every Woman”. Blending powerful storytelling and iconic music, I'm Every Woman is a celebration of resilience, passion, and the enduring impact of a true musical icon.

Music and lyrics are by Chaka Khan.

The book is by Nia T. Hill. Hill is an award-winning writer, producer, and director whose credits span theatre, television, and film. She produced and toured Tyler Perry’s first musical I Know I’ve Been Changed , and co-founded Strange Fruit Media, winning an NAACP Image Award for Sunday Best and a Grammy Award for the song "Jesus" performed by Le’Andria Johnson. She has served as creative director for Chaka Khan, producing international concerts and new studio work.

Racky Plews directs. Plews is an award-winning creative whose credits include American Idiot , Footloose , and Josephine Baker . She has also choreographed for the BBC’s The Famous Five.

Choreography is by Jade Hackett. Hackett’s credits include Miss Saigon (Sheffield Crucible), Hex (National Theatre), and Get Up Stand Up! The Bob Marley Musical (West End).

Chaka Khan - Alexandra Burke

Since winning the fifth series of X Factor in 2008, Alexandra Burke has hit Number One in the UK Charts and appeared in several stage productions, including The Bodyguard, Sister Act and The Addams Family .

Further casting includes:

Born Yvette Marie Stevens, Chaka Khan is an American singer whose career spans over five decades. She rose to fame in the 1970s as the lead vocalist of the funk band Rufus, delivering hits like "Tell Me Something Good" and "Ain't Nobody." Embarking on a solo career in 1978, she achieved success with songs such as "I'm Every Woman" and "I Feel for You." Known as the "Queen of Funk," Khan has sold approximately 70 million records worldwide and won ten Grammy Awards. In 2023, she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, recognising her significant contributions to music.

With 22 albums, 25 Billboard-charted songs, and over 70 million records sold, Khan's influence on pop, soul, jazz, and funk is undeniable. I'm Every Woman marks the first time Khan's life will be explored on stage - her passion for civil rights, her struggles with addiction and against a toxic music industry, and her triumphs as a working woman.

Nobody does it better than Chaka Khan! So put on your dancing shoes and shimmy on down to Wembley Park Theatre. You won't want to miss the chance to see the powerful, inspirational and uplifting story of a true music legend as you’ve never seen it before. Book your tickets for I'm Every Woman: The Chaka Khan Musical today.

shows.title: Iphigénie En Tauride

sources.title_as_listed: Iphigenie en Tauride - English National Opera

shows.description:
Iphigenie en Tauride , the rarely performed masterwork opera by Christoph Gluck, makes its English National Opera debut at the London Coliseum, in the heart of Leicester Square. Performed in the original French, this brand new staging is directed by Olivier Award-winner Lindsey Turner. Based on the play by Euripides, this stirring opera tells the story of two siblings who must fight their fate to reunite. Book your tickets today.

Iphigene and her brother Orestes are part of an ancient family, the inheritors of a bloody legacy that dates back to the dawn of time itself. The siblings are separated: Iphegene stranded on a remote island at the world's end, at the beck and call of a terrifying ruler, and Orestes is brought to the brink of madness. Both fear the other is dead, but dream of someday returning home.

When an enigmatic stranger washes up on the shores of Iphegenie's island, bringing news of the collapse of her family, the hope that she will someday see her brother again is shattered, and she believes the worst must have happened. But there may be more to the stranger than it first seems, and the situation is perhaps not quite as hopeless as Iphigenie fears…

Based on the Ancient Greek play Iphigenia in Tauris by Euripides, the Opera premiered in 1779 at the Paris Opera to critical acclaim. Gluck later created a German version in 1781 to celebrate the visit of the Russian Grand Duke Paul to Vienna. This remains Gluck's only opera in German. In 1889, a new German arrangement was made by Richard Strauss, which is more frequently performed than Gluck’s original. Widely regarded as Gluck’s most important work, this new staging of Gluck’s rarely performed gem, in the original French, marks the production's ENO debut.

Iphigenie en Tauride is composed by Christoph Gluck ( Orfeo ed Euridice, Alceste ), with an original French libretto by Nicolas-François Guillard ( Arvire et Evelina, La Mort d'Adam ). Baroque specialist David Bates ( Die Zauberflote, Dido and Aeneas ) conducts, making his ENO debut. Olivier winner Lyndsey Turner ( The Crucible, Chimerica ) directs.

Don’t miss this rarely staged masterpiece, as Gluck’s most powerful and important opera, makes its ENO debut in a brand new staging, with an award-winning creative team. This production has a strictly limited run - so secure your tickets for Iphigenie en Tauride at the London Coliseum today.

shows.title: Ivanov
shows.description:
Hollywood superstar Chris Pine makes his London Theatre debut in Ivanov , the brand new adaptation from award-winning writer and director Simon Stone. This bold reimagining of Anton Chekhov's comic drama about the trials and tribulations of the melancholic Nikolai Ivanov comes to London for a strictly limited run, debuting at the Bridge Theatre just by the iconic Tower Bridge. Dont miss out - secure your tickets today!

Has Nikolai Ivanov ever been happy? Or has he just forgotten how? Despite his flourishing career and his loving marriage, Nikolai can’t help but feel like his world is falling apart. Could it be his ever-growing debts, the distaste of his parents-in-law, his relentless partying, or perhaps the mysterious illness plaguing his wife that is causing his melancholy? Or does he just need to get it together and rediscover his lust for life? When Nikolai heads to a party at his friend’s, the Lebedevs, it seems like the perfect chance to shake off his worries and get his groove back.

But as Nikolai stumbles from mishap to mishap, trying to put on a happy face, something unexpected causes his fortunes to begin looking up - an affair. In the fallout of his infidelity, can Nikolai turn his life around, save his marriage, fix his career and restore his will to live all in one fell swoop?

Ivanov was written in 1887, when Anton Chekov was commissioned to write a comedy for the Korsh Theatre, Moscow. Instead, Chekov wrote Ivanov, which was initially a drama, in only ten days. After the play’s debut, Chekhov undertook extensive rewrites, displeased with the work, and it later premiered fully in St. Petersburg in 1889, in its current dramatic-comedy form.

The play has since had many revivals, adaptations, translations and reinterpretations, including productions adapted by David Harrower for the Almeida and Chichester Festival Theatre, by David Hare for the Vivian Beaumont Theatre, New York, and by Tom Stoppard for Wyndham’s Theatre, which starred Kenneth Branagh. This bold new reimagining from writer-director Simon Stone explores all the highs and lows of Chekhov's original while firmly transplanting the action into modern day.

Chris Pine stars as Nikolai Ivanov. Pine is an Emmy-nominated American actor and director, best known for his roles as James T Kirk in the Star Trek reboot film series and as Steve Trevor in the Wonder Woman film franchise. His other credits include Don’t Worry Darling, Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, Just My Luck , and Poolman , which he co-wrote and directed. Ivanov marks Pine’s London theatre debut

Further casting is to be announced.

Ivanov is written and directed by Simon Stone, after Chekhov. Stone is an Olivier award-winning Australian writer, director and producer. Stone is best known for his bold, modern adaptations of classic plays. His adaptations include Phaedra for the National Theatre, Yerma starring Billie Piper, for the Young Vic, Medea for Ivo van Hove's company Internationaal Theater and The Lady From the Sea for the Bridge Theatre, starring Alicia Vikander.

Ivanov is presented by London Theatre Company in collaboration with Wouter van Ransbeek

Things might be rough for Nikolai Ivanov, but they’re certainly looking up for theatre goers, who get the chance see Hollywood royalty Chris Pine making his London stage debut! Secure your place today for this witty, keenly observed comic-drama from the award-winning team behind The Lady from The Sea - book tickets for Ivanov at the Bridge Theatre!

shows.title: Jeeves Takes Charge
shows.description:
First seen 45 years ago, the unexpected theatrical phenomenon, Jeeves Takes Charge , returns to the stage for a limited season this summer. Playing at the Charing Cross Theatre, close to The Strand, this comedy play is an “absolute treat” (Bath Echo) for anyone wanting to experience P. G. Wodehouse’s gloriously absurd world. Brought to life in a tour-de-force performance by Sam Harrison - secure your tickets today!

Adapted by James Duke, Edward Duke and Hugh Woolridge, Jeeves Takes Charge transports us to a world of country houses, terrifying aunts, engagements gone wrong and gentlemanly panic. Based on a short story by P.G. Wodehouse published in 1916, meet the unfortunate Bertie Wooster, who is steered away from disaster – and an engagement to Lady Florence Craye – at every turn by the brilliantly resourceful valet Jeeves.

Jeeves Takes Charge first debuted in London in 1980 by Barbara Dickson and Bernard Theobald with Andrew Lloyd Webber and Cameron Mackintosh. It earned an Olivier Award for Edward Duke’s performance as Most Promising Newcomer. There was a subsequent production at the Lyric Theatre, Hammersmith.

The latest production, which also starred Sam Harrison, opened at the Theatre Royal Bath before acclaimed runs at the Jermyn Street Theatre and Tabard Theatre. This new staging at the Charing Cross Theatre, for a limited time, will precede a UK tour in 2027.

Sam Harrison brings to life twenty-two characters in this one-man adaptation show, heading to London’s Charing Cross Theatre. He is a West End, Chichester and RSC favourite with credits including The Magician’s Elephant , Les Miserables and Chitty Chitty Bang Bang .

Hugh Woolridge directs the production. His directing credits include Chess in Concert, Sondheim Tonight , and the last staging of Jeeves Takes Charge at Theatre Royal Bath in 2024.

The rest of the creative team includes scenic design by Caite Hevner, lighting design by Tim Mitchell, and sound design by Paul Groothuis.

This summer, take a trip to experience the warmth, silliness and sheer brilliance of P. G. Wodehouse’s writing during this limited run in the heart of London. This superb Olivier Award-winning comedy is not to be missed — book your tickets for Jeeves Takes Charge at the Charing Cross Theatre today!

shows.title: Kinky Boots
shows.description:
Everybody say yeah - Kinky Boots is back in London! Fresh from a critically acclaimed UK tour, Strictly Come Dancing star Johannes Radebe leads the cast as the larger-than-life drag queen Lola, who teams up with mild-mannered Charlie Price to help save his father's shoe factory. This joyous, award-winning musical is a “sizzling five-star masterpiece” (Chronicle Live). Strutting into the London Coliseum for a strictly limited run, read our Kinky Boots review and book your tickets today.

When Charlie Price’s father unexpectedly dies, he inherits the family business - Price and Son, a shoe factory in Northampton that is down at heel. As Charlie struggles to revive the failing business, his relationship with pushy fiancée Nicola becomes strained when she encourages him to sell the factory to a corporation that wants to turn it into flats, and Charlie is at risk of losing not only his relationship but the livelihood that meant so much to his father. Downtrodden, Charlie can think of no other solution... then in sashays Lola, a drag artist in need of a sturdy pair of heels. With the help of Lola and assembly line worker Lauren, who is harbouring a secret crush, Charlie sets to work designing the ultimate “kinky boot”, hoping to tap into a niche market and save the factory. But not everyone is happy about working with a drag queen, and Lola has troubles of her own… Will Charlie and Lola be able to save Price and Son, or will their differences cause them to stumble?

Kinky Boots is based on the 2005 film of the same name, which starred Joel Edgerton and Chiwetel Ejiofor and drew inspiration from a remarkable true story. The show premiered on Broadway in 2013 with Pose star Billy Porter playing the fabulous Lola. It snagged six Tony wins, including Best Musical, and later transferred to London’s West End, where it won three Olivier Awards. In 2014 the production won a Grammy for Best Musical Theatre Album. This fierce new revival comes to the West End following a fabulous UK tour in 2025.

South African dancer and choreographer Johannes Radebe stars as Lola. Best known as a professional on Strictly Come Dancing, in 2021 Radebe was a runner-up on the show with his partner John Whaite, as part of the first male same-sex pairing in the history of UK Strictly . Radebe made his musical theatre debut in 2025 as part of the UK tour of Kinky Boots and has previously toured with dance show Burn the Floor . He has also appeared on Doctor Who , RuPaul's Drag Race: UK vs. the World , Celebrity Masterchef and The Great British Sewing Bee .

Further casting for the West End transfer is to be confirmed.

Kinky Boots has a book by Harvey Fierstein, based on the screenplay by Geoff Deane and Tim Firth, with music and lyrics by Cyndi Lauper. Nikolai Foster directs.

Harvey Fierstein is a Tony Award-winning American actor, playwright, and screenwriter. One of the first openly gay celebrities in Hollywood, Fierstein is a trailblazer and LGBTQ+ activist. His credits include Torch Song Trilogy , La Cage aux Folles and Newsies . In 2007, Fierstein was inducted into the American Theatre Hall of Fame, and in 2025 he was awarded a Lifetime Achievement Tony Award.

Cyndi Lauper is an American singer, songwriter and actress, best known for her iconic hits "Girls Just Wanna Have Fun" and "Time After Time". Lauper is a Grammy, Emmy and Tony Award winner and inductee of the Rock’n’Roll and Songwriters Hall of Fame. In 2013, she made history when she won the Tony for Best Original Score for Kinky Boots , as the first woman to win the category by herself, rather than as part of a songwriting team.

Nikolai Foster is an award-winning British-Danish theatre director and the current Artistic Director of the Curve Leicester. Foster’s credits include Billy Elliot the Musical at the Curve, Grease at the Dominion Theatre, The Wizard of Oz at the London Palladium and UK tour and A Chorus Line at Sadler’s Wells.

Fall head over heels for this energetic, feel-good musical that our Kinky Boots review describes as full of “heart and joy” It returns to London for a special limited run. Johannes Radebe is truly “mesmerising” (Chronicle Live) as Lola, so grab your glitter and get ready to strut down to the West End this Spring 2026! Don’t miss out – book your tickets for Kinky Boots at the London Coliseum today!

shows.title: La Traviata
shows.description:
Passion, music and heartbreak collide in Peter Konwitschny’s operatic masterpiece of Verdi’s iconic romantic tragedy, La Traviata. Playing at the London Coliseum, a short walk from the National Gallery, this is the perfect production for those discovering opera for the first time, whilst still offering a rich experience for seasoned enthusiasts of this art form. Secure your tickets for this unmissable opera today!

La Traviata shares the story of Violetta Valéry, a celebrated Parisian courtesan who returns to high society after an extended period of illness and discovers love with the earnest Alfredo Germont. However, they are blighted by societal pressures and personal sacrifice.

Combined with some of Verdi’s instantly recognisable melodies, such as "Let me live the life I want to (Sempre Libera)" and "Brindisi Let’s drink and be merry (Libiamo)", La Traviata is a heartbreaking drama that explores love, freedom, class and mortality.

Written in 1853, Verdi’s opera made its premiere at the La Fenice opera house in Venice later that year. Although it was initially unpopular with audiences, now it is one of the best-known works and one of the most recognisable operas, with many versions of the story being presented on stages across the world.

Recognised for having a more modernistic, minimalist lens on this story, Peter Konwitschny’s production earned an Olivier Award for Best New Opera following its premiere in 2013. “A radical reimagination of La Traviata that bursts with possibility” (Oscar Cunningham), a second revival by director Ruth Knight cemented this opera as a firm favourite with audiences.

Hailed as being radical, captivating and powerful and an exciting reinvigoration of a classic by critics, there’s no better time to experience one of the most powerful operas for the first time in the heart of London. Get ready for a sizzling Shakespeare summer in London with this brand new production of Love’s Labour’s Lost at Shakespeare’s Globe on Bankside. In sun‑drenched Navarre, four noble lords swear off love and all worldly pleasures in pursuit of study and self‑discipline. Their plans are joyously derailed when the Princess of France and her spirited entourage arrive on a diplomatic mission, bringing wit, music, and irresistible allure.

This brand new production of Shakespeare's playful, lyrical comedy infuses this rarely staged gem with the vibrant spirit of flamenco in a tale of oaths, desires, and the inevitable havoc love wreaks on even the most resolved hearts.

Written in the late 1590s, Love’s Labour’s Lost is celebrated for its energetic wordplay, intricate rhymes, and youthful wit. Though less frequently staged than Shakespeare’s greatest hits, the play has enjoyed notable productions over the centuries, including a 2009 Globe staging directed by former Globe Artistic Director Dominic Dromgoole.

This summer’s production embraces that rich tradition while offering a bold contemporary twist, inviting audiences to experience Shakespeare’s joyous celebration of language, love and the human heart in one of the world’s most iconic theatrical spaces.

Casting for this production is to be announced.

Love’s Labour’s Lost is written by William Shakespeare.

This production is directed by Indiana Lown‑Collins ( The Solid Life of Sugar Water ), making her Globe debut following her time as a Resident Artist and JMK Award winner.

Set and costume design is by Katie Lias ( Much Ado About Nothing ), with movement direction from Carmen Igarza ( Manolita Chen ), infusing the production with flamenco-inspired physicality.

shows.title: Mother Courage and Her Children
shows.description:
Witness history this summer as Mother Courage and Her Children comes to Shakespeare’s Globe, on vibrant Bankside. This visceral staging of Bertolt Brecht’s timeless epic about survival, commerce and the cost of conflict marks the first time this revolutionary playwright’s work has been staged at the Globe Theatre. This ambitious staging of one of Brecht’s masterwork play invites audiences into a world where war is not just a backdrop but the engine of life itself - secure your tickets for this remarkable production today.

Following the devastation of the Thirty Years’ War, Mother Courage hauls her war‑wagon through a landscape of conflict, selling supplies to soldiers and trying to keep her three children safe, even as the violent world around her exacts a devastating toll. Mother Courage will do whatever it takes to survive - but in the business of war, everything has a cost. Is she willing to pay the price?

This Globe production interrogates the brutal economics of conflict with live music, urgent performances and Brecht’s epic theatrical style, asking audiences to consider not just the horrors of war but the systems that perpetuate it. With humour, resilience and startling emotional depth, this staging brings Brecht’s incisive storytelling vividly to life beneath the London sky.

Written by Bertolt Brecht in 1939, Mother Courage and Her Children first debuted in 1941 in Zurich. Several productions have been staged since, many of which were directed by Brecht himself. In 1961, several years after Brecht's death, the play was adapted as a German film, Mutter Courage und ihre Kinder, starring Helene Weigel, Brecht's widow.

Considered a cornerstone of Brecht’s epic theatre, the play uses techniques that encourage reflection over mere emotional identification, blending music, direct address and episodic scenes to challenge audiences to think as much as feel. Mother Courage has remained an enduring indictment of war and profiteering, celebrated for its political force and theatrical innovation, and this blistering new staging marks a historic occasion for the Globe, as this production becomes the first ever staging of Brecht’s masterwork on its stage.

Michelle Terry stars as Mother Courage. Terry is an actor, writer and the Artistic Director of Shakespeare’s Globe. She has performed leading roles in numerous Globe productions, including Hamlet, The Merry Wives of Windsor , and As You Like It , as well as many roles at other prestigious venues, including the National Theatre, RSC, and Royal Court.

Further casting includes:

Mother Courage and Her Children is written by Bertolt Brecht, with significant contributions by Margarete Steffin. Brecht (1898–1956) was a German playwright, poet and director. His most influential works include The Threepenny Opera with composer Kurt Weill, The Caucasian Chalk Circle , and The Life of Galileo . Brecht’s techniques, including direct address, visible staging, and songs, reshaped 20th-century theatre and continue to influence political and socially engaged performance today.

Bruntwood Prize winner and Succession writer Anna Jordan provides the English translation. Her other credits include Yen , Lost Atoms, Becoming Elizabeth, One Day for Netflix and Killing Eve .

The production is directed by Globe Associate Artist Elle While ( A Midsummer Night’s Dream, Hamlet ). Music is composed by James Maloney ( Much Ado About Nothing, A Very Very Very Dark Matter ), with set and costume design by takis ( Wicked, A Midsummer Night's Dream ).

Witness a Globe Theatre first as Mother Courage and Her Children storms the yard with humanity, protest and unflinching theatrical power. Whether you’re drawn by Brecht’s epic vision, Michelle Terry’s commanding performance, or the Globe’s iconic setting, this production promises to resonate deeply. Don’t miss this chance to experience one of theatre’s greatest works at one of London’s most remarkable venues - book your tickets for Mother Courage and Her Children at Shakespeare’s Globe!

shows.title: Much Ado About Nothing
shows.description:
Lovers fight and make up, and mischievous plots are unravelled as Shakespeare’s hilarious comedy Much Ado About Nothing returns to Shakespeare’s Globe Theatre on the banks of the Thames. This timeless tale of love conquering all and the iconic battle of wits between Benedick and Beatrice is one of Shakespeare’s best-known works, and this brand-new production transplants the action to a world of late-night parties, style and status. Much Ado is the perfect play to enjoy in London this summer - secure your tickets today.

Years of war are finally over, and the soldiers are standing down. But in image-obsessed Messina, nothing is quite as it seems - and gossip, plotting, and mind-games are soon afoot. Young lovers Claudio and Hero, and sharp-tongued singletons Beatrice and Benedick, are about to discover that their idyllic surroundings are the setting for a series of deceptions that might end in tragedy. And while the war may be over, the battle for true love has just begun...

Shakespeare’s celebration of love and redemption is the ultimate original rom-com! With sharp wit, laugh-out-loud arguments, and heartwarming romance, you'll be swept up in this timeless tale of love in all its forms.

Much Ado About Nothing is one of William Shakespeare’s most popular and frequently performed comedies. Believed to have been written in 1598 or 1599, the play was likely first performed at the newly built Globe Theatre in London. Blending witty romantic sparring with darker themes of deception and honour, the play explores misunderstandings, mistaken identities, and clever wordplay.

Its enduring appeal lies in its balance of sharp humour and emotional depth, particularly in the fiery love-hate dynamic between Beatrice and Benedick, with acclaimed actors such as Kenneth Branagh and Emma Thompson, David Tennant and Catherine Tate, and Vanessa Redgrave and James Earl Jones tackling the roles of the quarrelling lovers.

Much Ado About Nothing was first published in quarto form in 1600, and has remained a staple of the stage ever since, with stagings spanning from David Garrick’s 18th-century productions to notable modern interpretations, including acclaimed film adaptations, including Kenneth Branagh’s 1993 version (which also starred Keanu Reeves and Denzel Washington), and Buffy creator Joss Whedon’s 2012 version.

Casting for this production includes:

Much Ado About Nothing is written by William Shakespeare.

Chelsea Walker directs. Walker is an award-winning director whose credits include the recent stage adaptation of The Da Vinci Code , All’s Well That Ends Well, and Hedda Gabler . Design is by Sami Fendall ( Brigadoon, Hamlet ), with music by composer, multi-instrumentalist and recording artist Angus MacRae ( Mrs Warren’s Profession, Cabaret on Broadway).

Sigh no more, ladies, gents and everyone in between, because you can laugh, swoon and revel in the ultimate battle of wits, romance and redemption with Much Ado About Nothing . Whether you’re a Groundling or sitting on the benches, the irrepressible joy of this ageless tale, told in a sizzling new staging, promises to be the ultimate Shakespeare experience this summer. Book tickets for Much Ado About Nothing at Shakespeare’s Globe Theatre today!

shows.title: My Neighbour Totoro
shows.description:
‘Wow is too small a word!’ (Broadway World). The ‘jaw-dropping’ (Metro) multi-award-winning MY NEIGHBOUR TOTORO will soon be closing in the Gillian Lynne Theatre in the West End – MUST END 10 JAN 2027

Find your spirit with this ‘profoundly magical experience’ (Elle) and winner of six Olivier Awards, as the five-star, widely acclaimed adaptation of Studio Ghibli’s animated feature film appears on stage at the Gillian Lynne Theatre.

With ‘blockbuster awe-inspiring puppets’ (Time Out) from Puppetry Director & Designer Basil Twist and Puppetry Associate Mervyn Millar (War Horse), MY NEIGHBOUR TOTORO is brought to you by the Royal Shakespeare Company and Executive Producer Joe Hisaishi – in collaboration with Improbable and Nippon TV – and adapted by Tom Morton-Smith (Oppenheimer) with direction from Phelim McDermott.

From 10 March 2026, Helen Chong will join the company, making her West End principal debut as Satsuki.

Discover this ‘huge, healing hug of a show’ (The Stage) and book your MY NEIGHBOUR TOTORO theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

What is My Neighbour Totoro about?

Join sisters Satsuki and Mei as they move to their curious new home in the countryside. Exploring their unfamiliar surroundings, they soon encounter a world of spirits, sprites and magical creatures. Maybe it was all a dream? Or perhaps they really are now friends with the giant, ancient protector of the forest named ‘Totoro‘ and his friend the ‘Catbus‘…

Ticket Information

shows.title: My Son's A Queer, But What Can You Do

sources.title_as_listed: My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?)
My Son's A Queer (But What Can You Do?)
My Son’s a Queer (But What Can You Do?)
My Son's A Queer, But What Can You Do

shows.description:
Known for blending queer joy with theatrical nostalgia, Rob Madge’s My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?) heads to the Apollo Theatre, near Piccadilly Circus tube station. Get ready to participate in the ultimate Disney parade and experience a heartfelt story about growing up, identity, and unconditional support. Purchase your tickets now for the “Triumphant and transformative” (The Stage) Olivier Award-nominated show on its welcome return to the West End – just don’t forget to pack your tissues!

Armed with costumes, props, and wigs, 12-year-old Rob Madge creates a Disney parade in their living room. Rob confidently plays characters like Mary Poppins, Ariel, Mickey Mouse, and Belle, even though their parents struggle to keep up. Despite their challenges, Rob's parents' unwavering support highlights the importance of encouragement. Through a treasure trove of home videos and theatrical magic, My Son’s a Queer is a sparkling show that captured the hearts of people worldwide with its gorgeous celebration of the parents who simply say “yes”.

My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?) makes its stage debut at the Turbine Theatre in 2021, where it won the WhatsOnStage Award for Best Off-West End. It went on to play at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 2021, before having two West End runs at the Garrick and Ambassadors Theatre.

Its transfer to Broadway in 2024 was initially cancelled, with a UK tour taking its place. The rescheduled season at the New York City Center took place in 2025.

Rob Madge stars in this one-man autobiographical show, My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?) . Their theatre credits include Acorn Antiques , Cabaret and Mary Poppins . They have become a seasoned performer in the London Palladium pantomime over the last couple of years and will be starring in this year’s production of Sleeping Beauty.

Madge has also started writing some new productions, including Charley’s Aunt at the Watermill Theatre and Bank of Dave – The Musical , which premieres with a run at The Lowry, Salford and Curve Theatre, Leicester in 2026.

Written by Rob Madge, the show features music composed by Pippa Cleary and lyrics by Madge and Cleary. Pippa Cleary is an acclaimed musical theatre composer, with credits including The Great British Bake Off Musical and T he Secret Diary of Adrian Mole Aged 13¾ The Musical. She’s working with Rob Madge on Bank of Dave – The Musical.

My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?) is a lively show that provides a memorable “insight into the lives of those who commit to defying society’s ‘norms’ and make the world a better place for it” (Musical Theatre Review). Get your tickets for My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?) at the Apollo Theatre and enjoy this special, uplifting theatrical experience firsthand!

shows.title: Now You See Me Live
shows.description:
Experience an explosive mix of high-tech illusions, solo stunts, and jaw-dropping spectacles as Now You See Me Live arrives at the London Coliseum, the largest theatre in London’s West End. Located on St Martin's Lane in the heart of theatreland, Now You See Me is inspired by the blockbuster franchise and delivers a “high-energy blend of wonder and humour” (Broadway World) this summer.

Now You See Me is presented by a world-class music ensemble inspired by the film’s characters, the ‘Four Horsemen’. During the cutting-edge production, the performers will stun audiences with their unbelievable skills but also with the addition of some shocking twists and grand feats of illusion.

The film franchise which this show is influenced by was first released in 2013. Although it was met with mixed reviews initially, it became a box office success and earned the People’s Choice Award for Favorite Thriller Movie. A sequel was released in 2016, followed by a third installment, Now You See Me: Now You Don’t which came out in November 2025.

The Now You See Me live production has been hugely successful, having performed thousands of shows across the world. They have sold out shows in Australia, Asia, Las Vegas and Broadway. Now it heads to the UK for a limited five-week summer season at the London Coliseum.

Now You See Me is brought to the stage by the team behind Broadway’s record-breaking hit The Illusionists . Simon Painter and Adam Trent are co-creators, whilst Painter is joined by Tim Lawson as Executive Producer. Ash Jacks McCready is the creative and staging director, Kirsty White is the creative director, and Enzo Wenye is the illusion director.

The show is co-produced by Runaway Entertainment, BOS Productions and Timothy Laczynski.

If you’re looking for a production to blow your mind this summer, the UK premiere of Now You See Me Live at the London Coliseum is must-see. See the boundaries of state magic get pushed to the absolute edge and be left in awe by all that this show has to offer.

shows.title: Nutcracker
shows.description:
Escape into a world of whimsy, magic and incredible dancing this winter as The Nutcracker returns to St Martin's Lane's historic London Coliseum for its annual festive season. The classic ballet has been a staple of Christmas theatre in London for over 50 years, and English National Ballet Artistic Director Aaron S. Watkin’s new version promises to keep the spirit alive. Anything is possible in this enchanting production, so book your tickets early for a spot in the audience this year.

It is a cold and frosty Christmas Eve in Edwardian London, and Clara is unwrapping a special present. As the paper falls off, an enchanted Nutcracker appears and whisks her off on a spellbinding adventure. In this magical new world, Clara meets handsome strangers, comes face-to-face with the terrifying Mouse King, and drifts high above the Land of Snow in a hot air balloon. Exquisite dance, soaring music from Tchaikovsky and gorgeous visual storytelling make The Nutcracker a pure spectacle that will delight all ages, as an array of wonderful characters leap, pirouette and glide across the stage.

This year, enjoy a new re-telling of the classic tale, as world-class dancers and musicians transform the Coliseum into a winter wonderland. English National Ballet’s Artistic Director Aaron S. Watkin and Olivier Award-winner Arielle Smith choreograph a dance extravaganza, with sets and costumes designed by Dick Bird. As Clara absconds from her London home into a technicolour new world populated by the beautiful Sugar Plum Fairy and handsome Cavalier, a rush of excitement and possibility sends a thrill through the auditorium.

Russian composer Tchaikovsky wrote The Nutcracker’s score, and even those newest to ballet and classical music will be familiar with the lively notes of “Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy” and “The Nutcracker Suite”. There is no better place to hear the opening notes and soaring melodies of this world-famous work than at the beautiful London Coliseum. Even five decades on, the dynamic mix of dance and music is still an exhilarating experience for theatregoers, who return time after time to enjoy the enduring magic of this award-winning production.

This magnificent ballet has kept audiences rapt with wonder for generations, and for many, it marks the beginning of the most wonderful time of the year! Avoid disappointment and secure your Nutcracker tickets now; this is a sell-out year on year.

shows.title: Oh, Mary!
shows.description:
Oh, Mary! is a hilarious dark comedy that puts First Lady, Mary Todd Lincoln, firmly in the spotlight, telling the story of this famous couple as you’ve never seen them before. Written by Tony Award winner, Pulitzer finalist and self-proclaimed idiot Cole Escola, this hilarious spoof history play dazzled audiences in New York, and London audiences can finally enjoy this “rude, crude, darkly funny, deeply silly” (SeatPlan) show as Oh, Mary! comes to the West End's Trafalgar Theatre, just off Whitehall, at last. Check out our Oh, Mary! review and book your tickets today!

Think you know the story of Abraham Lincoln, his wife Mary Todd Lincoln, and the assassination that rocked a nation? Think again! While everyone might know the story of the American President, who exactly was Mary? Known in the history books as Abraham Lincoln’s wife and mother to his children, the IRL MLT was a troubled and somewhat controversial figure whose life was marred by grief and mental illness.

This riotous black comedy puts a satirical slant on the troubles of this lesser-known First Lady, and runs fast and loose with the facts to shed a queer new light on a not-quite-so-honest Abe. Deliciously dark and sharply satirical, Oh, Mary! uncovers the unrequited yearnings, alcoholism and buried desires of Mrs Lincoln in the weeks leading up to her husband’s assassination, and asks - what were Mary’s dreams when she wasn’t standing dutifully by as First Lady?

Oh Mary! is “the best kind of stupid: a broad, wildly funny comedy that spits in the face of American history” (Variety). The show premiered off-Broadway at the Lucile Lortell Theatre in February 2024 to critical acclaim, receiving several extensions and later transferring to Broadway’s Lyceum Theatre. The show won an Outer Critics Circle Award and an Obie for its off-Broadway run and went on to snatch two Tonys, a GLAAD Media Award and a Drama League Award during its (still ongoing) Broadway run, and was a finalist for the 2025 Pulitzer Prize for Drama.

Main cast:

Catherine Tate stars as Mary Todd Lincoln until 18 July 2026. Her credits include Doctor Who and The Catherine Tate Show on television, and Much Ado About Nothing, opposite David Tennant, on stage.

Performers who have donned MLT’s iconic “brat curls” wig in New York include writer and creator Cole Escola, who originated the role (and won the Tony Award for Best Leading Actor in a Play), star of The Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt and Emmy nominee Titus Burgess, two-time RuPaul's Drag Race w inner and Broadway sensation Jinkx Monsoon, Emmy nominee and star of Netflix’s GLOW Betty Gilpen, and Tony winner and 30 Rock star Jane Krakowski.

Oh, Mary! is written and created by Cole Escola. Escola is a Tony and Writers Guild of America Award-winning writer and performer, and a Pulitzer finalist. Their credits include Difficult People, Hacks, At Home With Amy Sedaris and The Other Two .

The original New York production was directed by Tony Award-winning director and choreographer Sam Pinkleton. Pinkleton’s credits include Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812, La Cage Aux Follies, Can I Be Frank , and choreography on Stephen Sondheim’s final show Here We Are .

Oh, Mary! is a “smartly stupid riot” (Variety). Enjoy the story of the Lincolns told from a hilarious, farcical and bold new perspective - just don’t expect historical accuracy! Oh, Mary! pushes President Lincoln out of the limelight and turns it on to one of US history’s most overlooked figures. Don’t miss out on this witty, wild and “gleefully irreverent comedy” (Time Out) - Book your tickets for Oh, Mary! at the Trafalgar Theatre today!

shows.title: Oliver!
shows.description:
Oliver! can consider itself part of the West End family once more! Lionel Bart’s “musical masterpiece” (Sunday Times) is breathtakingly reconceived by producer Cameron Mackintosh and award-winning director and choreographer Matthew Bourne ( Nutcracker! ) in this intimate and imaginative new production. Whether you have seen it before or are ready to experience it for the very first time, the story of the boy who dared to ask for more is pure magic. Read our Oliver! review , now playing at Shaftsbury Avenue's Gielgud Theatre.

When young orphan Oliver escapes the harsh Victorian workhouse, he is taken under the wing of one of London’s most lively gangs. Led by wily Fagin and the Artful Dodger, Oliver joins a team of light-fingered pickpockets and finds a friend in warm-hearted Nancy. But when he is wrongly arrested for stealing, Oliver’s new life and rag-tag family come under threat… until an unexpected saviour shows him that true happiness might be just around the corner.

Based on Charles Dickens’ Oliver Twist , Lionel Bart’s Oliver! is one of the most beloved shows of all time, and its sensational score - including “Food Glorious Food”, “Consider Yourself”, “You’ve Got to Pick-a-Pocket or Two”, “I’d Do Anything”, “Oom Pah Pah” and “As Long As He Needs Me” - and vivid storytelling have made it the gateway to musical theatre for generations of children. Since debuting at Wimbledon Theatre in 1960, it has played to sold-out crowds in London and on Broadway, toured the UK and been adapted into an Academy Award-winning film.

Powerhouse producer Cameron Mackintosh and Olivier Award-winning director/choreographer Matthew Bourne have collaborated on this thrilling revival of Lionel Bart’s musical, which is in London direct from its premiere at Chichester Festival Theatre. Read our review of Oliver at the Gielgud Theatre .

The duo are responsible for some of UK theatre’s biggest productions: Mackintosh has driven the success of Les Miserables , The Phantom of the Opera and Mary Poppins , whilst Bourne’s bright and bold ballets including Nutcracker! and The Red Shoes are genre-defining spectacles that audiences return to again and again.

Main cast:

Who will buy Oliver musical tickets? Everyone! It is one of the greatest shows of all time and a crowd-pleaser that never fails to make your heart swell and tears flow. Rediscover the magic or experience it as a family as it returns to London for an unforgettable new season.

shows.title: Paddington The Musical
shows.description:
Get ready for a most wonderful adventure, as Paddington The Musical comes to London’s Savoy Theatre. This heartwarming new musical tells the story of everyone’s favourite bear as you’ve never seen him before. So book your tickets today and join Paddington as he finds a new home in London - just be sure to pack plenty of marmalade sandwiches!

When his Aunt Lucy retires to a Home for Retired Bears, a young spectacled bear travels to London from his homeland of Peru, seeking a new home. With only a hat, coat and a case full of marmalade sandwiches to his name, the bear is lost, afraid, and lonely. When the Brown family meet the cub at Paddington station, with a note that reads “Please look after this bear” pinned to his lapel, they bring him along to their house in Windsor Gardens, despite Mr. Brown’s misgivings.

Though Paddington causes plenty of mishaps and hijinks, he soon settles into his new life in England. But, Paddington discovers that London isn't all polite smiles and cups of tea, and that the Brown family have plenty of problems of their own. When a sinister villain appears, putting Paddington’s life at risk, the Browns must decide just how far they’re willing to go to make this special little bear a part of the family.

First appearing in 1958 in the children's book A Bear Called Paddington by Michael Bond, Paddington has since become one of the most beloved fictional characters in the UK. As well as 29 best-selling books starring the precocious little bear, Paddington has also appeared in commercials, an immersive experience and even in a skit with Queen Elizabeth II as part of the Platinum Party at the Palace. Bond’s books have been adapted into multiple animated TV series, as well as a BAFTA-winning film series starring Ben Whishaw as the voice of Paddington.

This brand new musical is based on Bond’s popular book series and shows the much-loved character as you’ve never seen him before, so don’t miss out - secure your tickets today!

Paddington The Musical has music and lyrics by Tom Fletcher, with a book by Jessica Swale. The show is directed by Luke Sheppard.

A songwriter, vlogger, children’s author and musician, Fletcher is perhaps best known as one of the lead vocalists of pop band McFly. As a songwriter, Fletcher has written 10 number one singles, penning hits for bands including One Direction, Busted, and 5 Seconds of Summer. He has previously written the music and lyrics for adaptations of his children's books The Creakers and The Dinosaur that Pooped.

Jessica Swale is an Olivier Award-winning playwright, director and screenwriter. Her work includes the screenplay for Summerland , the play Blue Stockings at Shakespeare’s Globe, Nell Gwyn at the Globe and in the West End and The Overwhelming at the Royal National Theatre.

Luke Sheppard is an Olivier and Tony Award-nominated director. His previous credits include Starlight Express , In the Heights , Billionaire Boy and My Son’s a Queer (But What Can You Do?).

The musical is adapted from A Bear Called Paddington , the first book in the Paddington series, by Michael Bond (1925-2017). Bond was a popular children's author and screenwriter. As well as penning over 29 Paddington books - the last of which was published posthumously in 2018 - Bond is the author of the Olga da Polga series, the Monsieur Pamplemousse series, Here Comes Thursday and many more. Bond held both an OBE and a CBE for his services to children's literature, and sold over 35 million copies of the Paddington books worldwide.

Main cast:

No! Paddington Bear is played by two people who work together to bring the marmalade-munching bear to life. Arti Shah ( Star Wars, Attack the Block, Guardians of the Galaxy ) is in costume, performing movement and choreography, and James Hameed is the "off-stage performer" providing the voice and remotely controlled facial expressions. The alternate Paddington on-stage performers are Abbie Purvis and Ali Sarebani.

So come and join this little bear on a very big adventure! Paddington The Musical is an uplifting, hilarious and moving new show jam-packed (or should we say marmalade-packed?) with dazzling choreography, catchy songs and plenty of heart. Book tickets for Paddington at the Savoy Theatre today and see this iconic cultural figure like never before!

shows.title: Paranormal Activity
shows.description:
Are you brave enough? Paranormal Activity , a new story set in the world of the terrifying supernatural horror film series of the same name, comes to the Ambassadors Theatre for a strictly limited run this winter. This “terrifyingly good” (The Reviews Hub) play about an American couple who relocate to London, only to find their haunted past has followed them overseas, will have you on the edge of your seat. Only the fearless need book - secure your tickets today, if you dare.

When American couple Jamie and Lou are offered an opportunity to move to London for work, they jump at the chance to relocate from their native Chicago. Hoping to escape their troubled history, the couple are eager to turn over a new leaf, to shake off the demons of their past and have a fresh start. But when sinister occurrences begin to happen in their new London home, the couple soon learn that houses aren’t haunted - people are, and the past might not be as easy to leave behind as they had hoped…

A brand new original story, set in the spine-tingling world of the Paranormal Activity film franchise, the production premiered in 2024 at the Leeds Playhouse and will have a short tour of several US cities before coming to London’s West End for a strictly limited run. Combining innovative stagecraft with psychological horror, Paranormal Activity is sure to haunt you long after you’ve left the theatre - book your tickets today.

The Leeds Playhouse premiere of the show featured Patrick Hesuinger ( Gossip Girl, Black Swan ) as James and Melissa James ( Wheel of Time, Moulin Rouge! The Musical ) as Lou, who both return to their roles in the West End.

Joining them are Jackie Morrison as Etheline Cotgrave and Pippa Winslow as Carolanne.

Paranormal Activity is written by Levi Holloway and directed by Felix Barrett.

Levi Holloway is an American Playwright and actor. He is the founder of Neverbird Project, a theatre company for deaf and hard-of-hearing youths. Holloway’s credits include Grey House on Broadway, Turret and The Haven Place .

Felix Barret is an award-winning British director and the artistic director and founder of immersive theatre company Punchdrunk. Barrett’s credits include The Drowned Man: A Hollywood Fable, The Burnt City, Sleep No More in London and on Broadway, The Duchess of Malfi with English National Opera and The Third Day for HBO and Sky Atlantic. In 2016 he was awarded an MBE for his services to theatre.

Set and costume design is by Tony nominee Fly Davis ( Caroline or Change, The Ocean at the End of the Lane ) with illusion design by magician and illusionist Chris Fisher ( Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, Back to the Future the Musical ), lighting design by Anna Watson ( Giant, A Christmas Carol ), video design by Luke Halls ( The Book of Dust, The Lehman Trilogy ) and sound design by Gareth Fry ( Til The Stars Come Down, Harry Potter and the Cursed Child ).

The production is presented by Melting Pot, the minds behind the award-winning stage adaptation of The Life of Pi and terrifying shows including Ghost Stories and The Girl on the Train , in association with Leeds Playhouse, by arrangement with Paramount Pictures.

Paranormal Activity is “unnerving entertainment sure to delight” (Wharfdale Observer). Don’t miss this edge-of-your-seat thriller as it comes to the West End for a strictly limited run. Secure your tickets for Paranormal Activity at the Ambassadors Theatre today!

shows.title: Peppa Pig's Big Family Show!
shows.description:
Join Peppa Pig and your favourite family of piggies for a very special day! The beloved character and all her friends return in this delightful children’s show at the Theatre Royal Haymarket, close to Leicester Square. Jam-packed with music, fun and plenty of surprises, Peppa Pig's Big Family Show is the perfect family viewing for mummy and daddy pigs and little piglets alike! Secure your tickets for this oinksome show today!

With a new baby piglet on the way, there’s a lot to do to make sure everything is ready for the oink-dorable new arrival! Peppa Pig, George, Mummy and Daddy Pig and all their friends are rushed off their trotters as they race against the clock to ensure everything is perfect ahead of the big day. But with decorating and building still to be done, will Peppa and her family be able to get everything finished in time?

Peppa Pig has been delighting little piggies since 2004, when it first aired on Channel 5. The show has since moved to Nick Jr. and remains one of the UK's top children’s shows, as well as enjoying huge popularity overseas. The award-winning show has won several British Academy Children's Awards, and has released songs, books and been adapted into previous stage shows, video games and even theme parks. This live stage show premiered in 2025, and focuses on Peppa and her family as they prepare for a new addition to their family. Teaching children about how to cope when their family expands and how to be a good older brother or sister, Peppa Pig’s Big Family Show is a fantastic introduction to the magic of theatre for little ones!

This live show features all your favourite characters from the Peppa Pig TV show, including Peppa, her little brother George, Mummy Pig, Daddy Pig, Grandpa and Grandma Pig, and Peppa’s friends Suzy Sheep, Rebecca Rabbit, Zoe Zebra, along with many more!

Peppa Pig’s Big Family Show is produced by Fierylight, in association with Hasbro. Fierylight have produced previous Peppa Pig stage shows, including Peppa Pig’s Fun Day Out and Peppa Pig’s Best Day Ever .

Make sure to secure your tickets for this oinktastic live show, suitable for all the family! With catchy new songs, lots of adventure and loads of fantastic surprises, Peppa Pig’s Big Family Show will have the whole family snorting with laughter and tapping their trotters all the way home! So come join the Pig family in welcoming their new bundle of joy and secure your tickets for Peppa Pig’s Big Family Show at the Theatre Royal Haymarket today!

shows.title: Phantom Of The Opera
shows.description:
Experience the thrill of the West End’s most haunting love story, as PHANTOM OF THE OPERA musical enters its 40th year, marking four extraordinary decades at His Majesty’s Theatre.

Cameron Mackintosh’s production of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s PHANTOM OF THE OPERA is widely considered one of the world’s most beautiful and spectacular musicals. Since 1986, PHANTOM OF THE OPERA has become a global phenomenon, with productions playing to 160 million people in 217 cities, 52 territories and in 23 languages. Lloyd Webber’s celebrated romantic and soaring score includes The Music of the Night, All I Ask of You, Wishing You Were Somehow Here Again, Masquerade and the iconic title song.

PHANTOM OF THE OPERA tells the haunting story of Christine Daaé, a young soprano whose extraordinary voice enchants a mysterious masked figure known as The Phantom. A brilliant yet tormented musical genius, The Phantom dwells in the depths of the Paris Opera House, casting fear over all who inhabit it.

Drawn to Christine’s sensational talent, The Phantom becomes her mentor, believing she alone can truly bring his music to life, and as he guides her from the shadows, he falls deeply and dangerously in love. When Christine is reunited with her childhood sweetheart, Raoul, now the young patron of the Opera House, she has to wrestle with the unpredictable nature of a powerful love triangle. The Phantom’s obsession with his new star sets off a dramatic turn of events where devotion, jealousy and passions collide.

See it at His Majesty’s Theatre with Dean Chisnall as The Phantom, Anna Zavelson as Christine Daaé and Ashley Gilmour as Raoul.

Book your PHANTOM OF THE OPERA London tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

Read More for soundtrack, cast & creative, age guidance and more…

Phantom of the Opera Ticket Information

shows.title: Relics
shows.description:
Relics, a dark new family drama all about the legacies we inherit, and the choices and compromises we make growing up, makes its world premiere at West London’s vibrant Lyric Hammersmith. This bold new play from up-and-coming playwright Ben Ockrent, directed by the legendary Michael Longhurst, is heartbreaking and hilarious in turn. Don't miss out - book your tickets to Relics t oday!

After the death of their mother, four siblings must come home to sift through the detritus of her life. They include bossy, bulldozing Liv, who constantly micromanages her siblings, people-pleaser Rob, who just wants them all to just get along for once, and the fed-up Michelle, who is sick of playing nice and walking on eggshells around her family's fragile egos. And when the prodigal son, Jonny, unexpectedly returns, he seems more determined than ever to push everyone’s buttons.

Though the siblings return to their family home with the intention of dividing up their mother’s belongings, what they unearth there will challenge everything they thought they knew about themselves and one another. As explosive secrets come to light, the family are set to lose everything - including their dignity.

This production marks the play's world premiere. Secure your tickets today!

Casting for Relics is to be announced.

Relics is written by Ben Ockrent. Ockrent is an award-winning playwright, director and screenwriter. His credits include Hacktivists for National Theatre Connections, Carrot for Theatre 503, At Risk and short play Honey , commissioned as part of Olivier-nominated short play series The Great Game , both at the Kiln Theatre (formerly the Tricycle), as well as screenwriting on Waterloo Road and Material Girls for BBC1 and Youngers for E4.

Michael Longhurst directs. Longhurst is an Olivier-nominated director and former Artistic Director of the Donmar Warehouse. His credits for the Donmar Warehouse include Constellations , Blindness, The Cherry Orchard, Macbeth starring David Tennant and Cush Jumbo and the UK premiere of Pulitzer-winning musical Next to Normal . Other credits include Caroline, or Change for the Chichester Festival Theatre, Amadeus for the National Theatre and Much Ado about Nothing for the RSC.

Relics is the riotously funny and deeply moving new play from rising star playwright Ben Ockrent, directed by Michael Longhurst. Don't miss out on the world premiere of this pitch-black family drama, all about loss, legacy and learning who you are. Book your tickets for Relics at the Lyric Hammersmith today!

shows.title: RENT
shows.description:
Get ready to live “La Vie Boheme” as smash hit rock musical Rent returns to London. This landmark revival of Jonathan Larson’s Pulitzer and Tony-winning musical, about a group of bohemian friends grappling with addiction, illness and artistic endeavours in 1980s New York, celebrates the show's 30th anniversary. Don't wait “Another Day” - tickets are on sale now.

Set over the course of a year, Rent follows a group of impoverished artistic friends living in the East Village, New York City, in the 1980s. Roommates, musician Roger and filmmaker Mark, are struggling to pay the rent to their former friend-turned-landlord, Benny, while each is dealing with a turbulent love life. Mark has recently been dumped by his girlfriend, activist and performance artist Maureen, for another woman, straightlaced lawyer Joanne; Roger is struggling with HIV and has fallen for wildcard addict and stripper Mimi. Maureen and Joanne struggle to find balance in their fiery relationship, while anarchist university professor Collins, meets drag queen and drummer Angel, who handles her HIV positive status with unrelenting optimism and kindness.

As the year unfolds, the friends fall in and out of love, protest the incoming gentrification of their city, battle with addiction, and face the tragedy of the AIDS crisis, all while trying their best to keep making art and living their bohemian lives as if there’s “no day but today”. Now a modern classic, Rent features iconic songs “Seasons of Love”, “La Vie Boheme”, “Today 4 U” and “Take Me or Leave Me”.

Rent is loosely based on the 1896 opera La Boheme by Giacomo Puccini. The musical began life at the New York Theatre Workshop in the early 1990s. The show opened off-Broadway in 1996, but tragically, writer and composer Jonathan Larson died suddenly of an undiagnosed heart condition the day before the show was due to open. The production opened as planned in tribute to Larson and was a sell-out success, transferring to Broadway later the same year.

Rent was groundbreaking at the time, earning a Pulitzer Prize and the Tony Award for Best Musical, and running in New York City for 12 years, making it one of the longest-running Broadway musicals. The show premiered in London in 1998, earning an Olivier nomination. The musical has toured extensively internationally and was adapted into a film in 2005,  featuring many of the Broadway production's original cast. This new production celebrates the show’s 30th anniversary.

Gaten Matarazzo stars as Mark, making his West End debut. Matarazzo is best known for his role as Dustin in Netflix smash hit Stranger Things , but is no stranger to musical theatre, having performed in productions since he was a child. His stage credits include Sweeney Todd on Broadway, Into the Woods at the Hollywood Bowl, Dear Evan Hansen, Godspell , and Parade .

Further casting is to be announced.

Rent has a book, music and lyrics by Jonathan Larson. Larson (1960 – 1996) was an American composer, lyricist and playwright. Larson died unexpectedly the day before Rent opened, but has posthumously been awarded a Pulitzer Prize and three Tony Awards for his work. Rent is Larson’s best-known work; other musicals include Supurbia and Tick, Tick... Boom!, an autobiographical rock-musical which was staged following Larson’s death, and later adapted into an Academy Award-nominated, Golden Globe-winning movie-musical for Netflix, directed by Lin-Manuel Miranda and starring Andrew Garfield.

This “exhilarating, landmark rock opera” (New York Times) comes to London for the first time in over a decade to celebrate the show's 30th anniversary. Hopeful, funny and with a rock-infused score, you won’t want to miss Rent , so don't wait 525,600 minutes to see this huge revival of the groundbreaking Grammy and Olivier-nominated, Tony and Pulitzer-winning show. shows.title: Romeo & Juliet
shows.description:
Stranger Things star Sadie Sink makes her West End debut in Romeo and Juliet , directed by revolutionary director Robert Icke. Sink is joined by rising star Noah Jupe as Romeo. This bold new staging of Shakespeare’s timeless romantic tragedy comes to the Harold Pinter Theatre in the heart of Leicester Square and promises to be the hottest show of the season - secure your tickets today!

"Parting is such sweet sorrow."

The two oldest families in Verona, the Capulets and Montagues, have been feuding for an age. So when Juliet, the Capulets' youngest daughter, and Romeo, a Montague, fall for each other at a party during the height of summer, their forbidden love and whirlwind romance spark a series of events that can only end in tragedy…

Romeo and Juliet is one of William Shakespeare’s most performed tragedies. The plot is loosely based on an Italian tale by Matteo Bandello, which is one of many such tragic love stories, and which was translated into verse in 1562 as The Tragical History of Romeus and Juliet by Arthur Brooke, and later in prose in 1567 as part of the story collection Palace of Pleasure by William Painter. Shakespeare’s version of the story was inspired by both translations, but was significantly expanded, adding supporting characters and secondary plots. The play is believed to have been written between 1591 and 1595, as part of the first folio.

Romeo and Juliet has been revived and adapted numerous times, including several times for film with significant adaptations including the 1968 version by Franco Zeffirelli and Baz Luhrmann's 1996 Romeo + Juliet , which starred Clare Danes and Leonardo DiCaprio.

Sadie Sink and Noah Jupe lead the cast as Juliet and Romeo, both making their West End debut in the roles.

Sadie Sink is an American actor best known for her role as Max in Stranger Things . She is a Tony nominee, and was the second youngest woman in history to be nominated for ‘Best Actress’. Her credits include The Whale, Fear Street , Annie and John Proctor is the Villain on Broadway.

Noah Jupe is a British actor best known for his roles in Honey Boy, A Quiet Place Part II, Lady in the Lake for Apple TV, Ford v Ferrari , and most recently Hamnet with Paul Mescal. He is an Independent Spirit nominee.

Robert Icke directs. Icke is a playwright and director, best known for his play The Doctor and his modern adaptation of classics including Mary Stuart starring Juliet Stevenson, Oedipus with Mark Strong and Lesley Manville and 1984 for Headlong theatre company. His directing credits include Manhunt, which he also wrote, for the Royal Court, Hamlet starring Andrew Scott for the Almeida and Henry IV, Parts 1 and 2 starring Ian McKellen. He is a former associate director at Headlong Theatre and the Almeida.

Further creative team members are to be confirmed.

Don't miss Sadie Sink and Noah Jupe as star-crossed lovers in their West End debut, with direction by "one of the most important forces in today’s theatre." (Observer), Robert Icke. It’d be a tragedy to miss it - book your tickets for Romeo and Juliet at the Harold Pinter Theatre today.
