English National Ballet: Romeo and Juliet

shows.description:
In January 2027, Romeo and Juliet, one of the greatest love stories ever told returns to the London Coliseum, just off Leicester Square, in a landmark revival from English National Ballet. In celebration of the ballet’s 50th anniversary, Rudolf Nureyev’s iconic production returns to the stage where it first premiered in 1977, for Queen Elizabeth II’s Silver Jubilee. Based on Shakespeare’s tragic romance, and set to a score by Sergei Prokofiev, “'Emotion pours from every corner of the [...] stage” (Bachtrack) - secure your tickets to English National Ballet: Romeo and Juliet today.

A balletic reimagining of Shakespeare’s ultimate tragedy, Romeo and Juliet is set in Renaissance Italy, in the divided city of Verona, where hostility between the Montagues and the Capulets threatens to erupt into violence. Amid simmering hatred and public clashes, fate intervenes when Romeo Montague and Juliet Capulet meet and fall instantly, irrevocably in love. Their relationship blooms in secret, but the world around them is ruled by loyalty, honour and revenge. As tensions escalate, their love is tested by forces beyond their control. The question at the heart of the story remains as urgent as ever: can young love survive in a society consumed by conflict?

Rudolf Nureyev’s choreography captures both the intimacy of first love and the electrifying drama of street battles and ballroom encounters. From the famous balcony pas de deux to the devastating final embrace, the ballet moves from tenderness to tragedy with gripping theatrical power.

Nureyev created the production in 1977 for Queen Elizabeth II’s Silver Jubilee, and it premiered at the London Coliseum the same year. Since its debut, Romeo and Juliet has become one of English National Ballet’s defining works, remaining a cornerstone of the company’s repertoire, admired for its scale, emotional clarity and faithful storytelling. Prokofiev’s score features some of the ballet's most instantly recognisable works and orchestral suites, including the stirring “Dance of the Knights”, performed live by the English National Ballet Philharmonic.

Now celebrating its 50th anniversary, this revival offers audiences the chance to see a landmark production in the theatre where it began, in a full-circle moment for one of ballet’s most enduring interpretations.

Casting varies by performance, with principal dancers from English National Ballet taking on the roles of Romeo, Juliet, Mercutio, Tybalt and the wider Verona ensemble.

The score is performed by the English National Ballet Philharmonic.

This production of English Romeo and Juliet was choreographed by Rudolf Nureyev(1938–1993). One of the most influential figures in 20th-century ballet, Nuruyev was a Soviet-born ballet dancer choreographer, and former director of the Paris Opera Ballet. Formerly a principal dancer for the Kirov (now Mariinsky) Ballet, Nureyev defected from the Soviet Union in 1961, establishing an international performing career which included roles with the Chicago Opera Ballet and as principal dancer for The Royal Ballet. As a choreographer, he is best known for his dramatically intense productions, which expanded roles for male dancers, including Swan Lake, The Sleeping Beauty, Don Quixote, and La Bayadère .

Sergei Prokofiev (1891–1953) was a Russian composer, pianist and conductor, regarded as one of the major composers of the 20th century. His body of work spans symphonies, concertos, operas, film scores and ballets. Among his best-known works are the ballet Cinderella , the children’s classic Peter and the Wolf , the opera War and Peace , and the cantata Alexander Nevsky (adapted from his score for Sergei Eisenstein’s film). His piano concertos and symphonies remain staples of the orchestral repertoire, and Prokofiev’s music continues to be widely performed worldwide.

You won’t want to miss this huge revival of one of literature's greatest romances, adapted into one of ballet’s most powerful works by one of the 20th century's most influential choreographers. Romeo and Juliet is “entertainment as vital, as alive and as stirring as can be” (The Telegraph), and returns to London to celebrate the production's 50th Anniversary. Allow yourself to fall in love - secure your tickets for English National Ballet: Romeo and Juliet at the London Coliseum today.

shows.description:
Be in the audience of a brand new musical every night as improv troupe The Showstoppers return for a Monday residency at the Cambridge Theatre in Seven Dials. Showstopper The Improvised Musical is a hilarious and brilliant display of quick-thinking creativity - so step aside Lloyd Webber, there’s some new musical theatre impresarios in town!

A top producer needs your help. He’s been asked to present a brand new musical - a sure-fire West End hit - but he’s stuck for ideas. Every night he takes prompts for name, setting, music genre and more from the audience, so you might find your suggestion brought to life live on stage.

From Phantom of the Operating Table to Sex, Drugs and Sausage Roll , every night is a premiere with the Showstopper team, and none of them know what they’ll be performing until the suggestions start rolling in.

This wacky and brilliant show, steered each night by a hugely talented team of actors, musicians and techies, premiered at Edinburgh Fringe Festival before transferring to the West End for a series of residencies. In 2016 it won the Olivier Award for Best Entertainment and Family Show, and has remained a fast favourite ever since.

Crowds rush to see what the team have got hidden up their sleeves every Monday night… and if there’s any end to their astounding improv skills, they’ve shown no signs of it yet!

The Showstopper troupe is headed up by creators and performers Adam Meggido and Dylan Emery, who devised and premiered the show back in 2008.

The cast on any given night includes Ruth Bratt, Justin Brett, Matt Cavendish, Jonathan Ainscough, Pippa Evans, Susan Harrison, Joshua C Jackson, Ali James, Sean McCann, Philip Pellew, Ethan Pascal Peters, Martha Pothen, Andrew Pugsley, Lauren Shearing, Joy Tan, Lucy Trodd and Heather Urquhart.

Showstopper also features a group of musicians who perform live every night - a crucial role for any musical, and you will be amazed by how quickly they can come up with melodies for the cast to sing along to.

Where else can you enjoy a musical debut every night?! Showstopper The Improvised Musical is the perfect combination of comedy and theatre and the joy is in not knowing what to expect. Andrew Lloyd Webber tunes in a bakery, jazz-hands on a space station… book Showstopper tickets for a unique evening of musical theatre that might even inspire you to write your own hit.

When Prince Siegfried falls in love with the beautiful Princess Odette, he doesn’t know her biggest secret - and that he may be her salvation. When the sorcerer's daughter, the Black Swan Odile, interferes with a cruel trick, causing Siegfried to mistakenly betray his love, Odette may lose her last chance to become human again, forever…

Swan Lake is brought to life by the company of “versatile and accomplished” dancers (The New York Times), in this full-length production of the classical ballet, featuring sumptuous costumes, stunning sets, and an immaculate corps de swans, set to Tchaikovsky’s timeless score.

The State Ballet of Georgia is the ballet company of the Z. Paliashvili Opera and Ballet State Theatre in Tbilisi, Georgia. Founded in 1852 by Count Mikhail Vorontsov, a Russian governor in Georgia, the ballet was initially host to visiting troupes from St. Petersburg, Moscow, Kiev, and Warsaw. In 1935 the company was formally established as a resident company by dancer and choreographer Vakhtang Chabukiani, designer Simon Virsaladze, and composer Andria Balanchivadze, becoming a premier Soviet company renowned for mixing classical, Russian, and Italian technique.

Georgia-born dancer Nina Ananiashvili has been Artistic Director of the company since 2004. Considered to be one of the world's greatest dancers, Nina Ananiashvili is a former prima ballerina with the Bolshoi Ballet and the American Ballet Theatre.

The company has previously staged the production in London in 2024, and prior to this performed work at the Edinburgh International Festival.

Swan Lake is written by Russian composer Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky. The show is performed by members of the State Ballet of Georgia company, accompanied by the Royal Ballet Sinfonia. The production is under the artistic direction of the company AD Nina Ananiashvili.

Ananiashvili's accolades include a People's Artist of Russia award, both a Georgian Order of Honour and Medal of Honour (Georgia's highest order), and a Presidential Order of Light.

You won't want to miss this elegantly staged, “dazzlingly polished” (Charleston City Paper) Swan Lake , performed by a stunning company who “bring a lot of beauty, heart, and soul to their work” (Georgian Times). With breathtaking costumes, a company of over 70 dancers and a live orchestra performing Tchaikovsky’s iconic score. This acclaimed Georgia ballet company performing in London is a rare treat - secure your tickets to the State Ballet of Georgia: Swan Lake at the London Coliseum today.

shows.title: Tao of Glass
shows.description:
Boundary-pushing new show Tao of Glass makes its West End Premiere this summer at Soho Place, just off Tottenham Court Road. This groundbreaking collaboration between composer Phillip Glass and performer-director, Improbable’s Phelim McDermott, combines brand new music with Taoist wisdom in a “truly magical journey” (WhatsOnStage) that meditates on life and loss. Don’t miss it - secure your tickets today.

Where does inspiration truly come from? Sparked by a dream, this innovative new show explores this question, merging ten brand-new pieces of music from Grammy and Academy Award-nominated composer Philip Glass, with Taoist wisdom, meditating on loss, life and meaning. Part performance, part concert, this remarkable production weaves a mesmerising tapestry of music and storytelling, in the most personal collaboration yet from long-standing creative colleagues Philip Glass and Phelim McDermott.

Tao of Glass premiered at the acclaimed Manchester International Arts Festival in 2019, to critical acclaim, as a co-commission between Factory International, Manchester, Improbable, Perth Festival, Ruhrfestspiele Recklinghausen, Hong Kong New Vision Arts Festival and Carolina Performing Arts – University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in association with Naomi Milgrom AO.

Tao of Glass is the latest collaboration between Philip Glass, who composes music for the piece, and Phelim McDermott, who writes, co-directs and performs. The pair have previously worked together on Opera productions in London, New York and internationally.

Philip Glass is widely regarded as one of the most influential composers of the late 20th Century. The founder of the Philip Glass ensemble, his work spans opera, musical theatre, film scores and chamber and orchestral pieces. His credits include scores for The Hours, Notes on a Scandal, and The Truman Show , as well as operas Einstein on the Beach, and The Quiet American . Glass’s numerous accolades include a BAFTA Award, a Drama Desk Award, and a Golden Globe, nominations for three Academy Awards, four Grammy Awards, and a Primetime Emmy Award, as well as the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres, the National Medal of Arts, Kennedy Center Honors, a Grammy Trustees Award and a Lifetime Achievement from the World Soundtrack Academy.

Phelim McDermott is a performer-director. A founding member and co-artistic director of award-winning theatre group Improbable, McDermott is an Olivier Award winner. His credits include Satyagraha, Akhnaten, and The Perfect American with Glass, Shockheaded Peter for the West Yorkshire Playhouse, Leeds, and the Lyric Hammersmith, The Enchanted Island for the Metropolitan Opera, Così fan tutte for ENO and My Neighbour Totoro at the RSC, Barbican Centre and in the West End.

Kirsty Housley ( Drive Your Plow Over The Bones Of The Dead ) is co-director, with design by Fly Davis ( Caroline or Change ), lighting design by Colin Grenfell (Medea), sound design by Giles Thomas ( Master Harold and the Boys ) and musical direction by Chris Vatalaro. Little Angel Theatre co-founder Lyndie Wright ( The Magic Flute ) is the puppet designer and puppet maker

Tao of Glass is produced by Factory International, Improbable and Nica Burns.

This innovative show interweaves Taoist wisdom with the music of legendary composer Philip Glass in a boundary-pushing, deeply moving performance. “Every so often your eyes will fill with tears, for there is only so much that the human heart can hold within it” (Guardian) - don’t miss this remarkable piece of theatre, secure your tickets for Tao of Glass at Soho Place today.

shows.title: Teeth ‘N’ Smiles
shows.description:
Grab your tickets for the hottest gig in town, as Rebecca Taylor aka Self Esteem returns to the West End this Spring. Taylor stars as Maggie in Teeth 'N' Smiles , a major revival of the classic David Hare musical play, about a rockstar trying to keep her band together at a tough gig, staged in celebration of the show's 50th anniversary. Teeth 'N' Smiles comes to the Duke of York's Theatre, in the heart of Leicester Square, this spring for a limited time only. Don't miss out - book your tickets today!

It’s 1969, and in a dilapidated basement bar at Jesus College, Cambridge, a rock and roll band prepares to play for a university ball.

While her bandmates may be skint, disillusioned, and feel they’ve sold out by performing at the stuffy university, all lead singer Maggie wants to do is perform… and drink. But tensions are high as Maggie quarrels with both the band’s controlling manager, Saffian and her ex-lover, songwriter Arthur, who is grappling with his lingering feelings for Maggie, as well as a blooming attraction to Laura, the band’s new assistant. As the band’s dreams of stardom slowly collapse, Maggie is determined to go on with the show. Fuelled by alcohol, rage and rock’n’roll, as the night draws on, Maggie struggles to keep her grip on the gig, and on reality…

Teeth 'N' Smiles first premiered at The Royal Court Theatre in 1975, starring Helen Mirren as Maggie. A subversive, rock’n’roll smash hit, during the show’s initial run at the Royal Court, The Who drummer Keith Moon arrived intoxicated at the stage door to lavish praise on Mirren - before trying to join the cast on stage, and being stopped by the theatre’s management!

This anarchic, trailblazing play about counterculture and artistic integrity returns to London 50 years on, in a landmark new production with updated music from Self Esteem.

Rebecca Lucy Taylor stars as Maggie.

Taylor is best known for her work as a musician and songwriter under the stage name Self Esteem. Formerly part of indie duo Slow Club, Taylor began performing solo in 2019 and has since released three critically acclaimed, best-selling albums, winning an Ivor Novello and Attitude Award and receiving nominations for the Mercury, NME and Brit Awards. Taylor also composed the music for Olivier-winning play Prima Facie , starring Jodie Comer.

Taylor is also an accomplished actress, with credits including roles on I Hate Suzie with Billy Piper, in SKY TV series Smothered, and as Sally Bowles in Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club opposite Jake Shears. In early 2025, Taylor also performed in a staged version of her album, A Complicated Woman , at the Duke of York’s Theatre, which she also devised.

Further casting includes:

Teeth 'N' Smiles is written by David Hare, with music and lyrics by Nick Bicât and Tony Bicât and additional new music and lyrics by Self Esteem. Daniel Raggett directs.

Daniel Raggett is an Evening Standard Theatre Award-nominated film and theatre director. His credits include Brace Brace at the Royal Court, The Vortex at Chichester Festival Theatre, Anna X at the Harold Pinter Theatre, an Olivier-nominated production of Accidental Death of an Anarchist at the Theatre Royal Haymarket and Sheffield Theatres, and short film Hermit , starring Emma Corin. Ragett has also worked as an associate director to Ivo Van Hove on several productions, including Network at the National, Mary Stuart in the West End, and West Side Story on Broadway.

Sir David Hare is an award-winning playwright, screenwriter and director. He is an Olivier and BAFTA winner, and a Tony, Golden Globe, and Academy Award nominee. His most notable works include feature films The Hours , starring Meryl Streep and Julianne Moore, and The Reader , starring Kate Winslet and Ralph Fiennes, and plays My Zinc Bed, Skylight, The Vertical Hour and Straight Line Crazy .

Teeth 'N' Smiles was a trailblazing play upon its premiere and now celebrates its 50th anniversary with this bold, raucous and explosive new production featuring rock’n’roll star Rebecca Lucy Taylor, aka Self Esteem. You won't want to miss it - so what are you waiting for? Get the band back together and book for Teeth 'N' Smiles at the Duke of York Theatre today!

shows.title: The Book Of Mormon
shows.description:
Don’t miss the unforgettable, long-running musical comedy THE BOOK OF MORMON! Playing in London’s West End, at the Prince of Wales Theatre.

After stunning audiences on both Broadway and the West End, winning 9 Tony Awards and even winning a Grammy award for the soundtrack, THE BOOK OF MORMON musical is a certified theatrical phenomenon. Comedy duo Trey Parker and Matt Stone – the geniuses behind the animated hit South Park – joined forces to create this hilarious musical that breathes three-dimensional, all-singing, all-dancing life into the absurdities of Mormon dogma, whilst simultaneously being incredibly rude, potentially offensive and above all, unexpectedly endearing.

Book your THE BOOK OF MORMON theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

Read More for show synopsis, cast & creative, age guidance and more…

What is The Book of Mormon about?

This musical tells the story of two Salt Lake City Mormons, Elder Price and Elder Cunningham, sent as missionaries to Uganda, hoping for a few baptisms and a couple of conversions – instead, they are welcomed by some harsh realities and a particularly unpleasant warlord. With lyrics guaranteed to have you weeping with laughter, you’ll be humming the music by Avenue Q’s Robert Lopez for weeks after.

It is fun and lightweight, but also thought-provoking; addressing everything from consumerism to religion. The Book of Mormon is a musical like no other. Its staggering and well-deserved box office success makes it a real must-see.

Ticket Information

Tickets for The Book of Mormon are now on sale for performances until 3rd October 2026. Performances Monday to Saturday at 7:30PM, with matinee performances on Friday and Saturday at 2:30PM.

Show Information

Please note: Contains strobe lighting, flashing lights and gunshots. Parental advisory: Explicit language.

Children under the age of 16 must be accompanied by and sat next to a ticketholder who is at least 18 years old. Children under the age of 3 will not be admitted.

Running Time

2hrs 30mins (incl. interval, subject to change)

Cast & Creatives

shows.title: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind

sources.title_as_listed: The Boy Who Harnessed The Wind
The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind
The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind
The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind

shows.description:
Fresh from a world premiere in Stratford-upon-Avon, The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind makes its West End debut at Soho Place, in the heart of Soho, for a strictly limited run this spring. This bold moving and uplifting musical, about a young Malawian boy who fights to save his village from a devastating drought is based on the incredible true story, and the film adaptation by Olivier Award winner Chiwetel Ejiofor. Joyous, moving and telling a vitally important story, The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind promises to be unmissable theatre. Secure your tickets today!

In the midst of a scorching summer in Malawi and a devastating drought, 13-year-old William has a dream - he wants to save his village. As the drought worsens day by day, causing crops to fail and hope to run dry, nobody in William’s community believes he can find the solution to their problems, with even his family and friends doubting him. Armed only with library books, some scrap machinery and his own imagination and grit, William is determined to prove them all wrong and bring the village some relief. As William begins to build a windmill, challenges arise - can he harness both the power of his creativity and the wind to bring hope back to his people?

The musical is based on the 2019 film, which was written, directed and starred in by Chiwetel Ejiofor, and was based on the memoir of the same name by William Kamkwamba and Bryan Mealer. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2019, and later received a wide release on Netflix. The musical makes its world premiere at the Swan Theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon in February 2026 before transferring to London for a strictly limited run in April.

Adapted from the book by William Kamkwamba and Bryan Mealey, as well as the film by Chiwetel Ejiofor, who serves as executive producer, The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind has a book and lyrics by Richy Hughes ( Superhero, Mr Popper's Penguins ) and music and lyrics by Tim Sutton ( Restless Natives, The Merry Wives of Windsor ).

The production is directed by former Bush Theatre Artistic Director and BAFTA nominee Lynette Linton ( Shifters, Sweat, Intimate Apparel, Blues for an Alabama Sky ).

This joyous, deeply moving new musical is a celebration of ingenuity and the courage to dream, even whilst facing impossible odds. With a West End transfer confirmed before the world premiere has even opened in Stratford, we know this is going to be a deeply special show. Book your tickets for The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind at Soho Place today and allow yourself to be blown away by this remarkable story.

shows.title: The Car Man
shows.description:
Buckle up at Sadler’s Wells, in the heart of Islington, as Matthew Bourne’s multi-award-winning The Car Man returns for a strictly limited run. Based on Bizet’s Carmen, The Car Man is a dance-thriller spectacular which transports the classic opera’s story to a grease-slicked garage and diner in small town USA. This red-hot dance show is “sizzling and fizzing with lust” (Telegraph), and makes for unmissable theatre - secure your tickets today.

In a greasy 1960s diner, one small town’s dreams are torn apart when a handsome stranger arrives, and the townspeople soon descend into a frenzied spiral of greed, desire, backstabbing and revenge.

Matthew Bourne’s The Car Man premiered in 2000 at Plymouth’s Theatre Royal and is one of his most distinctive and provocative dance-theatre productions. Loosely inspired by Bizet’s Carmen and drawing narrative influence from James M. Cain’s novel The Postman Always Rings Twice , it reimagines the action of the sultry opera in small-town America. With a moody adapted score, the show blends passion, betrayal, and murder in a gripping noir-style tale. Over the years, it has been revived multiple times, including a major production in 2015 and a film version released by Sky Arts in 2022. In 2000, the show won the Evening Standard Award for best “Musical Event” and was nominated for a Laurence Olivier Award.

The Car Man is performed by the company of New Adventures. Direction and choreography are by acclaimed choreographer and New Adventures founder Matthew Bourne ( Swan Lake, The Red Shoes ), with a dramatic, cinematic score adapted and arranged by Terry Davies ( Frankenstein, The Wind in the Willows ) based on Bizet’s Carmen . The production also features set and costume design by Lez Brotherston ( Sleeping Beauty, The Red Shoes ), lighting by Chris Davey ( Nutcracker!, Romeo and Juliet ), and sound design by Paul Groothuis ( Oliver!, Follies ).

This incredible production is Bizet’s Carmen as you’ve never seen it before. Allow yourself to be swept into the world of The Car Man , where romance and revenge collide. This award-winning show from dance titan Matthew Bourne is “gripping, gasp-making, edge of your seat stuff” (Daily Mail) and returns for a strictly limited run - don’t miss out, book your tickets for The Car Man at Sadler’s Wells today.

shows.title: The Cherry Orchard
shows.description:
Ian Rickson directs Conor McPherson’s new adaptation of The Cherry Orchard, which is heading to the West End. A quietly devastating tragicomedy led by Kristin Scott Thomas, it plays at the Harold Pinter Theatre located close to Leicester Square. This play promises a piece of theatre which remains as timeless and resonant as ever.

The Cherry Orchard captures a world in a delicate and inevitable transition. Chekhov’s play follows an aristocratic Russian family who return to their estate, known for its large cherry orchard, only to be crippled by debt and the likelihood that they will lose their home. Although it is a simplistic story, The Cherry Orchard encapsulates a world that is tilting towards revolution in the 20th century.

Written in 1903, The Cherry Orchard was the last play written by Anton Chekhov. He is also known for publishing other outstanding plays like The Seagull, Three Sisters, and Uncle Vanya. It was first staged at the Moscow Art Theatre a year after it was published in 1904.

A plentiful number of productions of The Cherry Orchard have made it to the UK stage over the years, with the first in 1911 at the Aldwych Theatre. The most notable production starred Zoe Wanamaker at the National Theatre in 2011.

Kristin Scott Thomas is a five-time BAFTA Award and Olivier Award nominee. She won the Olivier Award for Best Actress for her performance in The Seagull , which Ian Rickson also directed. Her film and theatre credits include Nowhere Boy , Salmon Fishing in the Yemen , The Audience and Lyonesse .

Conor McPherson has adapted this production of The Cherry Orchard . He has received Tony and Olivier Award nominations for his work, including The Brightening Air, Girl from the North Country and Uncle Vanya .

The production will be directed by Ian Rickson. He has directed numerous productions across the globe, including The Weir , Jerusalem , and London Tide .

Joining him will be set designer Chloe Lamford, lighting designer Bruno Poet, movement director Shelley Maxwell and casting director Amy Ball CDG.

Don’t miss out on the opportunity to see one of the most poignant plays of our time, performed by the multi-award-winning actress Kristin Scott Thomas. Book your tickets to experience this bold new revival of The Cherry Orchard at the Harold Pinter Theatre for a limited time.

shows.title: The Comedy About Spies
shows.description:
Theatre fans, your mission - if you choose to accept it - is simple: enjoy some of the biggest laughs in the West End with The Comedy About Spies ! This riotous play from Mischief Theatre, the team behind the hilarious The Play That Goes Wrong , returns to London this August for a strictly limited run following a sell-out summer season in 2025. “Bigger, better and more brilliantly bungling than ever” (Daily Mail), The Comedy About Spies dives into the murky world of espionage in 1960s London. With stolen plans for a top-secret weapon, hurried meetings in hotels, and a hefty dose of mistaken identity, this Cold War farce is a little less suave than Bond, but much funnier! Don’t find yourself out of the loop: catch this five-star comedy play as it comes to the Adelphi Theatre, just off the Strand, this summer.

It’s London in the 1960s, and there’s fashion, rockin’ music and intrigue at every turn. When a rogue British agent steals top-secret plans for a new weapon, spies from the CIA and KGB meet at the Piccadilly Hotel to smoke out the treacherous mole. This is a Mischief Theatre play, though, so nothing’s simple… and the hotel is coincidentally welcoming a young British couple and an actor auditioning for the first ever James Bond film at the same time!

A straightforward mission for the world’s most daring spies quickly turns into a mess of mistaken identity and miscommunication. As the stakes get higher, will the traitor be found in time? This side-splitting Cold War farce brings together the best tropes from your favourite spy films and flips them on their head. The result? A madcap spoof full of bumbling agents, confused guests, valiantly misguided heroism… and one of the funniest nights out in London.

The Comedy About Spies premiered at the Noel Coward Theatre in summer 2025, and returns for a second missing this August - for eight weeks only!

Multi-award-winning theatre troupe Mischief Theatre have been tickling audiences’ funny bones since 2008 with some of London’s biggest comedy plays. From Olivier Award winner The Play That Goes Wrong to The Comedy About a Bank Robbery and Groan Ups , Mischief proves that it doesn’t have to be all about drama and tragedy in the West End - there’s plenty of room for laughter as well!

Mischief Theatre was formed by Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer, and Henry Shields, with a trusty company of actors regularly appearing in their shows. The Comedy About Spies is co-written by Lewis and Shields and directed by Matt Di Carlo ( The Play That Goes Wrong Off-Broadway, Christmas Carol Goes Wrong ). Fans will be pleased to hear that the original Mischief members will be returning for this silly summer revival:

MI5? More like LOL! This new Mischief Theatre comedy is perfect for fans of James Bond, Austin Powers, and every agent in between. This hilarious comedy play will “leave you crying helpless tears of laughter” (Guardian) and sold out its previous run, so move quickly and book your tickets for The Comedy About Spies at Adelphi Theatre today… Our surveillance says it’s a hit!

shows.title: The Devil Wears Prada
shows.description:
The production has received four nominations for the 2025 WhatsOnStage Awards, including Best New Musical, Best Performer in a Musical for Vanessa Williams, Best Supporting Performer in a Musical for Amy Di Bartolomeo, and Best Wigs, Hair and Make Up for Campbell Young Associates.

THE DEVIL WEARS PRADA, a new musical, has consistently smashed sales records since opening at the Dominion Theatre, becoming the fastest selling show in the theatre’s history, with the largest advance, with the first 100 performances of the hit show at 100% capacity! Over 220,000 audience members have come through our ‘Dior’s’ since 24 October 2024, and the “absolutely fabulous” (Evening Standard ★★★★★) musical shows no signs of stopping!

Starring as the irrepressible Miranda Priestly is Vanessa Williams, best known for her celebrated roles in Ugly Betty and Desperate Housewives and as a multi-award-winning singer. Alongside her is Olivier Award winner and Grammy nominated, Matt Henry, MBE, as Runway’s Creative Fashion Director, Nigel. They are joined by Stevie Doc playing the driven Andy, Taila Halford as the icy First Assistant to Miranda, Emily, James Darch (Mamma Mia!; Wicked) as the devious journalist, Christian, and Keelan McAuley as Andy’s long-term boyfriend, Nate.

Hilariously fun and fabulously stylish, THE DEVIL WEARS PRADA tells an inspiring story about discovering what kind of person you truly want to be. Choose your outfit carefully and get ready for a new musical that’s hautter than hell!

Don’t be fashionably late. Book your THE DEVIL WEARS PRADA theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

Vanessa Williams and Matt Henry are in the show until 17th October 2026

Read More for show synopsis, cast & creative, age guidance and more…

What is The Devil Wears Prada about?

Fresh out of college, aspiring journalist Andy scores a job at the prestigious Runway magazine working for fashion’s most powerful and terrifying icon — editor-in-chief Miranda Priestly. Sacrificing her personal life to meet Miranda’s impossible demands, Andy finds herself seduced by the glamorous world she once despised. How far will she go to succeed… and will it be worth selling her soul to get what she’s always wanted?

Ticket Information

Tickets available for performances from 24 Oct 2024 – 6 Feb 2027

Show Info

The show features strobe lighting effects.

Running Time

2hrs 30mins (incl. interval)

Cast & Creatives

Vanessa Williams (Miranda Priestly), Matt Henry (Nigel), Stevie Doc (Andy), Taila Halford (Emily), James Darch (Christian), Keelan McAuley (Nate), Maddy Ambus, Gabby Antrobus, Selena Barron, Pamela Blair, Robertina Bonano, Josh Damer-Jennings, Lloyd Davies, Elishia Edwards, Akeem Ellis-Hyman, Elizabeth Fullalove, Jinny Gould, Natasha Heyward, Samuel How, Luke Jackson, Debbie Kurup, Brandon Lee Sears, Nathan Lorainey-Dineen, Liam Marcellino, Ciro Lourencio Meulens, Theo Papoui, Christopher Parkinson, Eleanor Peach, Ethan Le Phong, Jon Reynolds, Harriet Samuel-Gray, Olivia Saunders, Joshua Steel, Kayleigh Thadani, Ella Valentine, Rhys Whitfield and Tara Yasmin.

THE DEVIL WEARS PRADA, features an all-star, award-winning creative team led by Elton John (Tammy Faye, Billy Elliot: The Musical, The Lion King), new direction & choreography by Jerry Mitchell (Kinky Boots, Legally Blonde, Pretty Woman, Hairspray), lyrics by singer-songwriter Shaina Taub (Suffs) and Mark Sonnenblick (Theatre Camp), book by Kate Wetherhead (Ever After, Submissions Only), set design by Tim Hatley (Life of Pi, Back to the Future), costume design by Gregg Barnes (Some Like It Hot, Legally Blonde), lighting design by Bruno Poet (The Tina Turner Musical, Frankenstein), sound design by Gareth Owen (Come From Away, & Juliet) and casting by Jill Green CDG.

The Devil Wears Prada Soundtrack

Age Guidance 8+. As per Dominion Theatre terms, children under 5 cannot be admitted to the theatre. Children aged 15 or under must be accompanied by an adult (at least one adult per 10 children).

shows.title: The Gruffalo
shows.description:
Take a stroll into the deep dark theatre and discover… The Gruffalo ! Celebrate 25 years of Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler’s beloved picture book with this boisterous stage adaptation from Tall Stories. The much-loved show has delighted families around the world and now returns to the West End’s Lyric Theatre, just a short walk from Piccadilly Circus, for another summer season.

Join Mouse as she heads into the woods searching for hazelnuts. Along the way, she runs into the eccentric Owl, cunning Fox and sneaky Snake. They’re all hungry and Mouse is the perfect size for their dinner plates! Quick-thinking Mouse distracts them with a tale about the fearsome Gruffalo… but is he just a product of her imagination, or is he real?

The Gruffalo has delivered just the right amount of scares for 25 years and is the most beloved of former Children’s Laureate Julia Donaldson’s creations. With its instantly recognisable illustrations from Axel Scheffler, this award-winning picture book is a modern classic, featuring an eclectic cast of woodland creatures and a small but plucky protagonist. Millions of children have enjoyed it read aloud as a bedtime story or seen it on the television - but this musical adaptation brings it to life in a whole new way!

Casting for this production is to be announced.

Kid’s theatre company Tall Stories have adapted several classic picture books for the stage, including Elmer and Room on the Broom , but none are quite as beloved as Donaldson’s not-so-fearsome monster. The Gruffalo is packed with songs, laughs, and physical theatre to get the whole family cheering as Mouse’s daring adventure unfolds! Even better, at 60 minutes it is the perfect length for little ones who are watching a theatre show for the very first time.

This magical story ticks all the right boxes for an unforgettable day out. Get ready for monstrous fun in the West End! If you are looking for the best show to make your toddler or pre-schooler love the theatre, book tickets for The Gruffalo at the Lyric Theatre today.

shows.title: The Hunger Games: On Stage
shows.description:
We volunteer as tribute! This thrilling new adaptation of beloved franchise, The Hunger Games , comes to the stage for the first time this autumn. This heart-pounding new play uses “innovative and immersive staging techniques” (Guardian) to transport audiences right into the heart of The Hunger Games at the brand new purpose-built Canary Wharf Theatre, in the heart of London’s Docklands. Witness Katniss Everdeen’s fight for survival as you’ve never seen it before - secure your tickets for The Hunger Games: On Stage today.

It’s the not-so-distant future, and sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen lives in the city of Panem, a poor and underprivileged district in a dystopian region of North America. Katniss and her impoverished family just want to get by, following the death of her father several years before. But when the Capitol declares Katniss’ little sister has been chosen as “tribute” for the 74th annual Hunger Games - a fight to the death between teenagers from each district, organised to entertain the citizens of the wealthy and out-of-touch Capitol - Katniss steps up to take her place. What follows is an exhilarating battle for survival and a journey of self-discovery, as Katniss must muster all her courage, defiance and bravery to survive.

This brand new stage adaptation is based on the young adult novel by Suzanne Collins, and the movie adaptation of the same name. The first in a trilogy, The Hunger Games novel was released in 2008, becoming a global smash hit and topping the bestseller charts. The film adaptation, starring Jennifer Lawrence as Katniss, was released in 2012, also to critical acclaim, and was followed by sequels Catching Fire and Mockingjay Parts 1 and 2. The series has since expanded to include two prequel novels, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, and Sunrise on the Reaping , which focus on the youths of adult characters from the novels - including Katniss’s mentor Haymitch and the villainous Coriolanus Snow - which have also been adapted for screen.

shows.title: The Mousetrap
shows.description:
Agatha Christie’s Mousetrap is a London institution, having been performed continuously in the West End since 1952.

It started life as a radio play written at the request of the BBC for Queen Mary, and holds the distinction of being the longest-running show in the world. The Mousetrap has performed through 14 different prime ministers’ terms in office, from Winston Churchill to Rishi Sunak, and over 460 actors have appeared in the show.

The Mousetrap tickets provide an authentic taste of theatre history. Just make sure you don’t spoil the ending for any future theatregoers!

Young couple Mollie and Giles Ralston have set up a country guest house at Monkswell Manor, but their grand opening is upstaged by a grizzly murder nearby. Trapped by a snowstorm and with the killer heading their way, the residents and guests of Monkswell must figure out who is guilty.

With everyone a suspect, this ultimate whodunit has plenty of twists and turns to trap even the canniest crime fiction fans - and a surprise ending that has remained a secret for decades.

This now-iconic play has a small but brilliant cast of characters, all with secrets to keep. Can you work out whodunit?

Mollie and Giles Ralston are a newly married couple and the country estate owners that form the setting of The Mousetrap . As the snowstorm hits, they are accommodating five guests: eccentric and flighty young architect Christopher Wren; acerbic retiree Mrs. Boyle; well-mannered and eagerly helpful Major Metcalf; stand-offish and secretive young professional Miss Casewell; and last-minute guest Mr Paravicini, a charming rogue who seems to delight in the fear and uncertainty weighing down on everyone else.

Detective Sergeant Trotter arrives at Monskwell Manor to keep the guests safe and find the killer in their midst. Will he be able to work out who is responsible before it is too late… and more importantly, can you beat him to it?

The Mousetrap first opened in London in 1952, and it thrilled West End audiences for the entirety of Queen Elizabeth's reign, and into King Charles'. Its original West End home was the Ambassadors Theatre, and in 1974 it transferred to its current home, St Martins Theatre.

Queen of Crime Agatha Christie wrote the whodunit as a gift for Queen Mary, airing on BBC radio on 30 May 1947 under the name Three Blind Mice . Christie is possibly the world’s most famous crime writer, having written over 60 murder mysteries and created the iconic characters of Poirot and Miss Marple. The Mousetrap had its world premiere at Theatre Royal, Nottingham in 1952, before touring the UK ahead of its West End debut on 25 November 1952. Christie famously stated in her autobiography that she initially expected The Mousetrap play to run for no more than eight months.

Now in its 70th year, The Mousetrap is the longest-running show in the West End and in the world, beating Les Misérables, The Phantom of the Opera, The Woman in Black and The Lion King .

The Mousetrap sets a new record at every curtain up. When you enter St Martins Theatre, you will see a large wooden tally that displays the exact performance number you are attending. The play currently exceeds 28,000 West End performances and its only extended closure was in 2020, when the Covid-19 pandemic forced all West End venues to shut.

In its impressively long history, The Mousetrap has also hit several cast records. One of its original cast members, the late Deryk Guyler, still “performs” each night in a recorded radio news bulletin, whilst David Raven earned a place in the Guinness Book of Records as “Most Durable Actor” for his role as Major Metcalf at 4,575 performances between 1957 and 1968. Nancy Seabrooke also made it into the record books, racking up 15 years as an understudy in The Mousetrap .

Main cast:

Casting for The Mousetrap traditionally changes every year, with many famous faces appearing since its first West End performance. Richard Attenborough starred as the original Detective Sergeant Trotter and stars including Patrick Stewart and Julie Walters performed in a special charity performance to mark the play’s 60th anniversary - and 25,000th performance - in 2012.

The Mousetrap has a brilliantly eccentric history, with its most well-known feature being the shock twist right at the end of the show. Audiences are asked to “preserve the tradition by keeping the secret locked in your hearts”, ensuring The Mousetrap’s intricate plot and compelling surprises remain just as exciting now as they were on opening night.

There has never been a film adaptation of The Mousetrap , and it is unlikely to happen any time soon! The play’s contract states that no film can be made until it has been closed in the West End for at least six months. The production famously managed to move theatres in 1974, and install a brand new set in 2000, without losing a single performance - so the only way to see this thrilling murder mystery is by booking The Mousetrap London tickets.

An icon of the West End, The Mousetrap is one of the best London plays , and a must-see for any theatre-lover. Full of surprises, chills and thrills that remain just as sharp today as they were in 1952, this is an unmissable classic that continues to attract audiences from across the world.

shows.title: The Oresteia
shows.description:
The ancient text of Aeschylus’s The Oresteia comes to the Bridge Theatre in a radical reimagining by the acclaimed Australian theatre, opera and film director Simon Stone. Situated near Tower Bridge, this play will be significantly and cathartically relevant for audiences heading to experience this classic work, which will be transformed into something new this summer.

This new production of The Oresteia at the Bridge Theatre follows a family haunted by their role in an unjust war. As the painful burden of inherited trauma and inter-generational conflict becomes more intense, the family spirals into a powerful vortex of violence.

Based on a trilogy of Greek tragedies written by Aeschylus in the 5th century BC, The Oresteia has been adapted multiple times into operas and plays, including a rap and hip hop-inspired show by French rapper D’ de Kabal in 2014.

The Oresteia was first staged in London in 1981 by Sir Peter Hall, who directed Tony Harrison’s adaptation at the National Theatre. A subsequent revival at the same theatre took place in 1999. The most notable production was by Robert Icke in 2015 at the Almeida Theatre, where it was a sold-out hit and was transferred in the same year to the Trafalgar Theatre. At this time, there was also another production of it playing at Shakespeare’s Globe in the same year.

The Oresteia will be written and directed by Simon Stone. An Australian director and writer, he has worked on productions across the world. His London debut was in 2016 when he directed a new adaptation of Euripides’ Medea at the Young Vic and starred Billie Piper in the title role. Other credits on the stage include Phaedra, Innocence, and the critically acclaimed production of The Lady from the Sea at the Bridge Theatre in 2025.

This includes set designer Lizzie Clachan, costume designer Mel Page, music by Stefan Gregory, lighting designer Nick Schlieper, and casting director Jessica Ronane CDG.

T he Oresteia will take a timeless story and transform it into a modern and visceral play for modern audiences. If you want to experience groundbreaking work from one of the best theatre directors of today, make sure you don’t miss out on a visit to the Bridge Theatre this summer.

shows.title: The Producers
shows.description:
The Menier Chocolate Factory’s acclaimed production of The Producers transfers to the West End’s Garrick Theatre this year! Mel Brooks' irreverent, boundary-pushing musical about two men who try to commit fraud by mounting a guaranteed-to-fail Broadway show is “irresistible, absurd and joyful, both celebrating and sending up the power of theatre” (The Guardian). The Producers sold out its run off the West End so “don’t be stupid, be a smartie”  - check out our The Producers review , and book your tickets today!

Once the “King of Broadway”, producer Max Bialystock is down on his luck, a washed-up hack who now earns a living conning little old ladies into investing for shows that never happen. When nervous accountant Leo Bloom comes to audit Bialystock and discovers he’s been cooking the books, Bloom has the revelation that a show that flops could earn more than one that succeeds. So... the pair team up to produce the worst show on Broadway. They land upon the perfect script, Springtime for Hitler: A Gay Romp with Adolf and Eva at Berchtesgaden : a "love letter to Hitler" written by pigeon-obsessed ex-Nazi Franz Liebkin, and the perfect director - campy cross-dresser Roger de Bris and his partner and assistant Carmen Ghia, who live by the motto “Keep It Gay”.

Swedish bombshell Ulla rounds out their gang of misfits, joining as both chorus girl and office assistant, and Leo quickly falls for her. Once the funds are raised, Leo and Max are ready to make a show that’s sure to be a disaster - and when the show closes early, they’ll skip town with the money and head to Rio de Janeiro. But when “Opening Night” changes everything, Bialystock and Bloom must figure out what to do when the show is an unexpected smash hit.

Based on Mel Brooks' 1967 satirical cult classic film, which starred Zero Mostell and Gene Wilder, The Producers is a provocative and hilarious “equal-opportunity offender” (The Standard). The original Broadway production opened in 2001, winning a record-breaking 12 Tony Awards, and was later adapted into a movie musical starring Nathan Lane and Matthew Broderick, who originated the lead roles on stage. Featuring side-splitting songs including “Der Guten Tag Hop Clop”, “Keep it Gay”, “We Can Do It” and “Springtime for Hitler” - a song dubbed “a contender for the funniest showtune ever written” by TimeOut - The Producers remains as risqué and riotous as ever.

The Menier Chocolate Factory hosted the first major production of The Producers in London for almost 20 years and delighted audiences and critics alike, with its “vigour, sparkle and controlled wildness” (The Guardian). Don’t miss out on a gay old time when this “grimy, funny and well-judged” (TimeOut) production transfers to the West End - book today!

Main cast:

The Producers is based on the 1967 film of the same name, which was written and directed by Mel Brooks. He also adapted his own work for the stage, writing the music and lyrics and co-writing the book for the musical. Brooks is part of the exclusive EGOT club, holding Emmy, Grammy, Tony and Academy Awards. His numerous other accolades include winning a Kennedy Center Honor, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, the AFI Life Achievement Award, a BFI Fellowship, a National Medal of Arts, a BAFTA Fellowship, and an Honorary Academy Award in 2024. Phew!

The book was written by Brooks and three-time Tony Award winner Thomas Stroman ( Annie, Hairspray, Young Frankenstein ), and the musical features original choreography by five-time Tony Award winner Susan Stroman ( Oklahoma!, Crazy for You, Smash ).

This production is directed by Olivier Award-winning comedian, playwright and director Patrick Marber, best known for his directing work on Leopoldstadt at Wyndham’s Theatre, The Old Neighbourhood at the Royal Court and Blue Remembered Hills at the National Theatre

You’ll want to be a producer this autumn! This “buoyantly vulgar” (Standard) musical is an uproarious delight, so grab a ticket for the best show in London about the worst show on Broadway. Book today for The Producers at the Garrick Theatre and get ready to do “Der Guten Tag Hop Clop” all the way home.

Packed with colourful characters and costumes, fun sing-a-longs, lots of surprises, and an engaging story that we all know and love, this stage adaptation is magical, roar-some fun for the whole family.

shows.title: The Truth
shows.description:
Oscar Winner Florian Zeller’s acclaimed play The Truth arrives at the Apollo Theatre, in the heart of Leicester Square, for a strictly limited season. This major revival of the razor-sharp comedy explores love, lies and self-deception, and comes to London for a strictly limited run, starring Tony nominee Stephen Mangan, comedy icon Ardal O’Hanlon, Olivier winner Janie Dee and Miranda star Sarah Hadland. Are you ready to learn the truth? Secure your tickets to this “ingenious puzzle of a play” (London Theatre) today.

Michel is having an affair. Or at least, that’s the truth, as far as he’s concerned. Married to Laurence, he is also involved with Alice, the wife of his best friend, Paul. When Alice suggests confessing to spare their spouses further deception, Michel resists, convinced that honesty would cause more harm than good.

As the couples’ relationships intertwine, truths are revealed, concealed and reshaped. Each character has their own version of events, and what seems certain in one moment is cleverly overturned in the next. With swift dialogue and escalating misunderstandings, The Truth examines how lies can protect, destroy or even sustain relationships, asking whether complete honesty is always the best policy.

Originally titled La Vérité , the play premiered in Paris in 2011 and quickly became a hit, cementing Zeller’s reputation as one of Europe’s most exciting contemporary playwrights. Zeller's acclaim grew further with his play The Father , which won the 2014 Molière Award for Best Play and was later adapted into an Academy Award-winning film starring Anthony Hopkins, and he  is now one of the most internationally performed French playwrights of his generation. The Truth debuted in London in 2016, and now returns in the first major UK revival of the production in over ten years.

The star-studded, award-winning cast of The Truth includes:

Roles are to be confirmed.

The Truth is written by Academy Award-winning French playwright Florian Zeller ( The Father, The Son, The Mother ). The English-language version is translated by Tony winner and Academy Award nominee Christopher Hampton ( Sunset Boulevard, Les Liaisons Dangereuses , Atonement ).

Lindsay Posner directs. Posner is an Olivier-winning British theatre director. His credits include Noises Off for the Old Vic, Death and the Maiden at the Royal Court, The Rivals starring David Tennant for the RSC, Sexual Perversity in Chicago starring Matthew Perry at the Harold Pinter Theatre, and A View from the Bridge for Duke of York’s Theatre.

Directed by Olivier winner Lindsey Posner, with a script by Oscar winner Florian Zeller, translated by Tony Winner Christopher Hampton, and a star-studded cast including comedy icons Stephen Mangan and Ardal O’Hanlon, The Truth is truly unmissable theatre. As secrets unravel and loyalties are tested, this sharply witty play invites audiences to question just how honest we really want our relationships to be - and whether there ever is one objective truth. Book your tickets for The Truth at the Apollo Theatre today.

shows.title: To Kill A Mockingbird
shows.description:
This landmark revival of To Kill A Mockingbird comes to the Wyndham’s Theatre, just off Leicester Square, following a huge UK and Ireland tour. Based on Harper Lee’s iconic Pulitzer Prize-winning novel about racial tensions in Southern America, Oscar-winner Aaron Sorkin’s critically acclaimed stage adaptation has taken Broadway and the West End by storm and now returns to London for a strictly limited run. This “powerful. Important. Deeply moving” (Sunday Express) play is unmissable - secure your tickets today.

Alabama, 1934, and successful lawyer Atticus Finch is a pillar of his community, determined to encourage empathy and kindness in his children, Scout and Jem. But when Finch finds himself at the centre of a shocking court case, in which a Black man may have been falsely accused, he is pushed to the very limits of his own capacity for understanding. Can Finch uncover the truth, when the people of the town seem determined to obscure it?

To Kill a Mockingbird is based on the novel by Harper Lee, which was inspired by experiences from the author’s own childhood. The book was first published in 1960, to immediate acclaim, winning the Pulitzer Prize a year later. Widely considered to be one of the Greatest American Novels, the book is not without controversy, with the novel topping lists of banned books due to its themes of racial injustice and the use of racial slurs within the text.

Sorkin’s adaptation was written in 2018, following a previous stage adaptation by Christopher Sergel written in 1990, and reframes the story to make Finch the central character - as both the previous production and the novel are narrated from Scout, Finch’s six-year-old daughter’s point of view. Sorkin’s adaptation debuted on Broadway in 2018, earning nine Tony nominations and winning one, and was followed by a West End production in 2022, which was nominated for five Olivier awards. The play embarks on a huge UK and Ireland tour in 2026, before returning to the West End for a strictly limited run.

Richard Coyle will be reprising his role as Atticus Finch from the UK tour.

Further casting for the West End production of To Kill A Mockingbird is to be announced.

To Kill a Mockingbird is adapted from Harper Lee’s novel by Aaron Sorkin. Sorkin is an American writer, best known for creating and writing TV shows The West Wing and The Newsroom, and for films The Social Network and A Few Good Men . Sorkin is an Academy Award, BAFTA and Golden Globe winner.

Bartlett Sher directs. Sher is a Tony Award-winning American director and the former director of New York’s Lincoln Centre Theater. His credits include My Fair Lady, Oslo, The Light in the Piazza, The King and I , and South Pacific .

This award-winning revival of one of the greatest American stories of all time is “radical and pulsing with relevance” (Chicago Tribune), adapted by Academy Award winner Aaron Sorkin. “ Mockingbird soars anew in Sorkin’s blistering adaptation” (Daily Mail) - you won’t want to miss it. Secure your tickets for To Kill A Mockingbird at Wyndham’s Theatre today.

shows.title: Trainspotting The Musical
shows.description:
Trainspotting the Musical makes its world premiere this July at the Theatre Royal Haymarket, just a short walk from Piccadilly Circus. This brand new musical adapts Irvine Welsh’s novel, about a group of friends struggling with addiction in 1990s Edinburgh. The musical has a book by Welsh himself, and features original songs co-written by Welsh and dance legend Steve Mac, along with iconic tracks from the 1996 hit film adaptation, which starred Ewan McGregor. Trainspotting comes to London for a strictly limited run this summer - so choose life, choose tickets, and book today.

Leith, Edinburgh, in the 1990s: cynical Renton and his friends Sick Boy, Begbie, Spud, Tommy, and Kelly are trying to choose life - but life doesn't seem to want to choose them. Struggling with heroin addiction and economic deprivation, the gang faces the trials and tribulations of getting clean, love, sex and relationships, and earning some cash, as they try to find their place in a society that has pegged them as outcasts.

Darkly funny, life-affirming, and deeply nostalgic, this genre-defying musical is Trainspotting as you’ve never seen it before, featuring your favourite tunes from the film alongside brand-new songs.

Trainspotting the Musica l is based on the book, and its film adaptation, of the same name. Published in 1993, Trainspotting was the debut novel by Scottish author Irvine Welsh, written in Scots and Scottish English. Trainspotting quickly became a cult hit and was shortlisted for the 1993 Booker Prize. Three sequel novels and a prequel have also been released.

A film adaptation was made in 1996, directed by Danny Boyle, which starred Ewan McGregor, Johnny Lee Miller and Robert Carlise. The film was a critical and commercial success; the highest-grossing film of the year, Trainspotting earned an Academy Award nomination and won BAFTAs for Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Actor. Often considered to be one of the top films of the 90s, in 2004 Trainspotting was voted the best Scottish film of all time in a public poll, and was ranked tenth in the BFI’s list of the Top 100 British films of the 20th century. A sequel, T2 Trainspotting , was released in 2017.

The novel has previously been adapted for the stage both as a play in the mid-90s and as an immersive theatre show, Trainspotting Live , in 2013, which was also a critical success.

Confirmed casting includes:

Trainspotting the Musical is written by Irvine Welsh, adapted from his own novel of the same name. Music and Lyrics are co-written by Welsh and dance music pioneer Stephen McGuinness, aka Steve Mac (remixes on work by artists including Michael Jackson, Barry White, Amy Winehouse, INXS). The show is directed and developed by Caroline Jay Ranger ( Only Fools and Horses the musical, Fawlty Towers Live ).

Welsh is a Scottish author, screenwriter and playwright, best known for his novels, frequently written in an Edinburgh dialect Scots and set in his native Scotland, which depict themes of working-class life, drug addiction, and social alienation. Notable works include Trainspotting sequels/prequels Porno and Skagboys , as well as his novels and short story collections Glue , The Acid House , and Filth , which was also adapted into a film starring James McAvoy.

Thirty years on, the story that defined a generation returns as you’ve never seen it before. You won't want to miss this defiant, provocative and truly unforgettable new musical as it makes its world premiere in London before embarking on a nationwide tour. So join the outsiders, feel the rush, and choose life - book your tickets for Trainspotting the Musical at the Theatre Royal Haymarket today.

sources.title_as_listed: Trial By Jury & The Zoo - English National Opera

shows.description:
A wildly entertaining double-bill of opera awaits you at the London Coliseum, a short walk from Trafalgar Square. Expect hilarity, an unexpected and heaps of chaos from Trial By Jury & The Zoo and experience a rare glimpse of Sullivan’s early work alongside a piece from one of opera’s most legendary partnerships for a limited time. Secure your tickets today!

The Zoo follows two young lovers who ultimately become engaged. Set in the gardens of a zoo, Thomas is concerned that Eliza, a refreshment seller, only cares about his money. Duke of Islington, a nobleman, is also in love with Eliza and, to win her affections, disguises himself as an ordinary man who works at the zoo. It’s a story of hidden identities, secret marriages and mischievous mix-ups that will have you laughing out loud.

Trial by Jury takes us to the courtroom, where Angelina is suing her former fiancé, Edwin, for breach of promise. What unfolds in this one-act opera is chaos, joyous absurdity, and an unexpected twist as the jury is easily swayed by emotion rather than the facts of the case. Trial by Jury is ultimately a sharp, humnourous satire of the legal system.

The Zoo is an opera by Gilbert and Rowe that made its premiere at the St James’s Theatre in London in 1875, before concluding its run at the Haymarket Theatre after a five-week run. There have been revivals of the piece in 1875 and 1879. The last time it was fully staged in London was at the Finborough Theatre in 2007.

Trial By Jury is an opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, one of opera’s most legendary partnerships. It initially ran for 131 performances in London, where it made its debut. After its original production in 1875, it has been revived multiple times. This will be the first time this production is staged at the ENO.

Frank Baum’s beloved characters from ‘The Wonderful Wizard of Oz’, revealing the decisions and events that shape the destinies of two unlikely university friends on their journey to becoming ‘Glinda The Good’ and the ‘Wicked Witch of the West’.

shows.title: A Christmas Carol
shows.description:
Warm your cockles at Waterloo's historic Old Vic Theatre this festive season as their magical, smash-hit production of A Christmas Carol returns for its tenth year. Charles Dickens’ tale of miserly Scrooge discovering the spirit of the season is “pure joy to behold” (The Telegraph) on stage, in a play that fills the theatre to the brim with goodwill, merriment and the smell of freshly baked mince pies.

Tight-fisted moneylender Ebenezer Scrooge has only one thing on his mind: money, and how to make more of it. Even Christmas Day can’t stop him, a fact his employee, Bob Cratchit, knows only too well when he has to grovel for a day off with his family. But everything changes when Scrooge is visited by the ghost of an old colleague on Christmas Eve. Marley has an ominous warning: before dawn breaks on Christmas morning, he will encounter three more ghosts with a chilling message…

Charles Dickens’s beloved story about a man whose heart thaws as he embraces the spirit of Christmas has been a firm favourite for over 170 years. It is one of the most adapted stories ever told, with everything from musicals to Muppets bringing the cast - including Cratchit, Tiny Tim, and the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come - to life for several generations.

Step into the Old Vic auditorium and you will be struck by the hustle and bustle of Victorian England, and the smell of oranges and mince pies. This unique in-the-round staging brims with music, merriment and the joys of the most wonderful time of the year. Since premiering in 2017, director Matthew Warchus (Matilda the Musical ) and playwright Jack Thorne’s ( Harry Potter and the Cursed Child ) A Christmas Carol at the Old Vic is now a festive tradition that theatregoers return to again and again.

Casting is to be announced.

Start a new tradition for your family with A Christmas Carol tickets this year. Inside the Old Vic, you’ll feel as if you’ve dropped right into the heart of Victorian London! Find out why this classic tale remains one of the most beloved Christmas stories; this show is a treat that will touch even the frostiest of hearts this winter.

shows.title: ABBA Voyage
shows.description:
Dance the night away to ABBA’s greatest hits in a concert like no other. Mixing the physical, the digital, and some of pop’s most irresistible hits, join Agnetha, Benny, Bjorn and Anni-Frid for the spectacular ABBA Voyage at ABBA Arena close to London's Olympic Park. If you're new to the show, our complete guide to everything you need to know is the perfect place to start.

Named after their first new album in 40 years, ABBA Voyage is an unforgettable live experience designed with all four members of ABBA, for their fans. Using cutting-edge motion capture technology, the pop quartet will appear as digital avatars on stage, accompanied by a 10-piece band made up of today’s best musicians.

The purpose-built ABBA Arena in East London was constructed especially for this never-before-seen concert and will immerse audiences in the magic of ABBA whether they’re on the Dance Floor or enjoying the music from their seats.

Fans of the chart-topping Swedish group can channel their inner dancing queens as they sing along to a setlist of ABBA’s most popular songs, taken from albums across the decades.

Get ready to dance and jive to “Dancing Queen”, sing along to the melody of “Thank You For The Music”, dance up a storm to “Waterloo” and get your friends together to enjoy the irresistible “Mamma Mia”!

Other songs included in ABBA Voyage include “The Visitors”, “SOS”, “Knowing Me, Knowing You”, “Chiquitita”, “Fernando”, “Does Your Mother Know”, Lay All Your Love On Me”, “The Winner Takes It All”, and “Voulez-Vous”. Find out more with our ultimate guide to the ABBA Voyage setlist .

While ABBA themselves do not appear in ABBA Voyage , the ABBAtars have been modelled from them using motion capture technology that is so cutting-edge, you will hardly believe that you aren’t seeing the real deal on stage!

To achieve the uncanny effect, the group performed wearing motion capture suits for five weeks, and 160 cameras scanned every inch of their body movements and facial expressions to create the ultimate likeness of themselves from the 1970s.

For a deep dive into the groundbreaking technology, read our full guide on how ABBA Voyage works .

Whether you choose to sit, stand or party in a Dance Booth, you will have the time of your life at ABBA Voyage . Get ready to enjoy one of the world’s biggest pop acts as you’ve never seen them before.

shows.title: Angel's Bone
shows.description:
This Autumn, Angel’s Bone , one of the most significant operatic works of the past decade, plays at the London Coliseum, just off Leicester Square, in a momentous revival from the English National Opera. Directed by Kip Williams, this dark fable delves into the harrowing realities of modern-day slavery and human trafficking. Secure your tickets to English National Opera: Angel’s Bone today.

A desperate couple who long for a better life, Angel’s Bone follows what happens when Mr and Mrs X.E. discover two wounded angels in their garden. As they set out to nurse them back to health, what begins as an act of apparent compassion quickly spirals into a stark look at greed and exploitation. Set to a pulsating score that fuses medieval polyphony, punk, electronics, chamber music and cabaret, Angel’s Bone will grip audiences with its unflinching take on human trafficking and modern-day slavery.

Composed by Du Yun and with a libretto by the playwright and filmmaker, Royce Vavrek, the “disturbing, powerful and original” (The Washington Post) Angel’s Bone made its world premiere in 2016 in New York. It was staged as part of the Prototype Festival and received the 2017 Pulitzer Prize for Music.

It was staged again in Asia at the Kwai Tsing Theatre in Hong Kong in 2018, before a streamed production by The Ventura College was streamed in 2021.

This new production by Kip Williams will receive a UK premiere in Greater Manchester in May, before heading to the London Coliseum from October 2026. The Manchester production is in collaboration with the BBC Philharmonic Orchestra and Kantos Chamber Choir.

Allison Cook, a Scottish mezzo-soprano and singing actress, will star as Mrs X.E. in this new production of Angel’s Bone . Her other credits with the English National Opera include the 2024 production of Duke Bluebeard’s Castle . Rodney Earl Clake, who has opera and musical theatre experience, will star as Mr X.E.

Mariam Wallentin will star in the role of Girl Angel. The Swedish cross-genre musician and voice actress will make her ENO debut in this production, but is best known as one half of the acclaimed duo Wildbirds & Peacedrums. She will be joined by the Scottish tenor Matthew McKinney in the role of Boy Angel.

Angel’s Bone is composed by Du Yun, the first Asian woman to receive the Pulitzer Prize for Music. Her other opera credits include In Our Daughter’s Eyes and Sweet Land .

The multi-award-winning theatre and opera director Kip Williams will make his UK opera debut with this production of Angel’s Bone . His recent credits include Dracula starring Cynthia Erivo, The Maids at Donmar Warehouse and The Picture of Dorian Gray starring Sarah Snook.

Marg Horwell, the Olivier Award-winning designer, who has collaborated with Kip, is also working on this production. Some of her other credits include The Seagull and Opera Australia’s production of Carmen . Completing the creative team is Jack Knowles as Lighting Designer, Ash J Woodward as Video Designer, and Dominic Bilkey and Joseph Reiser, who will be the Co-Sound Designers. The internationally renowned conductor Baldur Brönniman will lead the performances.

You won’t want to miss your chance to experience Du Yun’s “audacious and searing” (The New York Times) opera as it takes to the stage for the first time in nearly a decade. Prepare to be completely enthralled by Kip Williams genius artistry – secure your tickets for English National Opera: Angel’s Bone at the London Coliseum today.

shows.title: As You Like It
shows.description:
All of London's a stage this summer as As You Like It returns to Shakespeare’s Globe Theatre, on Bankside. Escape the confines of the city and revel in the forest with this hilarious play about two young women who flee their stifling lives in court and head into the woods, seeking self-discovery. This bold new adaptation of Shakespeare’s witty, gender-bending comedy simmers with lust, live music and festival spirit, and celebrates freedom, friendship and the redemptive power of love. Secure your tickets today!

Rosalind and Celia have escaped the restrictions of the court and are searching for Rosalind’s father, the exiled Duke. Orlando has fallen head over heels and wants the whole world to know about it. And, deep in the Forest of Arden, unexpected meetings, long-awaited reunions and incredible transformations are about to take place…

As You Like It is an exuberant celebration of love as friends, cousins, couples and parents come together under the liberating canopy of the forest. It is one of Shakespeare’s best-known and best-loved comedies, and has been performed all over the world and reinterpreted in myriad ways since it was written over 400 years ago.

As You Like It is one of William Shakespeare’s most beloved pastoral comedies, believed to have been written in 1599 or early 1600. It was first published in the First Folio in 1623, but no earlier quarto version survives. The play is thought to have premiered at the Globe Theatre, captivating Elizabethan audiences with its mix of romance, wit, and disguise. Based on Thomas Lodge’s prose romance Rosalynde , Shakespeare’s version transforms the story with greater emotional depth and clever wordplay. Set in the idyllic Forest of Arden, it explores themes of love, gender, exile, and nature versus society.

As You Like It remains a popular choice for modern productions, thanks to its engaging heroine and witty philosophical musings, including the famous “All the world’s a stage” monologue. Its playful subversion of gender roles and celebration of love in many forms continue to resonate with contemporary audiences, and this brand new production transplants the action to a vibrant, festival-themed forest where lust, love and self-discovery are waiting just around the corner or... tree!

Confirmed cast includes:

Further casting is to be announced.

As You Like It is written by William Shakespeare.

This production is co‑directed by Associate Artistic Director of Shakespeare’s Globe and former Artistic Director of the Lyric Hammersmith, Sean Holmes ( Romeo and Juliet, Pinocchio ), and writer-director Charlie Josephine ( Pinocchio, Cowbois ), who also stars as Orlando. Design is by Paul Wills ( The Comedy of Errors, The Tempest ) with further creative team to be confirmed.

You won't just like it - you’ll love it! As You Like It is a playful, joyous story, and one of Shakespeare’s most popular comedies - and this sexy, spirited and bold new production is more liberating than ever before. Journey into the Forest of Arden and delight in what - and who - you find: secure your tickets for As You Like It at Shakespeare's Globe Theatre today.

It is a truth universally acknowledged that an improv troupe with a taste for Jane Austen must be in want of an audience… Improv fans and Austenites rejoice as the riotous Austentatious play returns to The Strand at the Vaudeville Theatre. Enjoy one of the best nights out in the West End, thanks to a talented team who create a brand new story every night. Hold onto your bonnets and get ready for wit, romance, laughs and more!

How many novels did Jane Austen write? Get ready to discover a few new stories as the team behind Austentatious on stage take your title suggestions and turn them into fantastic period romps. From Mansfield Shark to The Longbourne Identity via The Empire Line Strikes Back , this sharp, smart and sometimes chaotic show is a good-natured tribute to the beloved Pride and Prejudice author. Expect full period dress, fulsome laughter, and a few surprises that will have you blushing more than Mr Darcy’s fan club!

Austentatious has a long and respectable history, starting back in 2011. It entered society - or to you and I, the theatre scene - in London before travelling up to Edinburgh, where it received rave reviews and played to sold-out crowds. Since 2017 it has held Monday night residencies at various West End theatres, and it is the talk of all the most influential newspapers: The Times called it a “potboiler of a parody, joyously performed” in their five-star review.

Austentatious is currently performed by a cast of six, including original members and creators Joseph Morpurgo and Rachel Parris ( Late Night Mash ). Other members of the company include award-winning comedian, actress and Griefcast podcast host Cariad Lloyd, Graham Dickson, Amy Cooke-Hodgson, Charlotte Gittins, and Daniel Nills Roberts.

The group pull on their petticoats, dust off their cravats and practice their stiff upper lip before every performance to bring you the very best madcap improv you could ask for.

Austentatious is the perfect night out whether you’re a die-hard Austenite or only caught the end of Pride and Prejudice on television. This “pop-up book of creative genius” (Broadway Baby), full of whip-smart jokes and silly plots that are guaranteed to put a smile on your face. shows.title: Cirque Alice
shows.description:
This Christmas, embark on a unique, kaleidoscopic adventure with some of the world’s greatest performers around the globe. Lewis Carroll’s timeless tale provides the perfect backdrop for this new show, which makes its European premiere this festive season. Playing at the Royal Festival Hall, located on the South Bank of the River Thames, Cirque Alice will dazzle audiences of all ages with a "wondrous evening filled to overflowing with incredible memories that will last a lifetime!" (Australian Arts Review).

Filled with some of the most eccentric and larger-than-life characters, Cirque Alice reimagines the popular classic story by Lewis Carroll. The story follows a girl named Alice who falls down a rabbit hole into a different world where she encounters curious characters like the Mad Hatter and the Queen of Hearts in a quest to get back home.

This new production is brought to life by a collective of aerialists, contortionists, and puppeteers, along with special guest music and comedy artists. Cirque Alice is set to a captivating soundtrack of newly arranged contemporary renditions of some of the world’s favourite classical hits.

Cirque Alice made its debut with sell-out seasons in Australia and Singapore. Brought to life by the same creators behind The Illusionists and Circus 1903 , this production marks the European premiere with a festive season at the Southbank Centre’s Royal Festival Hall.

The Creative Team for Cirque Alice is headed by creative directors Ash Jacks McCready and Kirsty Painter, with choreography by Dane Bates, costumes by Angela Aaron, lighting by Hugo Mercier and musical arrangements by Martin Raabe-Olsen & Marius Christiansen. Roast Productions and Senbla present the show in association with Tim Lawson and Simon Painter.

Take a trip down the rabbit hole into the breathtaking world of Cirque Alice at the Southbank Centre's Royal Festival Hall this Christmas. Perfect for families, festive outings, or special celebrations; book your tickets to see the "wonderland of its own making" (The Fame Reporter) - and don’t be late!
