shows.title: Glengarry Glen Ross
shows.description:
A major revival of Pulitzer Prize-winning play Glengarry Glen Ross comes to the Old Vic Theatre, just by Waterloo, this summer. David Mamet's blistering modern classic delves into the corrupt, capitalistic world of four ruthless real estate agents, who are willing to do anything to make a sale, living by the mantra “Always be closing!”. Directed by Tony winner Patrick Marber, this production marks the play's first major revival in London in almost a decade, and changes the game with an all-female cast. You won't want to miss it!

The unseen owners of a Chicago real estate company declare a sales contest: the highest-earning seller will snag the grand prize, a Cadillac, and the glory, while second place will earn a set of steak knives - but the two worst performers will be fired effective immediately. Over the course of two days, four corrupt estate agents battle it out to be top dog, willing to do whatever it takes to win.

When newcomer and upstart, the ruthless Ricky Roma, takes the lead, the other agents - fallen-from-grace former top earner Shelley Levene, timid and unassuming George Aaronow and the loudmouthed, envious Moss - scramble to take the top spot. But when a robbery at the agency adds extra pressure, the office soon becomes a boiling pot of backstabbing, betrayal and bribery.

The exciting all-female cast for this revival includes:

Glengarry Glen Ross premiered at London’s National Theatre in 1983. The show was a critical success, and opened on Broadway the following year, earning four Tony nominations, a Drama Desk Award and the Pulitzer Prize for drama. A film adaptation with an expanded script by Mamet was made in 1992, starring Al Pacino, Jack Lemmon and Alec Baldwin, which was nominated for an Academy Award and a Golden Globe. The show has been revived countless times over the years, most recently in a 2025 Tony-nominated production starring Succession's Kieran Culkin, but this brand new Old Vic production flips the script on its head, featuring an all-female cast for the very first time.

Glengarry Glen Ross is written by Pulitzer and Tony-winning playwright David Mamet. Renowned for his scintillating, snappily realist dialogue and sometimes controversial characters, Mamet’s best-known works include Oleanna, Speed-The-Plough, Bitter Wheat and Race . Mamet is a founding member of the acclaimed Atlanta Theatre Company and an inductee of the American Theatre Hall of Fame.

Patrick Marber directs. Marber is a playwright and director, whose credits include Leopoldstadt, Don Juan in Soho, Travesties and The Producers . Marber also directed the recent Broadway revival of Glengarry Glen Ross in 2025. Marber’s many accolades for his writing and directing work include Tony, Olivier and BAFTA awards.

The Old Vic makes history with this all-female premiere of one of the great American modern classics. With an explosive script, an award-winning creative team, and a boundary-breaking cast, Glengarry Glen Ross is not to be missed. So make sure you close on this deal - book tickets for Glengarry Glen Ross at The Old Vic Theatre today!

shows.title: Here Comes J. Edgar! A Comedy Musical

Here Comes J. Edgar! A Comedy Musical

shows.description:
Star of the hit US TV series Mad Men, Bryan Batt is set to take London by storm this Summer as J Edgar Hoover in the world premiere of the sizzling new comedy musical, HERE COMES J. EDGAR! A COMEDY MUSICAL, which opens at King’s Head Theatre in July.

Batt makes his London stage debut in the role of the long-serving FBI boss in the eagerly-awaited stage-show, written by US comedy aristocracy, Harry Shearer (The Simpsons and This Is Spinal Tap) and Tom Leopold (Seinfeld and Cheers), with a musical score written by the legendary musician, composer, arranger, and conductor Peter Matz (Barbra Streisand and Carol Burnett)

This raucous, no-holds-barred musical tells the public and private story of J. Edgar Hoover who, as director of the FBI from 1924 to 1972, secured his position as the most powerful man in America by gathering information on the private lives of others. Yet, behind all the machismo, was his concealed sexuality, his secret partying and his lifelong love affair with his deputy, Clyde Tolson. This was a man who stopped at nothing to use the secrets of others to build and exert his control … yet underneath the petticoats of power lay his own secrets … hidden … in plain sight.

This weird and twisted tale is told in the style of a 1950s musical romantic comedy. What emerges is a sharp and irrepressible comic musical about the love of power and the power of love … and what a simple black dress and a single strand of pearls can do for a guy!

This show tells the spectacular queer tale of J. Edgar Hoover, the American director of the FBI.

shows.title: Liberace & Liza: A Tribute
shows.description:
Feel good musical mashup Liberace and Liza: A Tribute comes to the West End this June, following a sell-out UK tour. This hilariously camp musical comedy imagines a performance between Liberace and Liza Minelli that never happened - but should have! Featuring all your favourite Liza songs and surprise covers, the show comes to the Harold Pinter Theatre, in the heart of Picadilly, for a strictly limited run. Secure your tickets today.

Famed pianist Liberace and singer, actress and powerhouse performer Liza Minelli may not have ever worked together - but this stunning show imagines how it might have gone if they had! Both renowned for their camp sensibilities, outrageous costumes and all-around fabulousness, Liza and Liberace make the perfect pair! This comedy tribute to two OTT icons is dripping with sequins and features iconic songs, including “Over the Rainbow”, “New York, New York” and, of course, “Cabaret” as well as some unexpected modern covers of artists such as Lady Gaga and Britney Spears, all accompanied by dazzling piano and lashings of laughs!

Liberace and Liza: A Tribute won the Best Show Offies Assessors’ Award at the Brighton Fringe. The show embarked on a smash hit tour of the UK and US tour in 2026, and shimmers into the West End for a strictly limited run before heading off to Edinburgh Fringe.

The show is created and performed by Jillian Snow, as Liza, and David Saffert, as Liberace.

Snow is a comedian and actress from New York City. Her credits include performances at 54 Below, Gotham Comedy Club and the Broadway Rose Theatre, Oregon.

Saffert is a classically trained pianist and performer from Wisconsin, US. His credits include work with the Guthrie Theatre, Oregon Shakespeare Festival and Portland Gay Men’s Choir. His solo piano album Stopping Time was released in 2025.

Liberace and Liza: A Tribute is produced by Robert C Kelly, whose credits include producing shows for a wide variety of stars, including Elaine Paige and Jenny Eclair, as well as musicals, including Menopause the Musical, Girls Night the Musical, and Always Patsy Cline .

So put down the knitting, the book and the broom… and come to the West End, for a camp old time with Liberace and Liza ! Expect heaps of humour, gallons of glitter and toe-tapping tunes in this hilarious musical tribute to two absolute icons. Secure your tickets for Liberace and Liza: A Tribute at the Harold Pinter Theatre today!

shows.title: Operation Mincemeat
shows.description:
Did you know that World War Two was quite possibly won by a well-dressed corpse? Join a team of secret agents at Covent Garden's Fortune Theatre for the high-spirited, delightfully eccentric new musical Operation Mincemeat . Boasting 67 five-star reviews and an Olivier Award for Best New Musical, this is one of the most fun nights out in the West End, with a hardworking cast bringing slapstick humour, catchy songs and uplifting stories of friendship and love to the stage.

The year is 1943 and the Allies are losing the war. From the great young minds at MI5 comes a bizarre but brilliant idea to wrongfoot the Nazis: dress a corpse up, handcuff a briefcase of “Top Secret” documents to his arm, and wash him up on the coast of Spain.

Stranger than fiction but 100% true, this madcap plan to fool Hitler is adapted into a new musical by fringe theatre company SplitLip. Playfully dubbed “ Singin’ in the Rain meets Strangers on a Train ”, the Operation Mincemeat musical features a fast-paced plot, wicked humour and original songs including “God, That’s Brilliant”.

Operation Mincemeat is the proud owner of 67 five-star reviews - and counting! The Stage declared it a “brilliant spy thriller, a brilliant comedy, and a brilliant musical all rolled into one”, and newspapers across the UK followed suit.

This “irrepressible wartime musical is a West End triumph” (The Guardian), “a delight from start to finish” (Time Out) and a “glorious combination of ingenious, silly and surprisingly moving” (The Telegraph).

If you’re still not convinced, read theatregoer reviews below, and book your tickets for a night of high-spirited and irrepressible entertainment.

The Operation Mincemeat musical cast consists of five actors who gamely play every role. It has already tickled theatregoers’ funny bones, with sold-out runs at New Diorama Theatre, Southwark Playhouse and Riverside Studios and has extended several times since opening at the Fortune Theatre in 2023.

SplitLip’s team includes David Cumming, Felix Hagan, Natasha Hodgson and Zoë Roberts - and all four co-wrote the book, music and lyrics to this irreverent hit.

Part spoof, part plucky fringe show and complete bags of fun: you’ll need a very stiff upper lip to resist Operation Mincemeat tickets in the West End! It’s the musical everyone has been talking about, showcases the best of British talent, and will have you on your feet for a standing ovation in no time.

shows.title: Raising Gays: A Concert Reading
shows.description:
In the small Somerset town of Little Malden, a group of parents meet in a support group for those raising queer children. When they find themselves unexpectedly organising a parents’ float for the town’s firstever Pride parade, they must confront their own beliefs, biases and fears in their determination to show up for their kids.

Written by Micha Mirto and Jordan Paul Clarke, RAISING GAYS is a brand new musical about those parents frantically googling pronouns, Pride flags and purple hair dye in a well-meaning – but often misjudged – endeavour to support their children.

The stakes could not be higher. There’s no manual and a hundred different ways to mess it all up.

Brimming with humour and heart – and completely gorgeous tunes – RAISING GAYS is a musical for everyone who’s ever had a kid (or a parent).

shows.title: The Enormous Crocodile
shows.description:
Get ready for a snappy, toe-tapping treat as The Enormous Crocodile slithers back to London this summer, at the Lyric Hammersmith in the heart of Hammersmith! This wickedly funny musical, based on Roald Dahl’s classic tale, brings the jungle to life with a menagerie of puppets, catchy tunes, and one very hungry crocodile on the hunt. Can the other animals stop his secret plans and clever tricks? Developed by an award-winning team, this lively family show is “inventive, jaunty and entertaining” (West End Best Friend) and is packed with adventure, laughs, and larger-than-life fun!

Deep in the jungle, the Enormous Crocodile is on the prowl, and he’s got a very particular craving… juicy little children! Armed with “secret plans and clever tricks,” this beastly reptile slithers his way through the jungle, determined to snap up a tasty treat. But the other animals have had enough of his greedy ways, and with a bit of teamwork (and a lot of courage), they just might be able to stop him before it’s too late!

This lively musical adaptation of Roald Dahl’s classic book is packed with cheeky humour, thrilling adventure, and toe-tapping tunes. With dazzling puppetry and a jungle bursting with character, it’s a riotous celebration of wit, friendship, and standing up to bullies - perfect for little explorers and their grown-ups alike!

Casting for this production is to be announced.

This mischievous musical is brought to life by an award-winning creative team. Suhayla El-Bushra ( The Ramayana, Hollyoaks ) adapts Roald Dahl’s classic tale with a script full of humour and heart, providing book and lyrics, while Ahmed Abdullahi Gallab, known for his musical work as Sinkane, provides the show’s infectious melodies alongside additional music and lyrics by Tom Brady ( Romeo and Juliet, Lord of the Rings ).

The production is developed and directed by Emily Lim ( Another Fine Mess ), with co-direction and inventive puppetry design by Toby Olié ( Life of Pi, Pinocchio ). Set and costume design is by Fly Davis ( Caroline, or Change, Standing at the Sky’s Edge ), with puppetry co-design and supervision by Daisy Beattie ( Ocean at the End of the Lane ). With this top-tier team at the helm, The Enormous Crocodile is packed with creative flair, jungle magic, and larger-than-life fun!

The Enormous Crocodile is a wickedly fun adventure for the whole family. Roald Dahl’s classic story bursts to life in the open air, making this the perfect summer treat for little theatre fans. Don’t miss your chance to see this “fun, vibrant and interactive” (Afridiziak Theatre News) mischievous musical - book your tickets for The Enormous Crocodile at the Lyric Hammersmith Theatre now, before they’re gobbled up!

shows.title: The Lives of Others
shows.description:
An extraordinary story of artistic censorship, state surveillance, and the relationship between art and politics is heading to the West End! Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck’s Academy Award-winning “triumph of nuanced tension” (Radio Times) is adapted for the stage for the first time by Robert Icke at the Adelphi Theatre, a short walk from the Victoria Embankment. Book your tickets to experience The Lives of Others in London for a limited time this autumn.

Transport to 1984 East Berlin, where Stasi officer Gerd Wiesler is spying on playwright Georg Dreyman and actress Christa-Maria Sieland from a nearby attic. Whilst Wiesler covertly monitors them for signs of opposition, he becomes absorbed in their lives... and ultimately conflicted by the surveillance and corruption carried out by the GDR regime he serves. Will the power of art be able to change the Stasi officer’s perspective on morality?

Inspired by Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck’s childhood visits to East Germany, The Lives of Others was created in response to a fear of a totalitarian state. The film was released in 2006 in Germany, where it was praised for how accurately it recreated the paranoia and clandestine rebellion experienced by people living in the shadow of the Berlin Wall.

It won several awards, including the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film and the BAFTA for Best Film Not in the English Language. The play is the first time it has been adapted for the stage.

The lead cast for The Lives of Others :

Keira Knightley is an Academy Award-nominated actress known for her extensive work in film and TV, as well as on stage, where she made her Broadway debut in 2015. Her credits include Atonement, Love Actually , The Pirates of the Caribbean, and The Misanthrope .

Luke Thompson plays the role of Georg. He is best known for his role in the hit Netflix series Bridgerton , as well as theatre credits including A Little Life , Hamlet and Oresteia .

Stephen Dillance stars as Gerd Wiesler. He has a well-established career on stage and screen, with credits including Game of Thrones , The Crown , A Long Day’s Journey Into Night and When We Have Sufficiently Tortured Each Other .

Produced by Sonia Friedman, The Lives of Others is directed by Robert Icke, who has collaborated with the writer and director of the original film to adapt this drama for the West End stage. Known for creating emotionally intense adaptations of classics, his recent credits include Uncle Vanya , The Doctor, and Player Kings .

Icke is joined on the creative team by designer Hildegard Bechtler, lighting designer Jon Clark and sound designer Giles Thomas. The Lives of Others features original music by Max Richter.

Arriving in the West End this autumn for a limited time, this brand-new psychological surveillance thriller reveals the power of listening. Brought to the stage by an exceptionally talented cast, including Academy Award-nominated actress Keira Knightley, this will showcase just how gripping theatre can be. Book your tickets for The Lives of Others at Adelphi Theatre today!

shows.description:
Will an obsession with fame be the death of us?
For one night only, ENO welcomes a Nederlandse Reisopera and Phion Symphony Orchestra guest production for the UK premiere of this exceptional new comic opera following the world premiere in The Netherlands in April 2026.
This exuberant and subversive black farce, by British Russian composer
Elena Langer
, mocks and questions our obsession with celebrity – and encourages us to embrace the highs and lows of our turbulent, gruesome, joyful and beautiful life.
Originally commissioned by the Stanislavski Nemirovich-Danchenko Theatre in Moscow, this comic opera was cancelled after the invasion of Ukraine. The piece was deemed insufficiently patriotic.
The existential angst of Semyón Podsekayev drives him to suicide, but he hopes that playing the tuba will save him. A plan that fails miserably.
TV presenter Ivan Vane is one of several characters keen to use Semyón’s possible suicide for their own gain. In the second act, we see Vane’s reality show The Naked Truth, in which Semyón’s desire to commit suicide – and everyone’s desire to profit financially from it – becomes a public game.

shows.title: Tosca
shows.description:
Head to the London Coliseum, just off Leicester Square, to witness Annilese Miskimmon’s gripping new production of Tosca . Playing for a limited time, Puccini’s timeless opera intertwines one woman’s fight for freedom with the political landscape of 19th-century Rome. Secure your tickets to English National Opera: Tosca today.

Tosca is based on Victorien Sardou’s 1887 play, La Tosca . The story follows beautiful singer Tosca, who is deeply in love with artist Cavaradossi, but corrupt and cruel police chief Scarpia is competing for her affections. When Scarpia arrests Cavaradossi for aiding an escaped political prisoner, he gives Tosca a choice: reveal the prisoner’s location or watch Cavaradossi die. As Tosca becomes more desperate to reject Scarpia’s advances and derail his plans, she resorts to deadly tactics.

Composed by Giacomo Puccini with a libretto by Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa, Tosca first premiered in Rome in 1900, where many Italian political and cultural figures were in attendance. It has had mammoth success across the world since, and it has been featured in the English National Opera’s programme a lot over the years. Some of the notable productions of Tosca include Catherine Malfitano’s productions in 2010 and 2016. The last revival by Christof Loy was in 2022, starring Sinéad Campbell-Wallace and Adam Smith.

Axelle Fanyo makes her ENO debut in the role of Tosca. She is a Grammy Award-winning singer for the Best Opera Recording of Adriana Mater , where she starred in the role of Refka. Other credits include Les Contes d’Hoffmann , Poulenc’s Dialogues des Carmélites and Verdi’s Luisa Miller.

Tosca is conducted by the internationally-renowned Ben Glassberg.

Previously Artistic Director of the English National Opera, Annilese Miskimmon directs this production of Tosca at the London Coliseum. She has worked in some of the largest international opera houses around the world and was previously the Artistic Director and General Manager of the Danish National Opera. Her other credits include the musical productions of Bernstein’s On the Town and the world premiere of Pink Floyd’s French Revolution-based musical Ca Ira .

Amanda Holden translated this production of Tosca .

If you want to experience “opera at its most passionate and stinging” (Alexander Russell) later this year, then Tosca is just the show for you. See one of the most timeless stories unravel in a world of desire, fear, and resistance, not to be missed. Secure your tickets for English National Opera: Tosca at the London Coliseum today.

shows.title: Archduke
shows.description:
Innovative new play Archduke, from Pulitzer Prize finalist Rajiv Joseph, makes its London debut this summer at the Royal Court Theatre in the heart of Sloane Square. This explosive, darkly comic fictionalised imagining of the events leading up to the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand is “an ambitious mix of history, comedy and tragedy” (LA Times). You won't want to miss it - secure your tickets today.

1914: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparks a series of events that, within a month, trigger the beginning of World War I.

But who were the perpetrators of this shockingly pivotal event? While Franz Ferdinand’s name looms large in the history books, you’ve likely never heard the name of the man who pulled the trigger before - Gavrilo Princip.

When 19-year-old Gavrilo receives a terminal tuberculosis diagnosis, he fears he is running out of time - he wants to start a revolution, he wants to make a difference in this world, and he doesnt want to die a virgin. Starved for purpose, and food, Gavrilo and two of his fellow consumptives are desperate to be remembered. So when Serbian nationalist Captain Dragutin “Apis” Dimitrijevic offers them a chance to leave their mark on history, the dying young men are soon swept along in a plot that will change the world forever.

A “deft play of fact and fiction” (Philadelphia Inquirer), Archduke boldly retells the motivations of the group of young men who planned the assassination, framing them not as sinister masterminds, but as teenagers hungry, hapless, and susceptible to radicalisation.

Archduke first premiered in Los Angeles in 2017 and was also staged in Philadelphia, before making an Off-Broadway debut in November 2025. This production marks the show's European premiere.

Casting for this production is to be announced

Archduke is written by Rajiv Joseph. Joseph is a two-time Obie Award winner and a Lucille Lortel Award winner. His notable works include Guards at the Taj, Shalimar the Clown , and Bengal Tiger at the Baghdad Zoo (which premiered on Broadway starring Robin Williams) for which he was a finalist for the 2010 Pulitzer Prize for drama.

Lyndsey Turner directs. Turner is an Olivier winner and an Associate Director at the Sheffield Crucible and The Gate Theatre. Her credits include Chimerica, Machinal, Fathers and Sons, and Posh .

Production design is by Tony and Olivier winner Es Devlin, whose credits include The Lehman Trilogy, Chimerica, The Motive and the Cue, and design for the London and Rio Olympic ceremonies.

This “slyly relevant new period dramedy” (Variety) is a stark reminder that history is often shaped by those least qualified. Pulitzer finalist Ravji Joseph’s innovative, daring and alarmingly prescient play about radicalisation, morality and mortality is unmissable. Book tickets for Archduke at the Royal Court Theatre today.

shows.title: Cloud 9
shows.description:
This major new revival of Caryl Churchill’s trailblazing play Cloud 9 comes to the National Theatre’s Lyttelton stage, on Bankside, for a strictly limited run. Olivier winner Dominic Cooke directs this landmark work from one of Britain's most important playwrights, about colonialism, gender, power and the legacy of empire, in an explosive new staging. With a cast featuring Ghosts and Fresh Meat star Charlotte Ritchie, this promises to be unmissable theatre - book your tickets!

Africa, during the Victorian era: patriarch and colonial administrator Clive, his wife, son, and servant each struggle to fit into the roles their society expects of them.

The action shifts to 1970s London, but only a short few years have gone by for the characters. The family must make sense of themselves in a world where the repercussions of Empire linger, and freedom calls out to them all.

One of Churchill’s most renowned works, Cloud 9 was first workshopped with the Joint Stock Theatre Company in the late 1970s, premiering at Dartington College of Arts, Devon, in February 1979. The play has since had several major revivals, including a premiere at the Royal Court starring Miriam Margolyes and a run off-Broadway in New York. Renowned for it’s gender bending, experimental form, and razor-sharp critique of societal norms, Cloud 9 has featured in the National Theatre's NT2000 poll of the 100 most significant plays of the 20th century and Time Out New York's list of the "best plays of all time".

Charlotte Ritchie leads the cast as Maud/Victoria. Ritchie is best known for her roles in long-running BBC sitcom Ghosts , Call the Midwife , Channel 4's Fresh Meat , and her appearance on comedy show Taskmaster .

Dominic Cooke CBE directs. Cooke is a five-time Olivier winner and the former artistic director of the Royal Court Theatre. His credits include Follies, Mrs Warren's Profession starring Imelda Staunton, The Crucible starring Iain Glen, Clybourne Park, and Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom .

Cloud 9 is written by Caryl Churchill. Considered by many to be one of Britain’s greatest living playwrights, Churchill is best known for her plays Top Girls, Love and Information, and A Number . Churchill’s numerous accolades include an Olivier, an Obie Award, an Evening Standard Theatre Award and the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize for Playwrighting. She is an inductee of the American Theater Hall of Fame.

Caryl Churchill’s boundary-pushing, darkly comic satire comes to the National Theatre for a strictly limited run this winter. Exploding societal norms and exploring themes of colonial legacy, gender and power through a wryly farcical lens, Cloud 9 will turn how you think about theatre on its head. Starring Charlotte Ritchie and directed by Dominic Cooke, this is an unmissable revival of a modern classic - secure your tickets for Cloud 9 at the National Theatre’s Lyttelton stage today!

shows.title: Electra/Persona
shows.description:
Hollywood superstar Cate Blanchett stars in Electra/Persona , a scintillating new play based on the Ancient Greek classic and Ingmar Bergman's 1966 film. Coming to the National Theatre’s Lyttelton stage, on stunning Bankside, for a strictly limited run, Electra/Persona follows two women as the line between identity and performance begins to blur. Secure your tickets today.

Which role undid you in the end?

Electra: a daughter clings to the idea of justice as her grief and rage consume her.

Persona: an actress suddenly falls silent during a performance of Sophocles' play.

As the boundaries between self and role begin to blur, two women are drawn into an unsettling and intense encounter that fuses Ancient myth and modern psychology.

Electra/Persona is based on Electra by Sophocles and the award-winning 1966 Ingmar Bergman film Persona . This new adaptation by acclaimed director Benedict Andrews fuses these two great works of storytelling together in a boundary-pushing new play.

Cate Blanchett leads the cast. Blanchett is an Australian actor, perhaps best known for her roles as Galadriel in The Lord of the Rings and for her award-winning performances in Tar, The Aviator, Carol, and Notes On A Scandal . Blanchett’s numerous accolades include two Academy Awards (and multiple nominations), four BAFTAs, four Golden Globe Awards, and nominations for three Emmys, an Olivier Award and a Tony Award. Her stage credits include The Seagull, Platonov, The Maids and Oleanna .

Joining Blanchett are Nina Hoss ( The Cherry Orchard ) and Ella Lily Hyland ( Black Doves ).

Benedict Andrews directs and adapts the script from Bergman’s film and Sophocles’ play. Andrews is an Australian director and writer. His credits include A Streetcar Named Desire with Gillian Anderson, The Maids with Blanchett and Isabella Huppert and Una with Rooney Mara.

Don't miss your chance to see Hollywood Royalty on stage this Autumn, as Cate Blanchett returns to London for a strictly limited run. This powerful adaptation of two of the greatest stories of all time explores identity, duality and the masks we all wear and promises to be explosive, unmissable theatre. shows.title: Fences
shows.description:
August Wilson’s landmark play, Fences , comes to the Lyric Hammersmith, in the heart of Hammersmith, this October in a huge new revival from Red Pitch director Daniel Bailey. This Pulitzer and Tony-winning drama follows Troy, the patriarch of a working-class Black family, as he grapples with his past in the changing racial landscape of the 1950s. This “powerfully captivating” (London Theatre) play comes to London for a strictly limited run this autumn - don’t miss it.

Formerly the star player in the Black American baseball league, Troy Maxson now works a blue-collar job to try to provide for his wife and child. Having cheated death once before, Troy will do whatever it takes to survive. While Troy is haunted by his past, his wife Rose holds the family together, facing the changing landscape of 1950’s Pittsburgh with an unrelenting hope that the future will be brighter for their teenage son, Cory. But as Cory’s dreams clash with Troy’s fears, tempers flare, sparking a reckoning that will change the Maxsons’ lives forever.

Fences premiered at the Yale Repertory Theatre in 1985, receiving its Broadway debut in 1987. A critical success, the production, which starred James Earl Jones as Troy, won several Tony awards and the Pulitzer Prize for drama. A later revival starring Denzel Washington and Viola Davis also won several Tony awards, including for Best Revival, with Davis and Washington later reprising their roles in the 2016 Academy Award-nominated film adaptation. The show’s UK premiere was in 1990, at the Liverpool Playhouse. The play's most notable UK revival was a 2013 staging at Theatre Royal Bath, starring Lenny Henry, which later transferred to the West End.

Casting is to be announced.

Fences is written by August Wilson (1945 – 2005). Often considered to be one of the most important Black American writers, Wilson is best known for his “Pittsburgh Cycle”, which includes Fences, ten plays set in the city, chronicling the African-American experience throughout the 20th Century. His works include Ma Rainey's Black Bottom, Joe Turner's Come and Gone, and The Piano Lesson . Wilson was an inductee of the American Theatre Hall of Fame, a Pulitzer and Tony winner and an Academy Award and Emmy nominee.

Daniel Bailey directs. Bailey is a dramaturg, director, and writer, and a former Associate Director at the Bush Theatre. His credits include Red Pitch at the Bush, in the West End and in Washington DC, August in England with Lenny Henry at The Bush, The American Dream 2.0 at the Young Vic and Dropped for Channel 4.

This scintillating drama from one of America’s most influential writers of the 20th Century comes to London for a strictly limited run this October. Exploring ambition, racial politics and the legacy of the past, you won’t want to miss this “bruisingly powerful” (Independent) Tony and Pulitzer-winning play. Secure your tickets for Fences at the Lyric Hammersmith today.

shows.title: Hay Fever
shows.description:
Catch Christine Baranski and Richard E. Grant, two of the biggest stars from stage and screen, in a dazzling new production of Hay Fever this autumn. Noel Coward’s irresistible 1920s comedy, set in an English country house, will play at the Wyndham’s Theatre, just a short walk from the National Gallery in the heart of Central London. Book your tickets for Hay Fever and don’t miss out on director Emily Burns’ take on this irresistibly good show that is only in the West End for a limited time!

Described as a cross between a high farce and a satirical comedy, Hay Fever follows Judith, a retired actor who is idling away with her family at their country home. Her husband, David, is a reclusive novelist, and her children, Sorrel and Simon, are failing to launch their own aspirations.

When each member of the Bliss family invites an unexpected guest to their home for the weekend, the house quickly erupts into unforgettable chaos. Over the course of three acts, the Bliss family seem to manage to bombard their guests with activities and conversation, who are lukewarm to their advances. Judith is the most ridiculous of them all, making wild exaggerations and exclamations and even performing an overdramatic faint. Will the poor guests be able to escape this family of lunatics with their dignity intact?

Hay Fever is one of Noel Coward’s most beloved plays, which first debuted in the West End in 1925. Subsequent revivals on the stage happened over the years across London, including a run at The Old Vic in the 1960s. The play has also been adapted for television over the years. The most recent production of Hay Fever was directed by Lindsay Posner in 2015 at the Duke of York’s Theatre, where it played after a debut at the Theatre Royal Bath.

Christine Baranski will make her West End debut as Judith Bliss in the West End revival of Hay Fever . She is one of the most honoured actresses in entertainment, with several accolades, including an Emmy and two Tony Awards. She is currently starring as Agnes Van Rhijn in the acclaimed HBO series, The Gilded Age . Other credits include Mamma Mia! , Into the Woods , How the Grinch Stole Christmas and Chicago .

Richard E. Grant will star as David Bliss. The award-winning actor has an incredible fleet of work on stage and screen, including Everybody’s Talking About Jamie , Saltburn and Downton Abbey . His role in this revival of Hay Fever at the Wyndham’s Theatre will mark Richard’s return to the West End stage after 20 years.

Further casting for the play is to be announced.

Emily Burns directs the production. An associate of the Bridge Theatre, and previously of the National Theatre, her theatre credits include Measure for Measure , Dear Octopus and The Comeback .

Catch two of the greatest actors of our time, two-time Tony Award-winning actress Christine Baranski and Academy Award nominee Richard E. Grant, as you’ve never seen them before, in what is set to be one of the most talked about productions in the West End this year. Book your tickets for Hay Fever and experience a blissful combination of wit and chaos at the Wyndham’s Theatre!

shows.title: I Puritani
shows.description:
Experience operatic romance and vocal fireworks as I Puritani makes a grand return to the Royal Opera House, in the heart of Covent Garden. Directed by Richard Jones, this production marks the first time the company has performed I Puritani in over thirty years - don’t miss this rare chance to see Bellini’s emotionally charged masterpiece about the tender bonds of love, the devastation of heartbreak, and the elation of reconciliation. Secure your tickets today.

Set during the English Civil War, I Puritani follows the doomed love between Elvira, the daughter of a Puritan governor, and Arturo, a Royalist supporter. On the eve of their wedding, political allegiances and suspicions intervene, throwing Elvira into a spiral of heartbreak and madness. As the tides of war shift, love and loyalty are tested to their limits in a powerful operatic exploration of obsession, faith, and forgiveness.

With its sweeping score, elaborate choruses, and dramatic flair, I Puritani is a towering example of bel canto opera. Bellini’s final composition is renowned for its vocal intricacy, and this new production transforms the narrative into a psychological portrait, heightening the tension and theatricality. Expect passion, betrayal, and vocal pyrotechnics in a production that brings gothic surrealism to Bellini’s haunting vision.

Bellini’s I Puritani stands as one of the most celebrated works of the bel canto era, balancing lyrical beauty with dramatic depth. Based on Têtes Rondes et Cavaliers , a historical play about Puritans and Cavaliers during the English Civil War, the opera was first staged in 1835 at Paris’s Théâtre‑Italien and quickly became a favourite for its radiant melodies and expressive vocal writing. The score features some of Bellini’s most beloved music, including Elvira’s virtuosic arias and the intense ensemble writing in its final act. Internationally, I Puritani continues to delight audiences with its emotional range - from tender romance to heartrending despair and ultimately to triumph.

Bellini’s final work, the opera remains a testament to his mastery of long, lyrical vocal lines and dramatic pacing, securing its place among the great masterpieces of the 19th‑century Italian repertory. Despite its initial success and stunning musical passages, it has long been underperformed compared to Bellini’s more popular works, such as Norma or La sonnambula . This new Royal Opera House production marks the company’s first staging of the opera in over three decades, and offers a rare opportunity to experience its full splendour.

I Puritani was composed by Vincenzo Bellini ( Norma, La sonnambula, Il pirata ), with a libretto by Carlo Pepoli,

The Royal Opera’s new staging of I Puritani is directed by Richard Jones ( Boris Godunov, The Mastersingers of Nuremberg ), one of the UK’s most celebrated opera directors, known for his bold, stylised interpretations. Riccardo Frizza ( La sonnambula, Norma, Don Pasquale ) conducts, making his Royal Opera debut.

Design is by Hyemi Shin ( The Cunning Little Vixen, The Rape of Lucretia, A Little Night Music ), with costumes by Nicky Gillibrand ( Billy Budd, The Magic Flute, The Light Princess ). Lighting is by Adam Silverman ( Pelléas et Mélisande, Katya Kabanova, Jenůfa ), and movement direction by Sarah Fahie ( The Marriage of Figaro, Der Rosenkavalier, Carmen ).

Casting varies by performance date. Principal cast includes:

Opera fans, rejoice! I Puritani promises a night of exceptional singing, rare repertoire, and theatrical flair. Richard Jones’s vision casts a stark, stylised light on the opera’s themes of madness and political extremism, in a haunting and expressionist staging. This is one of opera’s most exciting offerings of the year. Let Bellini’s romantic drama sweep you away - book tickets for I Puritani at the Royal Opera House today.

shows.title: Jesus Christ Superstar
shows.description:
The five‑star rock‑musical phenomenon Jesus Christ Superstar comes to the London Palladium in the heart of Soho, following critically‑acclaimed runs at the Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre in 2016 and 2017. This “gorgeous, thrilling, heavenly” (Guardian) staging of Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice’s sung-through rock-musical about the last days of Jesus Christ’s life, and his betrayal by Judas Iscariot, comes to the West End for a strictly limited run. Eurovision star Sam Ryder makes his West End debut in the lead role, before transferring the show for Jesus Christ Superstar at Theatre Royal Drury Lane later in the year.

Set in the final days of Jesus’s life, Jesus Christ Superstar follows the growing tension between Jesus of Nazareth and his disciple Judas Iscariot, who fears that Jesus’s message has been distorted and that his growing influence will provoke Roman retaliation. As crowds gather and expectations rise, Jesus struggles with his role as both spiritual leader and political figure. The story, told largely from Judas’s perspective, charts betrayal, sacrifice, and the weight of destiny.

This new staging brings the 2017 open‑air triumph into the West End, featuring all your favourite emotionally charged rock anthems, including “I Don’t Know How to Love Him”, “Gethsemane”, “Heaven on Their Minds”, and the title number “Superstar”.

Jesus Christ Superstar began life as a concept album in 1970, created by composer Andrew Lloyd Webber and lyricist Tim Rice. Its bold fusion of rock music and biblical storytelling quickly captured public imagination, with the album topping charts in several countries. Following its success, the show made its stage debut on Broadway in 1971 and premiered in London’s West End at the Palace Theatre in 1972, where it ran for over eight years.

It has since become one of the world’s most enduring and frequently revived musicals, inspiring numerous international tours, film adaptations and reimaginings - including most recently a concert staging at the Hollywood Bowl starring Cynthia Erivo and Adam Lambert. This 2026 revival revisits the critically acclaimed Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre 2016 production, which received a second staging at the Open Air Theatre in 2017 and received both an indoor staging at the Barbican and a US tour. The magic is brought indoors once again for a West End limited season this summer.

Sam Ryder plays the lead role of Jesus. Sam Ryder is a British singer-songwriter who rose to international fame after representing the United Kingdom at the Eurovision Song Contest 2022, where he finished in second place with the power ballad “Space Man” - the UK’s best result in over two decades. Ryder first gained attention through social media, sharing powerful covers during lockdown, and his debut album, There’s Nothing But Space, Man!, topped the UK Albums Chart in 2022. Known for his signature falsetto and positive energy, Jesus Christ Superstar at the London Palladium marks Ryder’s highly anticipated West End debut. Further casting includes:

Across the run, the role of King Herod will be shared by six performers:

The production reunites the Olivier-winning creative team from the 2016/2017 Regent’s Park Theatre Open Air Theatre production. Olivier winner Tim Sheader ( Hello, Dolly!, To Kill A Mockingbird ) directs, with choreography from Olivier winner and Regents Park Open Air Theatre Artistic Director Drew McOnie ( In the Heights, Carousel ). Tony winner Tom Scutt ( Cabaret, Fiddler on the Roof ) designs.

Musical supervision is by Tom Deering ( Standing at the Sky’s Edge ) with lighting design by Lee Curran ( A Streetcar Named Desire ), sound design by Adam Fisher ( Sunset Boulevard ), and fight direction from Kate Waters ( War Horse ).

There should be just one thing on your mind - grabbing tickets for the summer’s most unmissable theatrical event. Sam Ryder makes his West End debut in this award-winning staging that “really rocks” (Guardian). So don’t miss out, because in the Palladium, you might just feel like a “Superstar” - secure your tickets for Jesus Christ Superstar at the Palladium today.

shows.title: John Proctor is the Villain
shows.description:
Tony-nominated play John Proctor is the Villain transfers to the West End in 2027, following its sell-out debut in London at the Royal Court Theatre in Spring 2026. This bitingly witty coming-of-age dramady turns theatrical classic The Crucible on its head, examining what it means to be a teenage girl in a post #MeToo world, and who gets to decide who is the hero of the stories we tell. John Proctor is the Villain will “engage and electrify” (Guardian). Secure your tickets for the strictly limited run at Wyndham’s Theatre, located close to the electric atmosphere of Leicester Square, today.

In a rural Georgia town in 2018, a high-school honours English class sit down to study Arthur Miller’s The Crucible - but the teens are more preoccupied with sex, gossip, who’s making out with who, and conducting ‘witch hunts’ of their own than with a stuffy old play about the Salem witch trials.

As they try to figure out their place in a post-#MeToo world, a group of girls faces pushback from their conservative school administrators when they try to found a feminist club, and as they delve further into The Crucible, they start to question everything they previously thought about the play. Is its flawed yet celebrated protagonist, John Proctor, truly the hero their teacher purports him to be?

Both a response to and re-examination of The Crucible, John Proctor is the Villain flips the script on an American classic with a fresh new perspective that asks who the hero really is - “after watching it, you will never view ‘The Crucible’ in the same way again.” (Washington Post).

John Proctor is the Villain premiered in Washington DC in 2022. Following a further successful professional staging in Boston, the show made its Broadway debut in 2025, starring Stranger Things star Sadie Sink, and took an unusual path to New York - previously having been licensed for almost 100 non-professional productions, at high schools and colleges beforehand. The show’s Broadway premiere was a smash hit and earned seven Tony nominations. In 2025, a film adaptation, co-produced by Sadie Sink and Tina Fey, was greenlit, with Bellflower adapting her own script.

The production, which made its European premiere at the Royal Court Theatre in Spring 2026, sold out its entire run. The upcoming West End transfer to Wyndham’s Theatre is a result of the high demand and popularity of this show!

Casting for this production is to be announced.

“A fantastically cathartic play” (The Independent), “Absolutely nails the timeless fury of female adolescence” (The Telegraph), “The most validating theatrical experience a young woman can have” (A Young(ish) Perspective): critics adore the power of John Proctor is the Villain and the news of a West End transfer is exactly what this show deserves. If you’re looking for a piece of theatre that packs a punch, this five-star triumph is exactly that.

John Proctor is the Villain is written by American playwright and educator Kimberley Belflower. Bellflower is a Tony nominee and Drama Desk winner. Her other credits include Teen Girl FANtasies, Gondal , and The Sky Game. The 2025 production of John Proctor is the Villain , marking her Broadway debut, and now the play receives its West End premiere.

Tony winner Danya Taymor directs, fresh from a Tony-nominated run directing the show on Broadway. Taymor is an American director, and her credits include The Outsiders the Musical, Daddy, Familiar and Pass Over .

An American classic gets seen in a fresh new light in this feel-good, funny and moving play by one of America’s hottest young playwrights. It’s “absolutely essential” (WhatsOnStage) to book your tickets for John Proctor is the Villain and to get into “this utterly galvanising room” (BroadwayWorld) in 2027!

shows.title: La Boheme

sources.title_as_listed: La bohème - Royal Ballet and Opera

shows.description:
Step into the vibrant streets of 19th‑century Paris with La Boheme at the Royal Opera House, in the centre of Covent Garden. Puccini’s beloved opera captures the spirit of youth, community and passion, following a group of young artists - a poet, painter, musician and philosopher - as they navigate love, poverty and friendship against the backdrop of the Latin Quarter at Christmastime. Secure your tickets today.

La Boheme tells the story of a group of young bohemians living in the Latin Quarter of Paris in the mid‑19th century, chronicling their dreams, struggles and enduring friendships. At its heart is the poet Rodolfo, whose life changes when he meets the delicate seamstress Mimì on a cold Christmas Eve. Their instant connection sparks a tender romance, but poverty and illness soon threaten their happiness.

As well as scenes of laughter and warmth, from shared meals in their garret to playful flirtations at Café Momus, there are also moments of profound sorrow as reality encroaches on the lovers’ hopes. Puccini’s luminous score, featuring some of opera’s most cherished arias such as “Sì, mi chiamano Mimì” and Musetta’s waltz “Quando m’en vo’,” brings emotional depth to every relationship on stage.

Puccini’s La Boheme premiered at Turin’s Teatro Regio in 1896 and quickly became one of the most performed operas worldwide. Its intimate portrayal of love, youth and loss - drawn from Henri Murger’s Scènes de la vie de bohème - has made it a staple of the operatic repertoire. La Boheme has been a beloved favourite at the Royal Opera House for generations, and the most performed opera at the venue. Jones’ acclaimed staging was first performed for the Royal Opera House in 2017, and at the time of its premiere was the first new production of La Boheme for the theatre in four decades.

The opera’s blend of humour, lyricism and heartbreak has inspired countless productions and recordings, and its principal arias remain central to the lyric tenor and soprano repertories. The show has also inspired several adaptations, most famously Jonathan Larson’s hit musical Rent , which transplants the action to New York in the early 90s.

The cast of this production varies depending on the performance date. Principal cast includes:

La Boheme is composed by Giacomo Puccini ( Tosca, Madama Butterfly ) with a libretto by Giuseppe Giacosa and Luigi Illica ( Tosca ). The production is directed by Richard Jones (Handel’s Giulio Cesare, Peter Grimes ), with design by Stewart Laing ( Dead Man Walking ), lighting by Mimi Jordan Sherin ( Boris Godunov ), and movement direction by Sarah Fahie ( Der Rosenkavalier ). Conducting duties are shared by Christopher Willis ( Le nozze di Figaro ) and Lorenzo Passerini ( Faust ), making his Opera House debut.

Become a Bohemian this summer and join in the joys and sorrows that unfold through soaring duets, intimate arias and evocative choral scenes. Whether you’re a Rent fan exploring opera for the first time or an opera aficionado returning to a favourite, Richard Jones’ acclaimed staging offers a richly emotional experience with world‑class singing, evocative staging and Puccini’s unforgettable score. Book your tickets for La Boheme at the Royal Opera House today!

shows.title: La Fille du regiment

sources.title_as_listed: La Fille Du Regiment - Royal Ballet and Opera

shows.description:
Atteeention! March on down to the Royal Opera House, in the heart of Covent Garden, for La fille du regiment this summer. Gaetano Donizetti’s Bel canto comic opera, about a precocious girl raised by a troop of soldiers, is packed with vivacity and vocal fireworks and comes to life in Laurent Pelly’s humorous new staging, starring Juan Diego Flórez, Jonah Hoskins, and Sara Blanch, making her Royal Opera House debut. You won't want to miss it - secure your tickets today.

Set during the Napoleonic Wars in the Tyrol, the opera tells the story of Marie, a vivandière (aka canteen girl) adopted and raised by the 21st Regiment of French soldiers after being found as an infant on the battlefield. When Tonio, a young Tyrolean peasant, declares his love for Marie and joins the regiment to be with her, the path to their happiness seems clear. However, when the aristocratic Marquise de Berkenfield appears and lays claim to Marie, a long‑buried secret about her origins comes to light, threatening their plans and leading to lively comedy, heartfelt moments and, ultimately, a celebration of love and community.

La fille du regiment (which translates as The Daughter of the Regiment ) is an opéra comique in two acts by Gaetano Donizetti to a French libretto by Jules‑Henri Vernoy de Saint‑Georges and Jean‑François Bayard. Donizetti composed La fille du regiment while living in Paris in the late 1830s, and it was his first opera written directly in French. Since its premiere at the Opéra‑Comique on 11 February 1840, the work has become a beloved staple of the operatic repertoire, admired for its blend of lively ensemble numbers, bright orchestration and comic dialogue.

One of the opera’s most famous moments is Tonio’s aria “Ah! mes amis, quel jour de fête!”, renowned for its taxing series of eight (often nine) high Cs, a highlight for tenors and a crowd‑pleasing showstopper. Laurent Pelly’s engaging staging - a co‑production with the Vienna State Opera and the Metropolitan Opera, New York - evokes the military camp and aristocratic tensions with imaginative design and humour, making this production a lively experience for both seasoned opera lovers and newcomers alike.

Casting varies by performance date. Principal cast includes:

The spoken role of the Duchesse de Crakentorp is often a surprise highlight of La fille du régiment . In past Royal Opera House revivals, the part has been played by stars including Dawn French, Ann Widdecombe, Miranda Richardson, and Kiri Te Kanawa. Casting for the role in this production is award-winning actor Tamsein Greig.

La fille du regiment is directed by Laurent Pelly ( Lakmé, Don Pasquale, Cendrillon ), who also designed the costumes for the show. Giuseppe Finzi ( La bohème, L’elisir d’amore, Rigoletto ) conducts.

Dialogue is prepared by Agathe Mélinand (L’Impresario de Smyrne, Gypsy ), set design is by Chantal Thomas ( La Bohème, Manon ), lighting by Joël Adam ( Wozzeck, The Magic Flute ), and choreography is by Laura Scozzi ( Orpheus in the Underworld, La Dolce Vita ).

The music is by Gaetano Donizetti ( L’elisir d’amore, Lucia di Lammermoor, Don Pasquale ), with a French libretto by Jules‑Henri Vernoy de Saint‑Georges and Jean‑François Bayard.

Ready for high spirits and even higher Cs? La fille du regiment is a feel‑good operatic comedy full of charm, catchy melodies and thrilling vocal feats. From its touching heroine to its exuberant choruses and spirited duets, this production is an ideal night out for dedicated opera fans and newbies alike. Book your tickets for La fille du regiment at the Royal Opera House now and enjoy a summer of laughs, love and bel canto brilliance

shows.title: La Fille mal gardee

sources.title_as_listed: La Fille mal gardée - Royal Ballet and Opera

shows.description:
Take a trip to the countryside with La fille mal gardee at the Royal Opera House, in the heart of Covent Garden. Frederick Ashton’s beloved ballet, complete with mischievous antics, maypole dances and a cheerful score, is ideal for both families and long‑time ballet lovers and returns to London for a strictly limited run this spring.

Set in a rural village, the story follows Lise, the spirited daughter of Widow Simone, who is in love with the young farmer Colas. Simone, however, has other plans and hopes to marry Lise to the foolish Alain, son of a prosperous landowner. Through secret meetings and clever schemes, Lise and Colas work to outwit Simone’s plans and secure their own happy ending. A rural tale of love and family meddling, the ballet combines classical technique with bucolic humour, incorporating folk‑dance elements such as maypole and clog dances alongside vivacious ensemble work.

La fille mal gardee (French for The Wayward Daughter ) is a ballet in two acts choreographed by Sir Frederick Ashton for The Royal Ballet and first staged at the Royal Opera House in 1960. Ashton’s version revived the 18th‑century pastoral comedy originally created by Jean Dauberval and inspired by a 1765 painting by Pierre-Antoine Baudouin. Ashton’s version has since become a signature comedy in the Royal Ballet’s repertory.

The score, rooted in Ferdinand Hérold’s original 1828 music and fashioned into a new orchestral tapestry by Lanchbery, supports Ashton’s light‑hearted choreography, balancing lyrical tenderness with sprightly antics. Highlights often include the pas de ruban, Widow Simone’s clog dance and the maypole sequence, which together reflect the ballet’s pastoral charm. This production’s colourful design and inventive choreography have made La fille mal gardee a favourite not just in London but with ballet companies worldwide, celebrated for its blend of wit, grace and narrative clarity.

Casting varies by performance date, but principal dancers set to appear include:

La fille mal gardee is choreographed by Sir Frederick Ashton ( The Dream, Cinderella, Symphonic Variations ), with music by Ferdinand Hérold, arranged and orchestrated by John Lanchbery ( The Tales of Beatrix Potter, Coppélia ). The scenario is based on the original ballet by Jean Dauberval ( Psyché et l'Amour ).

Design is by Osbert Lancaster ( Coppélia, Pineapple Poll ), and lighting is by John B. Read ( Song of the Earth, Manon ).

Sir Frederick Ashton’s feel‑good ballet pairs humour with classical virtuosity as this acclaimed production returns to its Covent Garden home. With its memorable choreography, delightful costumes and engaging story, La fille mal gardee is an ideal introduction to ballet or a rewarding return for seasoned fans. Book your tickets for La fille mal gardee at the Royal Opera House today for a summer of sunshine, wit and romance.

shows.title: Malory Towers
shows.description:
Embark on a journey to Alexandra Palace in London, where the magnificent Grade II listed building between Wood Green and Muswell Hill will transform into the sun-soaked cliffs of Cornwall for a glorious musical adaptation of Malory Towers . Book your tickets for your dose of nostalgia and inspire the next generation of Enid Blyton lovers along the way this summer.

As one of the most beloved children’s book series, Malory Towers charts the journey of Darrell Rivers as she leaves home and enrolls at a girls’ boarding school. Largely centred on the friendship between Darrell and Gwendoline, Malory Towers is a wonderful story about personal growth, loyalty, and community.

Malory Towers was published as a book series between 1946 and 1951, with six more additions added by Pamela Cox in 2009. A TV series based on the series was first broadcast on CBBC in 2020, running for seven years until its final episode aired in October 2025.

The stage musical was first presented at The Passenger Shed in Bristol, where it debuted in 2019, before performing in Cambridge, York, Exeter, Manchester and Oxford. This production at the Alexandra Palace is part of the latest UK tour, which was postponed in 2020.

Malory Towers has been adapted and directed by Emma Rice. This musical is co-produced with David Pugh and Dafydd Rogers.

Emma is known for her fearless work and was the Artistic Director of Shakespeare’s Globe from 2016 to 2018 before launching her touring theatre company, Wise Children. Her infamous adaptations include Brief Encounter, The Red Shoes and Pandora’s Box .

The rest of the creative team includes set and costume by Lez Brotherston, music by Ian Ross, sound and video by Simon Baker, lighting by Malcolm Rippeth and movement and choreography by Alistair David.

Malory Towers is a musical for girls, boys and all grown-up children who still dream of midnight feasts and want to capture the series of raucous stories once more on the stage. Book your tickets to see this sparky and brilliant stage adaptation at the Alexandra Palace for a limited time this summer.

shows.title: Mermaids & Pirates
shows.description:
Get ready to set sail on a sun-soaked Caribbean adventure with joyous kids show Mermaids and Pirates . Coming to the St Martin’s Theatre, the home of The Mousetrap in the heart of Seven Dials, for a strictly limited run this summer, this feel-good family musical is full of Caribbean tunes, larger-than-life characters, and plenty of chuckles, as a rag-tag group of mermaids and pirates must work together to save the day.

When a bumbling band of pirates, led by their captain Long Gone Silver, discover Treasure Island while sailing the high seas, they’re expecting to find gold and jewels - what they find instead, are Marina and her flipping-cool girl gang of mermaids. When the Sacred Coconut mysteriously disappears from the island, chaos ensues, and the Pirates and Mermaids must band together, along with singing parrot Rita Conchita, to try and save the day.

With a cast of unforgettable characters - including Isla, the queen of the Island, seasick pirate Jack and the super-shy mermaid Myrtle - mermaids and pirates fuses salsa-style choreography with calypso-infused songs and plenty of laughs. This hilarious show celebrates the magic of the Caribbean and uplifts the importance of bravery and working together, and is perfect for the whole family.

Mermaids and Pirates is created by Perform Productions. Perform Productions create feel-good and fun shows for children, as well as running drama classes for children aged 4-12, which focus on building children’s confidence and self-esteem. Perform Productions was founded by Will Barnett and Lucy Quick. Their previous shows include Magical Merlin in the West End, Jungle Rumble, Midnight in the Toyshop, and The Dream.

There’s plenty of mischief, magic and melodies in this uplifting children's show, best for ages 3+. Join the adventure and sail the high seas with Mermaids and Pirates . Will this mismatched band of adventurers recover the Sacred Coconut and save the island? There’s only one way to find out - book tickets for Mermaids and Pirates at the St Martin's Theatre today!

shows.title: Mrs Dalloway
shows.description:
Experience Virginia Woolf like never before in this moving, witty, and dazzingly theatrical adaptation of a modern masterpiece. Mrs Dalloway is adapted and directed by award-winning director
Jen Heyes
, co-created with and starring
Olivier Award
-winning artist
Kit Green
(Tina C, Ida Barr), who also transforms into all 16 roles – including that of Woolf herself.
A single day, unfolding both in June 1923 – and in this very moment. Clarissa Dalloway travels across London preparing for her party, while war veteran Septimus Smith struggles with the horrors of his own experience. Their stories unfold side by side; blurring past and present, memory and identity. Fusing drama, live music, film and technical artistry into a fully immersive experience of modern cine-theatre,
Mrs Dalloway
invites you into Woolf’s world to ask –what makes us who we are?
A co-production of Storyhouse, Harlow Playhouse, and CutToTheChase Productions.

shows.title: Nine Night
shows.description:
Some secrets don’t make it to the grave
When Gloria passes, her family gathers for the traditional Jamaican
Nine Night
. And that means the whole family.
As more and more mourners gather bringing rum and curry and complaints, tensions build, and the family must face some uncomfortable truths.
‘A spirit never wan fi leave de family home’; and there’s still 8 days left…
Amit Sharma
(Retrograde, Please Please Me) directs this brand new production of
Natasha Gordon
‘s critically acclaimed debut play celebrating the humour and hardships of grief.

Join Peter and Wendy on an awfully big adventure in a quest to never grow up. Joined by the mischievous Lost Boys and feisty fairy Tink, can they work together to defeat the formidable Captain James Hook, who’s determined to take Peter’s sword and rule over Neverland once and for all?

shows.title: Prehistoric Planet: Discovering Dinosaurs
shows.description:
PREHISTORIC PLANET: DISCOVERING DINOSAURS at Lightroom is a celebration of our natural world through captivating storytelling, breathtaking visuals and groundbreaking technology, in collaboration with Apple TV+.

Lightroom’s state-of-the-art 360 projections allow viewers to see these majestic creatures at an awe-inspiring scale and travel alongside them through dangerous deserts, soaring skies and the deep sea.

As escapist as it is educational, the show will also include never seen before material, including exclusive extended CGI scenes and bespoke illustrations.

PREHISTORIC PLANET: DISCOVERING DINOSAURS will be directed and designed by 59 Studio in close collaboration with the makers of Prehistoric Planet, Apple TV+, and Executive Producer and BBC Studios Natural History Unit Creative Director Mike Gunton. Book your PREHISTORIC PLANET: DISCOVERING DINOSAURS tickets with LOVEtheatre today!

Evoking a feeling of wonder, you will be guided on a once in a lifetime adventure, exploring the fascinating role dinosaurs have played in shaping our world from 66 million years ago until now.

Through this epic journey, viewers will step inside some of the most beloved scenes from seasons one and two of Apple TV+’s Emmy Award-nominated series Prehistoric Planet, and encounter a vast array of dinosaurs (from Ammonites to Mosasaurs, Adaltheriums to the Tyrannosaurus rex) at the most pivotal moments of their lives.

shows.title: So Are We: León & Lightfoot

sources.title_as_listed: So We Are: León & Lightfoot - Royal Ballet and Opera

shows.description:
The Royal Ballet Company presents an exciting double-bill of contemporary work this year, as Sol León and Paul Lightfoot’s So Are We opens at the Royal Opera House near Covent Garden. Comprising two individual shows - Shoot the Moon and Salle de Dance - brought together for one exhilarating performance, this is a stirring, passionate mix of old and new from the acclaimed choreographer team, and marks the first time a British company has performed the duo’s work.

So Are We is a mixed programme that matches Leon & Lightfoot’s classic work Shoot the Moon with newly staged piece Salle de Dance .

Shoot the Moon celebrates its 20th anniversary this year, following its world premiere in the Netherlands in 2006. This intimate piece reflects on themes of solitude within relationships, as three couples teeter on the edge of intimacy and separation. With its expressive, fluid movement and yearning music, this is a contemporary classic that stands the test of time. It is scored by Academy Award-winning American composer Philip Glass ( The Hours, The Truman Show ) and his melodic Tirol Concerto.

Salle de Dance is a new world premiere stage performance, adapted from the filmed version by Leon & Lightfoot. The original version was created during lockdown as a celebration of the balletic art form, and it now leaps onto the stages that inspired it. Inspired by a dancer’s daily study of ballet classes, it is performed on a bare stage, with the power of dance right at the fore. It is set to a new score by award-winning composer Ilya Demutsky ( A Hero of Our Time ).

Sol León and Paul Lightfoot are a ground-breaking choreography duo who have worked extensively together on some of the best 20th and 21st century dance performances. Since 1959, they have created a huge number of works, including more than 50 for Nederlands Dans Theater, of which they were in-house choreographers between 2002 and 2020.

Best known for their expressive, abstract and often minimalist style and strong sense of collaboration, their work includes Skew Whiff, Subject to Change and Schubert .

This daring two-part show is a fantastic introduction to one of Europe’s most visionary dance creative teams, brought together in London for a unique evening of entertainment. Don’t miss out on seeing Leon & Lightfoot’s boundary-pushing work at the Royal Opera House, with tickets for So Are We available now.

shows.title: Table 17
shows.description:
Two exes. One dinner. What could go wrong?
Would you go to dinner with your ex? The one you were engaged to, but haven’t spoken to in years? You’re over them – right?!
Jada and Dallas are hashing things out in this sharp, hilarious new comedy. Can they leave 7 years of baggage at the door to give their love a second chance? Is the spark even still there? Or will the weight of their past pull them apart before the night ends?
Following sold out runs in New York and LA,
Douglas Lyons
‘ (Chicken & Biscuits) award-winning play, directed by
Zhailon Levingston
(CATS The Jellicle Ball), makes its UK premiere at Kiln. Featuring
Marisha Wallace
as Jada and
Michael Rishawn
as River/Eric, with further casting to be announced, get ready to give love a second chance this autumn.

shows.title: Tango After Dark
shows.description:
Escape to the city of Buenos Aires for the ultimate evening of romance and drama with Tango After Dark . Inspired by Argentina’s rich cultural tradition, German Cornejo presents a “Splendid, sensual, imposing extravagance of Argentine tango at its very best” (Dance Tabs) performed by world-class dancers from across the world. Travel to the Sadler's Wells Theatre, a short walk from the heart of Islington, for a “mesmerising spectacle” (The Mail on Sunday), which plays for a strictly limited run.

The theatrical experience draws inspiration from Astor Piazzolla, a popular Argentine tango composer who revolutionised the dance in the 1960s and 70s by incorporating elements of jazz and classical music. Tango After Dark takes this strong influence and immerses audiences into the heart of Buenos Aires. It is performed by ten of the world’s finest dancers alongside a live orchestra of five musicians and two singers.

Tango After Dark made its world premiere in London at the Peacock Theatre back in 2018, where it sold out its run. It returned to the same venue a few years later in 2022. This electric dance show has gone on to play across the globe and been praised by well-known celebrities like Simon Cowell, Jennifer Lopez and Heidi Klum. Recently, the show has been playing to packed out venues in Canada and the US on a tour this year.

The cast of Tango After Dark is led by World Tango Champions German Cornejo and Gisela Galeassi. An astonishingly athletic and powerful performer, Cornejo has also choreographed many other shows, including Immortal Tango and Tango Fire . They are joined by a group of 8 world-class tango dancers.

If you want to experience authentic Argentine tango thrust into the modern world, book Tango After Dark tickets for a “scorching display of smouldering tango, impressive acrobatics and thrilling set pieces” (Dancing Times). Let the power of dance warm up the colder evenings for you this November.

shows.title: Tender
shows.description:
The dazzling and moving play by Eleanor Tindall (Before I Was A Bear, Soho Theatre) is directed by Emily Aboud (Lady Dealer, Bush Theatre).

“My daydreams are just her now. She is in every corner of my brain, waiting.”

Ivy has life sorted; she’s got a flat, a boyfriend and she knows exactly where it’s all headed. Except there is this thing that she tries not to think about. The thing she left in her childhood bedroom.

Ash should be having the time of her life. But, fresh out of a bad relationship, she’s full of things she can’t leave behind. And there's something off about her new flat. The wallpaper pulses and sometimes it sounds like a heartbeat.

Two women. A chance encounter that tumbles into infatuation. And an undeniable force waiting just out of sight, ready to wreck it all.

By turns thrilling and surreal, Tender promises to subvert your expectations of queer love stories. Playing for a strictly limited run, this upscaled production reunites the original creative team behind the 2024 sold-out Studio hit.

shows.title: The Afronauts
shows.description:
The Afronauts rockets into London for its world premiere. This unmissable new play about resistance, imagination, and reaching for the stars from Olivier-nominated playwright Ryan Calais Cameron reimagines a little-known chapter of African history. Don't miss this sharply witty, politically charged play, coming to the Royal Court Theatre, in vibrant Sloane Square, for a strictly limited run in winter 2026, commissioned especially as part of the theatre’s 70th anniversary season.

1964: As the USA and USSR battle it out to reach the moon, another contender enters the space race - Zambia. In a country that has just gained its independence, one schoolteacher gathers a band of eccentric students and launches them into a dream that defies gravity.

With limited resources and limitless ambition, he gathers a group of ambitious misfits for the ultimate mission. What follows is part sci-fi fable, part political satire, part celebration of a nation reaching beyond the colonial legacy.

The Afronauts is inspired by the true(ish) story of Zambia’s 1964 space programme, reimagined by award winning playwright Ryan Calais Cameron. This world premiere is supported by the Genesis Foundation and is the first commission from their new Royal Court programme, designed to support bold, original work.

Casting for The Afronauts is to be announced in five, four, three, two…

The Afronauts is written by Ryan Calais Cameron. Calais Cameron is a Black British Theatre and Sky Arts Theatre Award winner and Olivier nominee. His credits include For Black Boys Who Have Considered Suicide When the Hue Gets Too Heavy, Queens of Sheba, Human Nurture, and Retrograde as well as Boarders for the BBC and Queenie for Channel 4.

Further creative team members are to be announced.

If you’re looking for theatre that rockets beyond the ordinary, The Afronauts offers a story of dreaming big when history told you to stay small. Don't miss the premiere of this bold new work from one of the UK’s most exciting young playwrights. Ambition becomes resistance, and the cosmos becomes a battleground for identity, legacy, and freedom - it promises to be out of this world. Book tickets for The Afronauts at the Royal Court Theatre today.

shows.title: The Children
shows.description:
National treasure Meera Syal leads the cast of The Children , coming to the Lyric Hammersmith near St Paul’s Green. Lucy Kirkwood’s Tony-nominated play about a married couple living in the aftermath of a nuclear disaster, whose life is upended by a figure from their past, celebrates it’s 10th anniversary in this major new revival. Darkly funny and deeply gripping, this “ingenious” (Guardian) drama “asks profound questions” (Guardian) about legacy, the decision to have children and environmental disaster. Secure your tickets today.

In the aftermath of a nuclear disaster, married couple Hazel and Robin are trying to cling to normality, despite living on the edge of a radiation exclusion zone. Hazel has her yoga and stays in contact with their eldest child, Robin farms and brews parsnip wine - so what if electricity is rationed and a geiger counter is on hand at all times?

When their old friend and former colleague, Rose, a nuclear physicist, knocks on their door, their attempt at normality soon crumbles. Rose brings with her buried secrets and a startling proposition that will test the couple’s loyalty and cause them to reassess what they owe to the next generation.

The Children premiered at the Royal Court in 2016 before transferring to Broadway in 2017, receiving two Tony nominations. It has since toured internationally and been revived in the UK. In 2019, The Guardian ranked The Children third on a list of the greatest theatrical works created post-2000. The show returns to London this September in celebration of its 10th anniversary.

Dame Meera Syal stars as Hazel. Syal is an Olivier-nominated comedian, playwright, novelist, journalist and actress, best known for her roles in The Kumars at No. 42 , Goodness Gracious Me and Anita and Me . She holds a CBE, a DBE, a BAFTA Fellowship, and is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature. Her stage credits include Shirley Valentine, Behind the Beautiful Forevers, Annie, Noises Off , and Much Ado About Nothing .

Further casting is to be announced.

The Children is by Lucy Kirkwood. Kirkwood is a playwright and screenwriter, best known for her plays Chimerica, Mosquitoes, NSFW and The Welkin . She is a Tony nominee and an Olivier, Critics’ Circle Theatre Award and Evening Standard Theatre Award winner.

Lyric Artistic Director Rachel O’Riordan directs. O’Riordan's credits include The Weir, Iphigenia in Splott, A Doll's House, Everything is Illuminated and Killology. In 2017, O’Riordan was named one of The Stage newspaper’s 100 most influential people in theatre in the UK.

This award-winning play is more prescient than ever. Starring Meera Syal, this bitingly witty “genuinely disturbing” (Guardian) drama dissects issues of generational responsibility, personal accountability and environmental crisis. Lucy Kirkwood's “taut tale of human and atomic meltdown” (Guardian) is unmissable - secure your tickets for The Children at the Lyric Hammersmith today.

shows.title: The Elvis Years
shows.description:
The hugely popular production of THE ELVIS YEARS has toured nationally and internationally ever since, and is delighted to be back in town at London’s Dominion Theatre to celebrate a huge milestone in the ongoing story of THE ELVIS YEARS.

Undoubtedly the UK’s premier Elvis theatre event, this stunning production takes the audience on a fantastic journey through all the years the King ruled the airwaves. With a full cast of West End talent, a spectacular set, breathtaking lights and awesome video content, Mario and the cast deliver over 50 golden greats, charting the rise and rise of the boy from Tupelo – from the early hits ‘That’s Alright Mama’, ‘Don’t Be Cruel’ and ‘I Got Stung’ all the way through to the iconic Las Vegas concerts with ‘In The Ghetto’, ‘The Wonder Of You’ and of course ‘Suspicious Minds’.

With more than 12 costume changes, Mario Kombou brings the essence of Elvis to every song from every era – The Ed Sullivan Show featuring ‘A Fool Such As I’, The Frank Sinatra TV special including ‘It’s Now Or Never’, the Hollywood years with ‘Return To Sender’ and ‘Viva Las Vegas’, and the legendary ’68 comeback special concluding with ‘If I Can Dream’.

In the words of Elvis’s first cousin Donna Presley – ‘The Best Elvis Since Elvis’

Book your THE ELVIS YEARS theatre tickets with LOVEtheatre today.

What is The Elvis Years about?

It was almost 20 years ago today that the smash-hit musical JAILHOUSE ROCK, starring Mario Kombou, opened in the heart of London’s dazzling West End. There was a magic on stage during the run of the show, and Mario, along with some of the cast, didn’t want the magic to end. So, along with the show’s musical director David Mackay, we set about combining forces and creating a new show – THE ELVIS YEARS – which would encompass the entire creative life of Elvis Presley

shows.title: The Jungle Book
shows.description:
A new production of The Jungle Book is coming to the iconic National Theatre this autumn, located on the South Bank of the River Thames. Adapted by Indian playwright Anupama Chandrasekhar, the beloved tale is reimagined through innovative puppetry and stunning visuals – secure your tickets today.
